title: update_memory can silently make a rule private, bypassing set_visibility's rejection
description:
PR #290 introduces the rule kind's core invariant: a rule's Visibility must always be "shared" (enforced explicitly in setVisibility, internal/server/tools.go:888-890: `if rec.Category == "rule" { return fmt.Errorf("rules are always shared — delete the rule instead of changing its visibility") }`). This is stated as binding design intent in the same PR's CLAUDE.md addition: "set_visibility is rejected for rules — delete the rule instead."

However update_memory (internal/server/tools.go:768-820) has a second, independent path to the same mutation and it is NOT guarded. updateArgs.Shared (*bool, tools.go:378) is passed straight through: `return d.st.Update(ctx, cur, a.Content, a.Shared, a.Tags, sumArg, vec)` (tools.go:819). Store.Update (internal/store/store.go:1241-1276) applies it unconditionally: `if shared != nil { if *shared { cur.Visibility = visibilityShared } else { cur.Visibility = "" } }` — no category check.

The PR's own updateMemory rule guard (tools.go:789-796) only validates a.Summary when cur.Category=="rule"; it does not check a.Shared. So any owner of a rule can call update_memory(id=<rule-id>, content=<unchanged>, shared=false) and flip the rule to private, defeating the very invariant setVisibility exists to protect — and silently breaking the feature's whole point (rules are meant to be visible to every authenticated actor via list_rules / the session-start hook).

This is reachable with no exotic setup: it's the same tool every other memory update goes through. rules_test.go's TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard (added in this PR) only exercises the Summary field (newline/oversize/clear cases) — there is no test covering Shared, so the gap ships untested.

Fix: add the same category=="rule" guard against a.Shared in updateMemory (mirroring setVisibility's check), e.g. reject any update_memory call with Shared != nil when cur.Category == "rule", or silently ignore/force it — whichever matches the intended contract — and add a regression test alongside TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard.
close_reason: Fixed: update_memory rule guard now rejects a.Shared==false for rules (mirrors set_visibility). Test TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuardRejectsUnshare. Commit lzyn.

title: search_memory: phrasing-sensitive ranking misses highly-relevant record while sticky topical neighbors dominate
description:
Source: GH issue #261 (https://github.com/seanb4t/engram/issues/261), reported by seanb4t 2026-07-01.

PROBLEM: search_memory (semantic/vector recall over Qdrant) fails to surface a highly-relevant record for queries that are near-verbatim restatements of that record's own content, returning less-relevant 'sticky' topical neighbors instead. A differently-phrased query for the SAME fact ranks the missing record #1. Surprising for a vector engine; caused a real curation miss (near-duplicate almost re-stored because search-before-store could not find the existing record). This erodes the zero-junk store guarantee — hence P0.

TARGET RECORD (exists, scope repo:github.com/fzymgc-house/selfhosted-cluster): id 03e33657-6d1f-4e57-867b-c7b26a264d22 (gotcha) — pod resolv.conf appends fzymgc.house search domain -> NODATA poisons search; musl getaddrinfo short-circuits on NODATA (ENOTFOUND) while glibc/c-ares tolerate; fix ndots:1 dnsConfig.

REPRO (same scope, all three):
- Query A (k=4, MISS): 'musl getaddrinfo fzymgc.house search domain NODATA short-circuit ndots dnsConfig HyperDX Pushover webhook' -> returns cacc40c4,10c120e0,d6444e83,d87deac9,4e477ae1; target ABSENT.
- Query B (k=5, MISS): 'HyperDX alert webhook delivery ENOTFOUND musl Alpine dns.lookup getaddrinfo vs c-ares, fzymgc.house appended search domain, fix ndots:1 dnsConfig interim manual kubectl patch' -> same set; target ABSENT despite near-verbatim phrases.
- Query C (k=8, HIT #1): 'ndots dnsConfig cs-clickstack-app pod resolv.conf search domain musl Alpine getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND c-ares' -> target #1. Difference: leads with 'pod resolv.conf' matching the record's opening sentence.

REPORTER HYPOTHESES: (1) extreme phrasing sensitivity / lead-token over-weighting; (2) sticky neighbors dominate topical cluster (A/B identical top set, all alerting records); (3) tag overlap not helping recall; (4) small k amplifies (miss at k=4/5, hit at k=8 different query).

ASKS FROM REPORTER: expected given current embedding model/ranking? would hybrid dense+lexical(BM25) fusion or higher default k + re-rank help sticky-neighbor crowding? could search_memory optionally return scores so callers see near-miss distance?

ENV: engram MCP tools; curating-memory skill v0.8.2. Record ids non-sensitive.

STATUS: triage in progress — do NOT propose fixes before root-cause investigation (systematic-debugging Phase 1).
notes:
TRIAGE (systematic-debugging Ph1-2, production-grounded via k8s + ClickHouse OTEL). Bug is REAL + CURRENT — reproduced live against scope repo:github.com/fzymgc-house/selfhosted-cluster:
- Query A k=4: target 03e33657 ABSENT. Query A k=20: target at RANK 6. Query C k=8: target RANK 1. => same record swings #1<->~#6 on semantically-equivalent queries = phrasing sensitivity confirmed. The 'miss' is small-k truncation of a rank~6 record, not non-retrieval.

PROD FACTS (ns agent-memory, deploy/memory-mcp, image ghcr.io/seanb4t/engram:0.8.1):
- EMBED MODEL = qwen3-embedding-8b @ 4096 dims (ENGRAM_OPENAI_BASE_URL=llm-gw.fzymgc.house/engram). NOT bge-m3 (chart default). Confirmed in OTEL: 727 embed.Embed spans model=qwen3-embedding-8b dims=4096 (+24 with empty dims = likely embed failures, minor separate observation).
- embed.Embed avg ~3.75s (8B model heavy); tool/search_memory avg ~3.8s (embed-dominated).
- k distribution (store.Search, 14d): k=5 modal (111, 109/111 SATURATED), k=8 (59), k=4 (48, 48/48 SATURATED), k=6/3/... ALL near-fully saturated (result_count==k). => searches near-universally return exactly k => Qdrant routinely has MORE readable candidates than k => rank>k records chronically truncated. Small-k is the NORM not an edge case.

CODE FACTS (current main):
- embed.go Embed(ctx,text) POSTs {model,input:text} IDENTICALLY for store (a.Content, tools.go:480/508/531) and search (a.Query, tools.go:653/694). ZERO query/passage asymmetry, ZERO Qwen3 'Instruct:'/'Query:' formatting anywhere in internal/ (grep clean).
- store.Search (store.go:503): single qdrant.NewQuery(vec...) Cosine top-k, Limit=k. NO over-fetch, NO rerank, NO hybrid/sparse fusion. memoriesFromPoints DROPS p.Score (scores never surfaced).
- Only a.Content is embedded — tags + summary contribute NOTHING to the vector (tags are hard AND pre-filter only). Explains reporter obs#3 (tag overlap doesn't aid recall).
- default k=8 (tools.go:638) only when unset; reporter/most callers pass k=4/5.

ROOT-CAUSE RANKING (contributing factors, not yet fixes):
B* (PRIMARY, model-specific) Qwen3-Embedding-8B is instruction-tuned + ASYMMETRIC (query gets an Instruct: prefix, doc raw); engram applies neither -> degraded + phrasing-sensitive retrieval. This is a real misconfig vs the model's intended usage.
A (proximate) near-universal k-saturation + no over-fetch => just-below-cutoff records (rank~6) dropped at common k=4/5.
C content-only embedding ignores tags/summary signal.
D pure dense top-k, no rerank/hybrid => sticky topical neighbors crowd small-k window.
E scores never returned => callers can't see near-miss distance (reporter ask #3).

NEXT (Ph3, needs approval before any change): (1) empirically test Qwen3 query-instruction formatting (query-side Instruct prefix) as the highest-leverage lever; (2) consider over-fetch+rerank or higher default k; (3) surface Qdrant score additively. Do NOT ship before A/B benchmark on the real corpus.
close_reason: Fixed and merged via PR #262 (commit 08a0b979): asymmetric query instruction (ENGRAM_EMBED_QUERY_INSTRUCTION), tags folded into document vector + reindex, Qdrant score surfaced, per-model guide (docs-site/guides/embedding-instructions). Follow-up engram-wd89.1 tracks cloud API-param passthrough + E5/nomic doc-side prefix.

title: search_memory/list_memory default response shape changed to recallView, dropping content and 8+ fields
description:
File: internal/server/summary.go (shapeRecall / toRecallView), internal/server/tools.go (listMemory / searchMemory)

Before this PR, search_memory and list_memory returned []store.Memory — full records including content, repo, workspace, worktree, base_dir, source, actor, owner, visibility. After this PR they return []any that resolves to recallView when full=false (the new default). recallView omits: content, repo, workspace, worktree, base_dir, source, actor, owner, visibility — 9 fields that were part of the stable memory contract documented in CLAUDE.md and memory-record.md.

Existing agent consumers that read content or any of the 9 absent fields from search_memory / list_memory results will silently receive the zero value (empty string or nil). This is not a new-field omission (additive change); it is a response-type change: the JSON shape returned is a different struct.

The full=true opt-in does restore the old shape, but callers must update their code and re-deploy before they see correct results. Until then they fail silently (no error, wrong data).

The minor-semver policy noted in the prompt does not cover removing fields from an existing response type — that is a major contract change under standard semver. The design choice is sound for new consumers but the transition is silent for old ones.

Suggested fix options:
1. Version-gate: ship behind a v2 Connect/MCP endpoint and keep v1 returning full content by default, OR
2. Accept this is a major-version bump and cut a semver major release, OR
3. Keep full=false as the default but change the compact response to embed content rather than drop it (use the same Memory shape with a summary field added, content preserved). This is additive and backward-compatible.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-mwq0 — ADR-engram-ambu-sanctioned summary-by-default behavior; release-comms follow-up, not a code defect

title: ADR engram-e38 violated: shadcn-svelte and bits-ui absent from implementation
description:
ADR engram-e38 mandates 'shadcn-svelte (copied-in, owned) on bits-ui headless primitives + Tailwind v4' as the component layer. The spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-10-engram-operator-console-spa-design.md, §Components and views) and plan (plan §Tech Stack) both list shadcn-svelte and bits-ui as required dependencies.

The implementation contains neither shadcn-svelte nor bits-ui anywhere in the codebase. ui/package.json has no bits-ui or shadcn-svelte entries. All components (AppShell.svelte, ScopeRail.svelte, MemoryList.svelte, MemoryDetail.svelte, SearchPalette.svelte) use plain HTML elements with inline CSS-variable style strings.

This is a direct contradiction of ADR engram-e38. If the decision was made to use a lighter inline-styled approach instead, a superseding or amended ADR is required (the spec states 'If the change contradicts an ADR, is a new ADR proposed?'). No such ADR appears in this PR.

Affected files: ui/package.json (no bits-ui/shadcn-svelte deps), ui/src/lib/components/*.svelte (all inline-styled).
close_reason: Adopted shadcn-svelte/bits-ui: components.json + cn() + /components/ui primitives (Button/Checkbox/Select over bits-ui); 5 components migrated. ADR engram-e38 satisfied.

title: workflow uses node-version 20 but astro@6.4.5 requires >=22.12.0 — CI build will fail
description: .github/workflows/docs-site.yaml (both build and deploy jobs) specifies node-version: "20". The lockfile at docs-site/pnpm-lock.yaml records astro@6.4.5 with engines: {node: '>=22.12.0'}, @astrojs/mdx@6.0.2 with node: '>=22.12.0', and @astrojs/prism@4.0.2 with node: '>=22.12.0'. Running pnpm install --frozen-lockfile or pnpm build on Node 20 will fail with an unsupported engine error. Fix: change node-version to "22" (or "22.12" / "22.x") in both jobs.

title: go.sum drift fails required 'test' CI gate
description: The required 'test' CI job fails on the 'go.mod tidy check' step. CI runs 'go mod tidy && git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum' and finds a diff in go.sum (several golang.org/x/* packages bumped from their PR-committed versions, e.g. golang.org/x/tools v0.44.0→v0.45.0, golang.org/x/crypto v0.51.0→v0.52.0). This means the go.sum committed in the PR was produced from a different module graph than the one CI resolves after the new connect-go/buf dependencies land. The 'test' job is a required status check in the protect-main ruleset, so this blocks merge. Fix: run 'go mod tidy' locally and commit the updated go.sum before merging.
close_reason: Fixed: go mod tidy (commit trvwtvmn) — go.mod direct requires + go.sum buf transitives; tidy now idempotent, CI tidy check passes.

title: SearchDiscoveriesResponse uses Memory type, silently dropping discovery-specific fields
description: proto/engram/v1/engram.proto line 60: 'message SearchDiscoveriesResponse { repeated Memory discoveries = 1; }' uses the Memory message type. However, internal/store/store.go's Memory struct has three discovery-specific fields: Kind (string, 'map'|'fact'), Citations ([]Citation), and Summary (string). These are zero-valued for ordinary memories but carry the substance of a discovery record. The proto Memory message (proto lines 11-26) defines none of these fields, so any discovery returned via SearchDiscoveries will silently lose its kind, citations, and summary on the wire. Fix: either add Kind/Summary/Citations to the proto Memory message, or define a separate Discovery message type for this response.
close_reason: Superseded by engram-1hb (needs-human design decision). The Memory-reuse for SearchDiscoveriesResponse was a twice-ratified plan choice (design-review r2 + plan-review r1 READY); whether to surface kind/citations/summary is a design call, not auto-implementable. Tracked outside the epic so it doesn't block the sentinel.

title: PR violates explicit 'Not used here: protobuf/buf' project convention
description: AGENTS.md line 39 states: '**Not used here:** protobuf/buf, database migrations, viper, cocogitto.' This PR introduces exactly that: proto/engram/v1/engram.proto, buf.yaml, buf.gen.yaml, go tool buf, and a 29 KB generated gen/ tree. This is a direct violation of an explicit project convention, not a matter of judgment. Before landing, the convention must either be updated to reflect the new direction (if that is deliberate) or the PR must be reverted.
close_reason: Superseded by engram-8sl.7. The 'revert' option is invalid: protobuf/buf adoption is a conscious, Accepted-ADR reversal (engram-8xe ConnectRPC, engram-bgj Go-BFF). Correct remediation = update CLAUDE.md convention, tracked in engram-8sl.7.

title: Pre-upgrade records with absent owner key become invisible after upgrade
description:
**Location:** internal/store/store.go — ownerOrSharedCondition, ownerScopeFilter; all callers (Search, List, GetReadable, SearchDiscovery)

**What is wrong:**
ownerOrSharedCondition(sub) builds a Qdrant Should filter with NewMatch("owner", sub) OR NewMatch("visibility", "shared"). In Qdrant, NewMatch on a missing payload key never matches — it only matches records where the key exists with the given value.

Records written before this PR do not include an owner key in their Qdrant payload (the old payload() function did not include an owner field). After upgrade, these records have no owner key. In an auth-disabled deployment (sub==""), NewMatch("owner", "") requires the key to be present with value ""; a missing key is not a match. In an auth-enabled deployment (sub=="user-sub-xyz"), the mismatch is obvious. In both cases, all pre-upgrade records immediately become invisible to search_memory, list_memory, get_memory, and search_discovery on the first request after upgrade.

The migration command (migrate-set-owner) is the documented fix, but:
1. It is framed as a post-upgrade step the operator "should" run, not as a hard prerequisite that blocks data loss.
2. There is no startup check or server-start warning that fails (or even warns) when NewIsEmpty("owner") count > 0.
3. The window between upgrade and migration results in silent data loss from the perspective of MCP tool consumers — every record disappears.

**Evidence:** ownerOrSharedCondition uses qdrant.NewMatch("owner", sub) — this is an exact match condition, not an IsNull/IsEmpty complement. Per Qdrant docs, payload match conditions do not match absent keys.

**Affected tools:** search_memory, list_memory, get_memory, search_discovery, delete_all (see companion finding), delete_memory.

**Suggested fix:**
- Add a startup check in buildDepsFromEnv() or Register() that counts NewIsEmpty("owner") records and logs a loud WARNING (not fatal, to allow fresh installs). Example: if count > 0, log.Printf("WARNING: %d records lack owner; run 'engram migrate-set-owner' before serving requests or all reads will return empty").
- Or consider making ownerOrSharedCondition also include NewIsEmpty("owner") in the Should clause for the auth-disabled (sub=="") case, treating missing-owner as equivalent to owner=="" — which matches the designed single-bucket invariant without requiring migration for auth-disabled deployments.
- At minimum, rename the migration framing in README/CLAUDE.md from 'should run once' to 'MUST run before serving requests after upgrade'.
close_reason: Fixed in 'fix: address PR #38 review findings' (uyvoknto); review-gate PASS.

title: List() doc comment still claims unconditional CreatedAt-desc ordering after PR adds Ascending
description: internal/store/store.go:718-722, the exported doc comment on Store.List: "List returns a CreatedAt-desc page of the caller's readable records in scope, the exact matched total (server-side Count), and a nextCursor..." This comment predates the PR but is directly invalidated by it: the PR adds ListOptions.Ascending (store.go:653-657, new field) and honors it in this same function (store.go:775-778: `dir := qdrant.Direction_Desc; if opts.Ascending { dir = qdrant.Direction_Asc }`), used by the new list_rules handler (internal/server/rules.go:200-205, Ascending:true) to get oldest-first ordering. The top-level func doc was never updated, so 'go doc', IDE hovers, and pkg.go.dev still describe List as unconditionally CreatedAt-desc, which is now false for a documented, exercised call pattern (list_rules, and TestListAscendingOrder in store_test.go). Fix: amend the List() doc comment to note that ordering is CreatedAt-desc by default, ascending when opts.Ascending is set (offset/all path only).
close_reason: Fixed: List() doc comment now describes desc-default/ascending-optional ordering. Commit lzyn.

title: update_memory's Shared field silently bypasses the rules-are-always-shared guard, unlike set_visibility
description:
The PR adds a rule invariant — "rules are always shared; set_visibility is
rejected for rules, delete the rule instead" — enforced in setVisibility
(internal/server/tools.go:873-891, checking rec.Category == "rule" before
calling d.st.SetVisibility) and covered by TestSetVisibilityRejectsRule.

But updateMemory (internal/server/tools.go:768-820) also accepts a Shared
*bool field (updateArgs.Shared, tools.go:378) that flows straight through to
d.st.Update (tools.go:819 -> internal/store/store.go Update(), which sets
cur.Visibility from `shared` with zero category check). The new rule guard
added at tools.go:789-796 only validates a.Summary for cur.Category == "rule"
— it never checks a.Shared. So a caller can silently flip a rule's visibility
to private via update_memory(id=<rule>, content=<unchanged>, shared=false),
completely bypassing the invariant that set_visibility explicitly rejects, with
no error and no log line.

Confirmed live against a real Qdrant testcontainer (temporary test added and
reverted, not committed):

    d.storeRule(ctx, storeRuleArgs{Content: "original rule text", Scope: scope, Summary: "original summary"})
    d.updateMemory(ctx, updateArgs{ID: id, Content: "original rule text", Shared: &false})
    // err == nil
    got, _ := d.st.Get(ctx, id)
    // got.Visibility == "" (private) — the rule silently lost its always-shared
    // guarantee; list_rules/session-start index for other actors no longer sees it.

Existing test coverage (TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard, rules_test.go) only exercises
the Summary guard cases (newline/oversize/clear); it never exercises a.Shared,
so this gap has no regression coverage today.

Impact: the "rules are always shared, delete instead of unsharing" contract
documented in CLAUDE.md and docs-site/reference/tools.md is not actually
enforced — it silently degrades to "shared unless you touch it through the
other mutation path." Since this is a resource-owner-only bypass (updateMemory
is gated by FetchForUpdate, owner-only) it isn't a cross-tenant leak, but it is
a silent, unlogged violation of a data-integrity invariant the PR explicitly
built and tested for the other mutation path — a rule an owner "edits" (even
just re-saving content, if they also pass shared=false out of habit or a stale
client) can vanish from every other actor's shared rule index with zero
feedback.

Suggested fix: mirror the setVisibility guard in updateMemory — reject when
cur.Category == "rule" && a.Shared != nil (either always, matching
set_visibility's "delete instead" message, or only when *a.Shared == false,
since forcing shared=true on a rule is a no-op). Add a regression test
alongside TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard exercising updateArgs.Shared.

Files:
- internal/server/tools.go:768-820 (updateMemory, rule guard at 789-796)
- internal/server/tools.go:375-381 (updateArgs.Shared)
- internal/server/tools.go:862-899 (setVisibility, the guard being bypassed)
- internal/server/rules_test.go:190-227 (TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard — no Shared case)
close_reason: Duplicate of engram-sysc.5 (update_memory shared=false un-shares a rule) — canonical finding tracks the fix

title: storeRule replace-in-place path (short_id carry-forward, cross-owner leak guard) has zero test coverage
description:
internal/server/rules.go:92-155 (storeRule) has a full a.ID != "" replace-in-place branch (lines 103-123): ResolvePointID, an OwnedOrAbsent ownership gate, a 404-indistinguishability re-wrap that echoes the caller's original input (never the resolved UUID), and short_id carry-forward via d.st.Get. None of this is exercised by internal/server/rules_test.go — TestStoreRuleHandler and TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard only ever call storeRule with a.ID=="" (create). No test in the PR sets a.ID to replace an existing rule, verifies the short_id survives the replace, verifies a nonexistent short_id is rejected rather than silently seeding a new record, or verifies a cross-owner replace attempt fails without leaking the resolved UUID.

This is a significant gap because the code's own doc comment says it 'mirrors storeDiscovery' (tools.go:551-624), and the implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-06-rule-memory-kind.md, Task 3) explicitly directs the author to mirror storeDiscovery 'including the id-replace ownership gate via OwnedOrAbsent.' storeDiscovery's identical pattern is covered by four dedicated tests in tools_test.go: TestStoreAndSearchDiscoveryHandlers (id-replace branch), TestStoreDiscoveryMintsThenReplacePreservesShortID, TestStoreDiscoveryRejectsNonexistentShortIDAsNew, and TestStoreDiscoveryCrossOwnerShortIDDoesNotLeakUUID. The rule twin of that exact code has none of the four.

Concrete risk: if a future refactor of rules.go's replace branch breaks the OwnedOrAbsent gate or the ErrNotFound re-wrap, another actor could overwrite (or learn about the existence of) another owner's rule via ID/short_id guessing, and no test in the suite would catch it. Likewise a broken short_id carry-forward would silently mint a new short_id on every rule edit, invalidating any short_id a user or session-start index had already pinned.

Fix: add rule-specific analogs of the four storeDiscovery tests above to internal/server/rules_test.go — e.g. TestStoreRuleReplacePreservesShortID, TestStoreRuleRejectsNonexistentShortIDAsNew, TestStoreRuleCrossOwnerShortIDDoesNotLeakUUID — mirroring their discovery counterparts but against d.storeRule / rule:* scopes.
close_reason: Fixed: added TestStoreRuleReplacePreservesShortID + TestStoreRuleCrossOwnerShortIDDoesNotLeakUUID mirroring the storeDiscovery tests. Commit lzyn.

title: ListOptions.Ascending is silently ignored in cursor-mode paging, unlike the analogous Cursor/Offset guard
description:
internal/store/store.go:653-657 adds ListOptions.Ascending (bool), documented as: "Honored only on the offset/all path used by list_rules; cursor mode is unaffected (rules do not paginate). Zero value preserves the existing desc behavior." This is an invariant expressed only in a doc comment, not enforced by the type or by List().

Store.List (store.go:723-...) does check opts.Ascending before the offset-mode Scroll call (store.go:775-778: `dir := qdrant.Direction_Desc; if opts.Ascending { dir = qdrant.Direction_Asc }`), so the field works correctly for list_rules's actual call (Limit:0, Ascending:true, no CursorMode).

But Store.listByCursor (store.go:807-813) hardcodes descending order unconditionally: `OrderBy: &qdrant.OrderBy{Key: "created_at", Direction: qdrant.PtrOf(qdrant.Direction_Desc), StartFrom: startFrom}` — opts.Ascending is never read there. So any caller who sets both Ascending:true and CursorMode:true (or a non-empty Cursor) gets silent descending order with no error, contradicting the field they explicitly set.

Compare to the existing Cursor/Offset interaction on the very same type, which IS enforced: List() rejects the invalid combination outright (store.go:740-742: `if (opts.Cursor != "" || opts.CursorMode) && opts.Offset > 0 { return ..., fmt.Errorf("list: cursor mode and offset are mutually exclusive: %w", ErrInvalidArgument) }`). No equivalent guard exists for Ascending+CursorMode/Cursor.

ListOptions is a shared, exported type used well beyond list_rules (list_memory, list_scheduled, the operator console UI path). Today's only Ascending caller (listRules, internal/server/rules.go:200-205) is safe because it never sets CursorMode/Cursor — but the type itself does not prevent a future caller from combining them and getting silently wrong results, and TestListAscendingOrder (store_test.go) only exercises the safe combination, so the gap is untested.

Fix: either honor Ascending in listByCursor's OrderBy.Direction, or reject the Ascending+CursorMode/Cursor combination in List() the same way the Cursor/Offset combination is rejected (returning ErrInvalidArgument), and add a test for the rejected/honored combination.
close_reason: Fixed: store.List returns ErrInvalidArgument for Ascending+cursor-mode; test TestListAscendingRejectedInCursorMode. Commit lzyn.

title: Missing spec-required integration tests: rule cross-actor shared-read, anon-bucket isolation, ordinary-scope search/list isolation
description:
The design spec's Testing section
(docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-rule-memory-kind-design.md:279-288)
explicitly lists these as required Integration (Qdrant) tests for the rule
feature:

  "cross-actor read (actor B reads actor A's rules via shared); anon-bucket
  isolation (mirrors TestAnonBucketDiscoveryReadIsolation); scope isolation
  (rules invisible to search_memory/list_memory over the ordinary repo
  scope)."

None of these three are present in internal/server/rules_test.go (the file
added by this PR). The file contains only: TestValidateStoreRule,
TestStoreRuleHandler, TestListRulesHandler, TestSetVisibilityRejectsRule,
TestUpdateMemoryRuleGuard — none of which exercise:

1. A second actor reading actor A's rule via the shared grant
   (GetReadable/ownerOrSharedCondition applied to category=rule).
2. Anonymous-bucket isolation for rules (mirroring
   TestAnonBucketDiscoveryReadIsolation for discovery).
3. That an ordinary (non-rule) search_memory/list_memory call over the
   scope's repo-tail does NOT surface rule:* records (the scope-prefix
   isolation the spec's "Decision: record shape" section calls out as the
   sole enforcement mechanism, since category is not a server-validated
   enum).

The underlying mechanisms are almost certainly correct by construction
(rules reuse the same GetReadable/ownerOrSharedCondition/listFilter code
paths already tested for discovery and ordinary memories), so this is a
coverage gap rather than a known functional defect — but it is a testing
requirement the spec itself enumerates as part of the feature's Definition
of Done, and the plan's Task 3/4/6 test steps did not carry it forward, so
it fell out of scope during implementation.

Fix: add the three integration tests described in the spec's Testing
section to internal/server/rules_test.go (or store_test.go for the
scope-isolation case, mirroring the pattern already used for
TestAnonBucketDiscoveryReadIsolation).
close_reason: Fixed: added TestRuleCrossActorSharedRead, TestRuleAnonBucketIsolation, TestRuleOrdinaryScopeIsolation. Commit lzyn.

title: Rules-index hook instruction renders rules AFTER the digest, contradicting ADR engram-d386's 'above the recent-10 digest'
description:
Accepted ADR engram-d386 explicitly decided: "The session-start-memory-recall
hook calls list_rules ... and renders a one-line-per-rule index ... **above
the recent-10 digest**." The design spec
(docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-rule-memory-kind-design.md:220-223) says
the same thing: "call list_rules once ... and render a Rules index as a
distinct section **above** the recent-10 digest" — and the spec's own
illustrative rendering block shows the Rules section first, listed before
any digest content.

The implementation contradicts this ordering. In
skill/engram/hooks/session-start-memory-recall:113-115, the injected
instruction reads:

    "Repository rules (normative ground truth) — after the recall digest, "
    f"call mcp__engram__list_rules once with scopes=[{joined}] and render a "
    "compact Rules index: ..."

This instruction is the LAST paragraph appended to additionalContext (after
the "REQUIRED FIRST ACTION" digest block, the "Memory store precedence"
block, and the "Capturing durable memory" block), and it explicitly tells
the agent to act "after the recall digest" — i.e., call list_rules and
render the Rules index only once the digest is already done, placing Rules
below/after the digest in the rendered output. This is the literal opposite
of the accepted ADR's decision that MUST-follow rules render as a distinct
section ABOVE the softer recency-windowed digest (the whole point being that
normative ground truth gets priority visibility over advisory recent-N
records).

No test in skill/engram/hooks/tests/test_session_start_memory_recall.py
asserts relative ordering of the two instruction blocks in the emitted
additionalContext string — only that both substrings are present — so this
regression is untested and unguarded.

Fix: reorder the instruction text (and/or explicitly instruct the agent to
render the Rules index before/above the digest it already produced) so the
emitted guidance matches ADR engram-d386's ordering decision, and add an
ordering assertion (e.g. ctx.index("Repository rules") <
ctx.index("REQUIRED FIRST ACTION")) to lock it in.
close_reason: Fixed: hook now renders Rules index ABOVE the recall digest per ADR engram-d386/spec. Commit lzyn.

comments.author: Sean Brandt
comments.text: Ordering-lock test added (commit vmp): test_rules_index_instruction_present now asserts 'ABOVE the recall digest' in the emitted context, per the review-gate's follow-up. task test:python 38 passed.

title: TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic not extended for store_rule/list_rules
description:
internal/server/tools_test.go's TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic (lines 40-103) exists specifically to catch jsonschema-generation panics at mcp.AddTool time — its own doc comment says it exercises 'every tool's argument type' and cites a real production regression: 'the exact path that panicked at startup in v0.4.2 ("tag must not begin with WORD=") because no test covered the AddTool calls in Register.'

PR #290 adds two new mcp.AddTool registrations in Register() (internal/server/tools.go): store_rule (storeRuleArgs) and list_rules (listRulesArgs), both with new jsonschema struct tags (internal/server/rules.go:25-37, e.g. Summary field's jsonschema:"REQUIRED one-line index entry..."). Neither tool was added to TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic's check(...) table (still only 11 entries: store_memory, search_memory, list_memory, get_memory, update_memory, delete_all, store_discovery, search_discovery, set_visibility, schedule_memory, list_scheduled — verified via rg on the current file, no store_rule/list_rules hits).

The new rules_test.go tests (TestStoreRuleHandler, TestListRulesHandler, etc.) call d.storeRule / d.listRules directly, bypassing mcp.AddTool entirely — so they provide zero coverage of jsonschema generation for these two arg types. TestRegisterReturnsErrorOnStoreInitFailure also doesn't reach the AddTool calls (Register returns early at buildDepsFromEnv on the induced failure). Confirmed by instrumented local test run: no test in the suite currently exercises mcp.AddTool(...storeRuleArgs...) or mcp.AddTool(...listRulesArgs...).

I verified there is no live panic today (added a throwaway check() call locally — it passes), so this is a coverage gap, not a currently-failing build. But it is a concrete, verifiable deviation from the test's own stated 'every tool' contract, and it is exactly the blind spot that caused a real v0.4.2 production panic.

Fix: add check("store_rule", ...) and check("list_rules", ...) entries to TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic mirroring the existing pattern, using storeRuleArgs and listRulesArgs.
close_reason: Fixed: added store_rule + list_rules checks to TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic. Commit lzyn.

title: docs-site tools.md reference doesn't document store_discovery id argument accepting short_id
description:
docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md line 215 (the store_discovery argument table) still reads: id | string | no | Omit to create; supply to replace in place -- unchanged by this PR.

This is inconsistent with the actual code change: internal/server/tools.go's storeDiscoveryArgs.ID jsonschema hint was updated in this same PR to 'omit to create; supply the full UUID or short_id to replace in place', and skill/engram/skills/discovering/SKILL.md was correspondingly updated to tell agents they may pass id (or short_id) to store_discovery. The docs-site reference page is the one place documenting this argument to human readers, and it was missed even though this same PR updated the analogous id-argument row for every other id-accepting tool in this file (get_memory, update_memory, delete_memory, set_visibility all got the UUID-or-short_id treatment around lines 145/166/182/258).

The same omission appears in docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/upgrade.md line 88, whose new v0.8.4 changelog entry enumerates the tools where short_id is now accepted (get_memory, update_memory, delete_memory, set_visibility, and the Connect GetMemory RPC) but likewise omits store_discovery's id argument.

Fix: update tools.md line 215's id row to mention short_id (matching the pattern used for the other five tools in the same file), and add store_discovery to the upgrade.md line 88 enumeration.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #288 branch; review-gate PASS + verification-runner all gates PASS

title: MintShortID doc comment misdescribes why the seen-map is needed vs BackfillShortIDs' actual sequential flush
description:
internal/store/store.go:1451-1456, MintShortID's doc comment says: 'When seen is non-nil, ids it returns are recorded there and candidates already in it are skipped — for a batch (backfill) that mints many ids before any is count-visible. The global Count is authoritative; seen covers the not-yet-flushed same-run window only.'

This describes a batched-mint-then-flush race that does not exist in the only caller that passes a non-nil seen map. BackfillShortIDs (store.go:1553-1562) mints and persists one short_id at a time, strictly sequentially: for each point in the page it calls MintShortID(ctx, seen), then immediately calls client.SetPayload with Wait: true for that single point, before moving to the next point. Per Qdrant's own semantics (confirmed via qdrant/qdrant docs: wait=true maps to WaitUntil::Visible, which blocks until the write is 'fully applied and visible in search results' — i.e. an immediately-following Count/Scroll is guaranteed to see it), each point's short_id is already Count-visible by the time MintShortID runs for the next point. There is no window in the current code where 'many ids' are minted 'before any is count-visible' — writes are flushed one-by-one, synchronously, before the next mint.

This means the comment's stated rationale for the seen map is factually inaccurate for the code as written. A maintainer who trusts this comment could draw wrong conclusions later — e.g. believing seen protects against an intra-batch consistency race that Qdrant's wait=true already closes, or conversely assuming it's safe to remove per-item Wait:true (batching writes for throughput) without realizing that seen currently provides no actual protection against the race such a change would introduce (seen is function-local and does not survive/help across a batched-write refactor either).

Fix: rewrite the comment to describe what seen actually guards against given the current sequential Wait:true design (e.g., a defensive/redundant safety net against pathological Qdrant Count-consistency edge cases, or an explicit statement that it exists for a future batched-write optimization that does not exist yet) rather than asserting a scenario ('many ids... before any is count-visible') that the current call site cannot produce. A prior reviewer already flagged this exact wording as suspect; this confirms it does not match BackfillShortIDs' Wait:true flush pattern.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #288 branch; review-gate PASS + verification-runner all gates PASS

title: Backfill resume-after-mid-run-failure is untested; the only cancel test never lets any work happen
description:
Design doc section 6 (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-short-id-handle-design.md) and boundary/edge-matrix item 24 explicitly call out the reason BackfillShortIDs/MintShortID use a GLOBAL short_id==candidate Count check rather than relying solely on the in-run 'seen' map: "The global check is what keeps a resumed or a concurrent backfill... from reusing an id committed outside the current run; the in-run set alone would not." This is the load-bearing correctness property for a real operational scenario: a backfill process interrupted (OOM, pod restart, network blip, Ctrl-C) partway through a large collection, then re-run.

The only test touching this area, TestBackfillShortIDsHonorsCancel (internal/store/store_test.go, added by this PR), cancels the context BEFORE calling BackfillShortIDs:

  cctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
  cancel()
  if _, err := st.BackfillShortIDs(cctx, false); err == nil { t.Error(...) }

Since the context is already cancelled when BackfillShortIDs is invoked, zero Qdrant calls or pages are processed before the error surfaces -- this only proves an already-dead context is rejected by the underlying gRPC client, not that a MID-run interruption after some pages/points are already committed leaves the collection in a state where a subsequent run correctly resumes without reusing a short_id. The test's own doc comment ("propagates context cancellation ... instead of running to completion") overstates what it actually exercises, since "running to completion" was never a possibility here.

TestBackfillShortIDs's "idempotent: second run finds nothing to do" assertion (n==0) only proves idempotency when the FIRST run fully completed for every record -- it never tests the partial-completion case where some records already carry a short_id (committed by a prior/interrupted run) and others don't, and confirms newly-minted ids for the remaining records never collide with the already-committed ones.

Suggested fix: add a test that (1) manually pre-stamps a subset of records with short_ids (simulating a prior partial run, e.g. via direct SetPayload or by running BackfillShortIDs against a context cancelled after the first page via a wrapping/counting context), (2) runs BackfillShortIDs again on the rest, and (3) asserts full uniqueness across the whole set and that no previously-set short_id changed.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #288 branch; review-gate PASS + verification-runner all gates PASS

title: Cross-owner no-leak behavior untested for update_memory/delete_memory/set_visibility by short_id
description:
PR #288 (short_id handles) implements ADR engram-xa6's no-leak invariant identically in all four MCP by-id handlers: internal/server/tools.go updateMemory (line 771), getMemory (821), deleteMemory (839), setVisibility (859) each call ResolvePointID then re-wrap a downstream ErrNotFound as fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", store.ErrNotFound, a.ID) so the error echoes only the caller-supplied short_id, never the resolved UUID of another owner's private record.

Only getMemory's variant of this behavior has a direct cross-owner test: TestShortIDCrossOwnerVisibility in internal/server/tools_test.go (~line 1374) stores a private record as owner-A, resolves its short_id as owner-B, and asserts the ErrNotFound message contains the short_id but not the UUID. TestStoreDiscoveryCrossOwnerShortIDDoesNotLeakUUID and TestConnectGetMemoryCrossOwnerShortIDDoesNotLeakUUID cover the store_discovery-replace and Connect GetMemory call sites respectively.

updateMemory, deleteMemory, and setVisibility — three of the design doc's six enumerated by-id call sites (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-short-id-handle-design.md, table in section 3, and boundary/edge-matrix item 4/28) — have ZERO test coverage proving their identical re-wrap logic actually fires when addressed by another owner's short_id. TestByIDToolsAcceptShortID (tools_test.go ~line 1345) exercises update/delete/set_visibility by short_id but only in a same-owner (owner-A calling on its own record) scenario, so it can't catch a leak.

Since this is a security-relevant, ADR-governed invariant (never distinguish 'exists but forbidden' from 'not found'), and three of six call sites implementing it have no negative-path test, this is a genuine coverage gap despite the code appearing correct by pattern-matching against the tested get_memory case.

Suggested fix: extend TestShortIDCrossOwnerVisibility (or add a sibling test) to also attempt update_memory, delete_memory, and set_visibility against owner-A's private record's short_id as owner-B, asserting ErrNotFound and asserting the error message never contains the resolved UUID.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #288 branch; review-gate PASS + verification-runner all gates PASS

title: backfill-short-ids CLI discards the partial-progress count when BackfillShortIDs errors mid-run
description:
cmd/engram/backfill.go:38-41 (RunE for backfill-short-ids):

    n, err := st.BackfillShortIDs(ctx, backfillDryRun)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    if backfillDryRun { cmd.Printf("[dry-run] would backfill %d record(s)\n", n) } else { cmd.Printf("backfilled %d record(s)\n", n) }
    return nil

On any error path, n is discarded -- only err propagates. root.go's Execute() (cobra SilenceErrors/SilenceUsage=true) prints just the literal string 'Error: ' followed by the error's message to stderr on RunE failure, so that is the ONLY output an operator ever sees.

This matters because internal/store/store.go's BackfillShortIDs (store.go:1518-1571) is NOT an atomic bulk operation like its siblings PruneExpired (store.go:1384) and MigrateSetOwner (store.go:1616) -- those do a single Count-plus-filtered-bulk-op and correctly return zero alongside the error on failure (partial progress is meaningless for a single atomic RPC). BackfillShortIDs instead pages via ScrollAndOffset and calls MintShortID plus SetPayload per point, incrementing n as it goes, and deliberately returns the ACCUMULATED n alongside err on every failure branch (ScrollAndOffset error, MintShortID error, SetPayload error). The store layer clearly intends partial progress to be observable -- the CLI wrapper just throws it away.

Concretely: a Qdrant hiccup after backfilling 900,000 of 1,000,000 records, the default --timeout of 5m expiring on a large collection, or the operator's own Ctrl-C (which the --timeout flag help text explicitly invites: 'also cancellable via Ctrl-C') all produce the exact same output: just 'Error: ' plus the raw error, with zero indication of how far the run got. An operator cannot tell 'made no progress, investigate before retrying' from '999,999 of 1,000,000 done, just re-run it'.

Compare the sibling reindex command (cmd/engram/reindex.go), which wires store.ReindexOptions.Progress to cmd.PrintErrf specifically so a mid-run failure still leaves an incremental progress trail on stderr -- the established pattern in this codebase for long-running, resumable, per-point operator commands. backfill-short-ids should follow it.

Suggested fix: at minimum, print the returned n before returning the error, e.g. cmd.Printf("backfilled %d record(s) before error: %v\n", n, err) then return err. Or add a Progress-style callback mirroring reindex's, so per-page progress streams to stderr as the run proceeds (this also covers the process-killed-outright case, e.g. OOM, before RunE can return anything).

No test currently exercises this error path either -- backfill_test.go only checks that the --dry-run/--timeout flags exist -- so the gap is unguarded going forward.
close_reason: Fixed on PR #288 branch; review-gate PASS + verification-runner all gates PASS

title: OwnerRemapSource doc comment's 'Unlike Subject' dispatch claim is backwards and self-contradictory
description:
internal/store/store.go's OwnerRemapSource doc comment (lines ~255-266) now says: "Unlike Subject, dispatch happens via a single type switch in RemapOwner (not per-variant interface methods) so an unhandled/nil source is nil-safe by construction -- a type switch's default arm matches a nil interface value without panicking, the same property that makes Subject's enforcement gates nil-safe."

This is factually backwards, and self-contradictory within the same sentence. Subject's actual enforcement dispatch is ALSO done via type switches, not per-variant interface methods:

- internal/store/subject.go's own doc comment (line 18-19): "read filters and write gates use the exhaustive type switch (with its default-deny arm), never Owner()." Owner() is explicitly called out as NOT the enforcement accessor.
- docs/adr/engram-12c-represent-authz-subject-as-sealed-go-interface.md line 17: "Every store enforcement gate (read filters + id/bulk write gates) uses an exhaustive type switch whose default arm denies."
- internal/store/store.go itself contains six separate switch-on-subj.(type) blocks implementing Subject enforcement (case authenticated / case anonymous): ownerOrSharedCondition (~428), ownerOnlyCondition (~449), GetReadable (~1053), getWritable (~1083), OwnedOrAbsent (~1124), DeleteAll (~1291).

So the comparison is inverted: Subject's real authorization dispatch already uses the exact same type-switch-with-default-arm pattern that OwnerRemapSource now adopts. The only per-variant interface method Subject has is Owner(), which is a persistence/stamping accessor explicitly documented as unused for enforcement -- it is not "dispatch" in the sense the comment means. The comment's last clause even admits this by crediting "Subject's enforcement gates" with the identical nil-safety property it just claimed was unique to OwnerRemapSource, contradicting its own opening "Unlike Subject" framing.

This is a new/reworded comment (not present in turn 1's diff) introduced since the last review, so it is in scope as newly-added prose making a demonstrably false comparative claim about the codebase's own design.

Suggested fix: correct the comparison -- e.g. "Like Subject, dispatch happens via an exhaustive type switch (in RemapOwner, mirroring Subject's enforcement gates) rather than per-variant interface methods, so ..." -- or drop the Subject comparison for the dispatch mechanism entirely and keep only the "sealed sum" analogy, which is accurate.
close_reason: Fixed: rewrote the OwnerRemapSource doc comment — Subject's enforcement gates DO use exhaustive type switches (confirmed via subject.go's own doc comment and 6 switch sites in store.go); the comment now says 'like Subject's enforcement gates' and explains the actual difference (no per-variant accessor needed).

title: oidc_exchange_test.go reinvents go-oidc's built-in oidctest fake OIDC server
description:
internal/webauth/oidc_exchange_test.go:33-108 (newFakeOIDCServer + mustSignJWT) hand-rolls a discovery endpoint, a /jwks endpoint, and JWT signing that github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3/oidc/oidctest — a package of the OIDC library engram already depends on directly (go.mod already pins github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3 v3.19.0) — provides out of the box:

- oidctest.Server{PublicKeys: [...]} implements http.Handler and serves /.well-known/openid-configuration and /keys (JWKS) itself, replacing the ~18 lines of mux.HandleFunc for those two paths (lines 46-63).
- oidctest.SignIDToken(priv, keyID, alg, rawClaimsJSON) replaces the hand-written mustSignJWT (lines 96-108), which duplicates oidctest's own internal newToken implementation almost line for line (same jose.NewSigner + kid header pattern).

Confirmed go-oidc/v3@v3.19.0's own go.mod requires github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 v4.1.4 — the exact version this PR's go.mod change (lines 138-150) promotes from indirect to direct. Since go-jose is not imported directly anywhere else in the repo (grep confirms only the two new test files touch it), that go.mod promotion is a side effect solely of this hand-rolled harness importing go-jose/jose and go-jose/jwt directly. Routing through oidctest removes the need for the test to import go-jose at all, which would let go-jose stay an indirect dependency (smaller direct dependency surface) and cut ~25-30 lines of duplicated discovery/JWKS/signing plumbing.

oidctest.Server only serves discovery+JWKS, not a /token endpoint, so the fake /token handler (lines 65-91) still needs to be hand-written for the code-exchange flow under test — but it can be composed with oidctest.Server via a mux (register /token on the custom handler, oidctest.Server as the mux's default handler for everything else), and mustSignJWT's body becomes a one-line call to oidctest.SignIDToken (claims need json.Marshal into the raw-JSON string oidctest expects, a trivial conversion from the existing map[string]any).

Suggested fix: replace the /.well-known/openid-configuration and /jwks HandleFuncs with an oidctest.Server mounted on the mux, and replace mustSignJWT's body with oidctest.SignIDToken. Then re-run 'go mod tidy' — go-jose should fall back to indirect since no source or test file imports it directly anymore.

title: Self-contradictory comment on nil OwnerRemapSource test case in store_test.go
description:
internal/store/store_test.go:2073-2078 (TestRemapOwner). The comment reads:

'A zero-value/nil source (no Missing/Anon/From selection) is now a compile-time-unrepresentable state via the sealed OwnerRemapSource interface — RemapMissing()/RemapAnon()/RemapFrom() are the only constructors, so the runtime "exactly one selected" check that used to live here is gone. Only the nil case (an explicit zero value) remains reachable and must still fail closed.'

This is internally contradictory: the first sentence asserts the zero-value/nil source is now 'compile-time-unrepresentable', then the very next sentence admits 'the nil case ... remains reachable' — and the test on the next line (s.RemapOwner(ctx, nil, "to", false)) both constructs and exercises exactly that 'unrepresentable' state.

What actually became unrepresentable via sealing is the *multi-select* combination (e.g. the old OwnerRemapSource{Missing: true, From: "x"}), because RemapMissing()/RemapAnon()/RemapFrom() each return a single sealed variant with no way to combine fields. The interface's own zero value (nil) is NOT unrepresentable — it is trivially constructible (var src OwnerRemapSource, or the nil literal) and is exactly what RemapOwner's src == nil guard (store.go, RemapOwner) exists to reject. The store.go doc comment on OwnerRemapSource gets this right ('the zero value is nil, which RemapOwner rejects rather than treating as a default selection'); this test comment conflates that reachable nil case with the now-eliminated multi-select case and states the opposite of what it means.

Fix: separate the two claims, e.g. 'Sealing eliminates the old multi-select combination (Missing+From together) at compile time; only the interface's own zero value (nil) remains constructible, and RemapOwner must still reject it explicitly (see the check below).'
close_reason: Fixed: rewrote the store_test.go comment to state precisely what sealing eliminated (the multi-select combo) vs what remains reachable (nil).

title: OwnerRemapSource's nil-safety relies on a single manual guard, not the structural type-switch pattern Subject uses
close_reason: Fixed: refactored RemapOwner to dispatch via an exhaustive type switch (nil-safe by construction, matching Subject's pattern) instead of interface methods + a manual nil guard.

title: buildRemapSource has no test pinning --from-missing/--from-anon/--from wiring to the correct sealed constructor
description: cmd/engram/migrate.go's buildRemapSource (lines ~72-99) was rewritten in PR #266 to route the CLI's --from-missing/--from-anon/--from flags to three distinct sealed store.OwnerRemapSource constructors via a switch: case missing -> store.RemapMissing(), case anon -> store.RemapAnon(), default -> store.RemapFrom(from). The pre-existing cmd/engram/migrate_test.go (TestRemapOwnerFlagValidation, not modified by this PR) only asserts err != nil / err == nil for each flag combination; it never inspects which concrete OwnerRemapSource variant was actually returned. Because Missing/Anon/From select semantically disjoint record sets on Store.RemapOwner (IsEmpty(owner) vs owner=="" vs owner==<value> per store.go's doc comment), a switch-case mix-up (e.g. case missing: src = store.RemapAnon()) would compile, would not trigger any error path, and would pass every existing test (both TestRemapOwnerFlagValidation and store_test.go's TestRemapOwner, which only exercises the constructors directly, never through buildRemapSource) -- yet would silently cause operators running 'migrate-remap-owner --from-missing' to re-stamp the wrong record set in a real Qdrant collection. This is a real, uncaught gap in a destructive/irreversible admin migration tool.\n\nSuggested fix: since OwnerRemapSource's concrete types (remapMissing/remapAnon/remapFrom) are unexported in package store, cmd/engram tests can still pin the wiring black-box via reflect.TypeOf(src).String() (e.g. assert it equals "store.remapMissing" for the --from-missing case, "store.remapAnon" for --from-anon, "store.remapFrom" for --from). Add these assertions to the existing 'missing ok' / 'anon ok' / 'from ok' table cases in TestRemapOwnerFlagValidation.
close_reason: Fixed: added reflect.TypeOf assertions to TestRemapOwnerFlagValidation pinning missing/anon/from to their concrete sealed variants.

title: Embedding-instructions guide table gives wrong input_type values for Voyage (should be query/document, not search_query/search_document)
description:
Location: docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/embedding-instructions.md:99

New table row (added this PR):

  | Provider / model | ENGRAM_EMBED_QUERY_PARAMS / ENGRAM_EMBED_DOCUMENT_PARAMS |
  | OpenRouter, Cohere embed v3, Voyage | {"input_type":"search_query"} / {"input_type":"search_document"} |

This collapses Voyage into the same row/values as Cohere, but Voyage's input_type parameter does not accept "search_query"/"search_document" — per Voyage's own API docs (docs.voyageai.com/reference/embeddings-api, and MongoDB's Voyage AI docs mirror), the valid input_type values are `query` and `document` only. Cohere's embed v3 API (docs.cohere.com/reference/embed) is the one that defines `search_query`/`search_document` as its enum values — this is provider-specific, not a shared convention.

The PR's own prior (pre-change) version of this table had this right: Cohere used `input_type=search_query` / `search_document (required)`, and Voyage was listed separately as `input_type=query` / `document (optional)`. The rewrite merged the rows and lost the distinct, correct value for Voyage, replacing it with Cohere's value.

Impact: an operator following this guide to configure ENGRAM_EMBED_QUERY_PARAMS/ENGRAM_EMBED_DOCUMENT_PARAMS for a Voyage embedder would set an invalid input_type value (search_query/search_document instead of query/document), defeating the asymmetric retrieval optimization this feature exists to enable.

Fix: split the merged row back out (or otherwise keep Voyage's value distinct) so Voyage shows `{"input_type":"query"}` / `{"input_type":"document"}`.
close_reason: duplicate of engram-lqh7.7 (same root cause: Voyage input_type wrong in docs table); spec-aspect finding is the canonical one
