This matters operationally: the surrounding comments and PR description prominently advertise 'fail-closed' and 'source left untouched', leading an operator to infer that any error leaves things in a clean state. An operator who receives a mid-loop scroll error may retry without first deleting the target, resulting in a target that appears complete but is missing records from after the failure point.

Similarly, an Upsert call failure (line ~1251) leaves the target partially written with no cleanup.

Suggested fix: wrap the error message to note the target may be partially populated, e.g.:
  'reindex: scroll source (target %q may be partially populated — delete before retrying): %w'
This is a documentation-of-invariant gap rather than a code-path bug, but it violates the operational contract implied by the 'fail-closed' framing.
close_reason: Fixed: Reindex doc now states the no-rollback/idempotent-retry contract; mid-loop errors are now visible (see .11)

title: embed error on later point leaves already-upserted points in target (partial write undetected)
description:
TestReindexFailsClosedOnEmbedError uses a `failing` embedder that errors on every invocation. With 2 seeded points both processed in a single page, the first embed call fails before any upsert, so the test assertion ('no points written') is trivially satisfied: the collection may not even be created yet (EnsureCollection is called before the loop, but with 2 points and fail-on-first-embed the first upsert never fires).

The untested scenario is: N points seeded, the embedder succeeds for points 1..K and fails on point K+1. In that case K points are already in the target when the error fires, the function returns the error, and the target is left with a partial population. The operator's visibility into this is only the returned ReindexResult counts (Scanned=K+1, Upserted=K) -- no rollback, no cleanup, no indication the target is incomplete.

This is not necessarily a bug in the implementation (partial-write-then-retry is a valid design), but the test as written does not exercise or document the actual failure contract for partial writes. A test with 3+ points where the embedder fails on point 2 (after successfully embedding point 1) would expose the real behavior and either confirm the contract or catch a regression.

File: internal/store/reindex_test.go (TestReindexFailsClosedOnEmbedError)
close_reason: Fixed: TestReindexPartialWriteOnLateEmbedError covers embed failure on a later point (1 upserted, error surfaced, count matches)

title: reindex silently re-embeds empty string for points without a 'content' key, corrupting their vectors
description:
File: internal/store/store.go, line 1237 (diff line ~591)

The reindex inner loop reads content via:

    content := p.Payload["content"].GetStringValue()

GetStringValue() on a nil *qdrant.Value silently returns "". Any point whose payload lacks a "content" key (schema-drift record, discovery point, or any future category that stores the embeddable text under a different key) will be re-embedded using an empty string, producing a near-zero-entropy vector. That vector is then upserted verbatim into the target collection with the original owner/visibility payload intact.

Security-relevant consequence: the record's vector no longer represents its content, making it invisible to semantic search (search_memory, search_discovery). For a pre-isolation record (missing 'owner') this is indistinguishable from silent data loss: the data survives in the target but can never be recalled semantically. For a shared record it means the owner loses the ability to retrieve it or delete it by search. The authz fields (owner, visibility) are preserved correctly — this is not an owner-field corruption — but it is a data-integrity failure that undermines the correctness guarantee the reindex is supposed to provide.

Suggested fix: detect a missing/empty content key and either skip the point with a warning log (counting skipped), or return an error to fail-closed (consistent with the embed-error policy). A warn-and-skip approach with a logged count is preferable for operational use:

    rawContent, hasContent := p.Payload["content"]
    content := ""
    if hasContent {
        content = rawContent.GetStringValue()
    }
    if content == "" {
        slog.WarnContext(ctx, "reindex: skipping point with empty/missing content", "id", p.Id.GetUuid())
        res.Skipped++
        continue
    }

Add a Skipped field to ReindexResult and surface it in the CLI output. The test already seeds a raw point with a 'content' key (value 'bravo'), so the existing test does not cover the missing-key path — add a test point with no content key to confirm skip behaviour.
close_reason: Fixed: Reindex skips empty-content points (no garbage vector) + ReindexResult.Skipped counter; TestReindexSkipsEmptyContent

title: pagination second page never exercised: scroll cursor path dead in all reindex tests
description:
Store.Reindex scrolls the source collection in pages (batch=256 by default), advancing via the ScrollAndOffset cursor stored in `offset`. The code path at store.go:1259-1260 (`offset = next` → loop continues) is exercised only when a page returns a non-nil `next`. All three tests seed exactly 2 points, so the first scroll call always returns both points and next==nil, breaking the loop immediately. The continue-loop branch — including the second and subsequent page fetches — is never reached.

A bug in cursor handling (e.g. off-by-one on offset, double-counting the last record of a page, or a nil-offset sent to Qdrant on the second call causing it to restart from the beginning) would be invisible to the current suite.

File: internal/store/reindex_test.go

Fix: Add a test that seeds N+1 points where N is ReindexOptions.Batch (pass Batch:1 and seed 2 points — the cheapest way), verifies Scanned==2, and asserts both points land in the target. This exercises the cursor advance path without seeding 257 real points.
close_reason: Fixed: TestReindexMultiPageCursor (Batch:1, 3 points) exercises the ScrollAndOffset next-page cursor path

title: list_scheduled state=all omits active-window carve-out, may mislead agents
description:
File: skill/engram/skills/curating-memory/SKILL.md — Scheduling section, paragraph 2.

The prose reads: 'list_scheduled surfaces those hidden records (state: scheduled default | expired | all).'

The word 'hidden' and the three-state enumeration imply that state=all covers every windowed record that is out of normal recall. This is wrong. The implementation (store.go ScheduledAll, scheduledStateCondition) defines 'all' as the union of pending (not yet active) and expired — it explicitly excludes currently-active windowed records (those whose not_before is in the past and not_after is in the future). Active windowed records surface normally via search_memory and list_memory; they never appear in list_scheduled regardless of state. The registered tool description in tools.go line 572 makes this explicit: 'Active memories surface via list_memory/search_memory.'

An agent following the skill that wants to find a windowed memory currently inside its active window may incorrectly reach for list_scheduled state=all and find nothing, then conclude the record is missing.

Suggested fix: add a clarifying sentence after the state enum, e.g.: 'Active windowed records — those currently inside their window — surface through normal search_memory / list_memory and are never returned by list_scheduled regardless of state.'
close_reason: Fixed: added 'A windowed record inside its active window surfaces normally through search_memory/list_memory' + explicit 'never the active ones, so an in-window record absent from list_scheduled is reached through ordinary recall, not missing.'

title: scheduledStateCondition godoc misidentifies 'now' parameter type as *float64
description:
File: internal/store/store.go, function scheduledStateCondition.

The godoc comment reads:

  // scheduledStateCondition returns the inverse-window clause for a state. now is
  // epoch seconds as *float64 (Qdrant Range field type).

But the function signature is:

  func scheduledStateCondition(state ScheduledState, now time.Time) *qdrant.Condition

'now' is time.Time, not 'epoch seconds as *float64'. The *float64 is the type of sec (the local variable qdrant.PtrOf(sec)) used inside the Qdrant Range struct — an implementation detail, not the parameter type.

A reader trusting this comment would have a false understanding of the function's interface. The comment should read something like: 'now is the reference time; epoch-second conversions to *float64 are handled internally for the Qdrant Range field.'
close_reason: Fixed: scheduledStateCondition godoc corrected (now is time.Time, not *float64).

title: scheduleMemory: capture time.Now() once for both window validation and CreatedAt
description:
internal/server/tools.go — scheduleMemory calls time.Now().UTC() twice: once as the 'now' argument to parseWindow (for not_after future validation) and once for m.CreatedAt. If the wall clock advances between the two calls the validation instant will differ from the stored creation timestamp. More importantly, the validation contract (not_after must be after 'now') is silently checked against a different 'now' than the one stamped on the record.

Fix: capture a single now := time.Now().UTC() at the top of scheduleMemory and pass it to both parseWindow and m.CreatedAt. This also makes the handler's time source mockable from a single point if the Store's WithClock pattern is ever extended to handlers.

Before:
  nb, na, err := parseWindow(a, time.Now().UTC())
  ...
  m := store.Memory{ ..., CreatedAt: time.Now().UTC(), ... }

After:
  now := time.Now().UTC()
  nb, na, err := parseWindow(a, now)
  ...
  m := store.Memory{ ..., CreatedAt: now, ... }
close_reason: Fixed: scheduleMemory captures time.Now() once for validation + CreatedAt.

title: list_scheduled leaks other owners' shared-but-inactive records before their scheduled reveal time
description:
internal/store/store.go — ListScheduled

The ListScheduled filter uses ownerOrSharedCondition(subj), which for an authenticated caller matches owner==sub OR visibility=="shared". This means any authenticated user can retrieve another owner's record that is both shared AND in scheduled or expired state via list_scheduled.

The design intent is temporal access control: a scheduled record is hidden from recall until not_before passes, giving the owner control over when it becomes visible. But list_scheduled bypasses that gate for shared records. An authenticated caller can discover a record's content and scheduling metadata (not_before, not_after) from another owner BEFORE the owner intended it to be active.

The tool description says 'List your windowed memories the recall gate is hiding.' The word 'your' signals ownership-scoped access, not shared access.

The CLAUDE.md contract says shared records are 'readable by any authenticated caller' — but this was written in the context of active/revealed records surfaced through search_memory/list_memory. Extending that grant to scheduled/expired records visible only through the management view list_scheduled defeats the temporal reveal mechanism.

Fix: change the ListScheduled filter to restrict to owner==sub only (not shared). The authenticated arm should be:
  qdrant.NewMatch("owner", subj.sub)
rather than ownerOrSharedCondition(subj). Other owners' shared records that are pending or expired are not the caller's records to manage.
close_reason: Fixed: ListScheduled now owner-only (ownerOnlyCondition); shared+scheduled records no longer leak cross-actor. TestListScheduledOwnerIsolation added. Verified APPROVE.

title: ListScheduled leaks cross-actor shared+scheduled records: no isolation test
description:
ListScheduled uses ownerOrSharedCondition, which for authenticated callers matches (owner==sub OR visibility=="shared"). This means actor B's shared+scheduled records appear in actor A's list_scheduled result — the same shared-read grant that applies to normal recall also applies here. Whether that is intended behavior is a design question, but it is currently unverified: no test exercises cross-actor visibility through list_scheduled.

The existing tests (TestListScheduledStates, TestListScheduledTool) use only a single actor (sub-A). TestRecallWindowGate does insert a sub-B shared+scheduled record (ID a0000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000005) and verifies it stays hidden from Search/List, but makes no call to ListScheduled at all for that record.

What's missing:
1. A test confirming actor B's private scheduled records do NOT appear in actor A's list_scheduled (isolation).
2. A test pinning whether actor B's shared+scheduled records appear in actor A's list_scheduled — and if they do, confirming that is intentional rather than an accidental over-share.

File: internal/store/store.go:597-600 (ListScheduled filter construction)
File: internal/store/store_test.go TestListScheduledStates, TestRecallWindowGate

Suggested test: Add a sub-B private + a sub-B shared scheduled record to the same scope, then call ListScheduled as sub-A and assert sub-B's private record is absent. The shared record's presence/absence should be an explicit assertion, not silence.
close_reason: Fixed: ListScheduled now owner-only (ownerOnlyCondition); shared+scheduled records no longer leak cross-actor. TestListScheduledOwnerIsolation added. Verified APPROVE.

title: PruneExpired Count-then-Delete TOCTOU yields wrong reported deletion count
description:
internal/store/store.go PruneExpired (around line 962): the function issues a Qdrant Count call to capture the pre-delete count, then a separate Delete call with the same filter. Between these two Qdrant RPCs, new records matching the filter could be inserted (or records could be deleted by a concurrent prune). The 'n' returned (and printed by the CLI as 'pruned %d expired records') reflects the count at the time of Count, not the records actually deleted by Delete.

This is observable: if two prune-expired processes run concurrently, both will Count the same set and one will Delete them; the other will report N deleted but actually delete 0. Similarly, records matching the filter inserted between Count and Delete will be deleted but not counted.

The spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-scheduled-memories-design.md line 194-200) notes this design: 'The CLI computes before = s.now() − grace and reports the deleted count.' Qdrant's DeletePoints response does not carry a count, so an exact count requires the Count+Delete pattern. The TOCTOU is inherent, but the code should document this limitation explicitly and ideally note that the count is an approximation (not a guarantee).

Recommended fix: add a comment in PruneExpired documenting that the count is a pre-delete approximation and may differ from actual deletions under concurrent access, so operators know not to treat it as an audit-quality figure. If exact counts become important, Scroll+Delete-by-IDs would eliminate the race at higher cost.
close_reason: Fixed: PruneExpired count documented as best-effort under concurrency (godoc + CLI '~N best-effort count'); delete filter unchanged/exact.

title: ListScheduled leaks other owners' shared-but-hidden windowed records
description:
internal/store/store.go ListScheduled (line 597+): The filter uses ownerOrSharedCondition, which for authenticated callers matches 'owner==sub OR visibility==shared'. This means caller sub-A calling list_scheduled can enumerate records where visibility=="shared" AND (state is scheduled or expired) owned by other actors. The design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-12-scheduled-memories-design.md line 156) explicitly calls list_scheduled 'The owner's management view of their windowed memories' and spec testing section (line 219) says it should 'never leak another owner's records.'

The active-recall gate (Search/List) correctly hides scheduled shared records from all callers until active. But list_scheduled uses the inverse gate — it shows records the recall gate hides. With ownerOrSharedCondition, sub-A sees sub-B's shared records that are scheduled or expired, which sub-B has not yet made visible. This is an isolation breach in the management view.

Fix: replace ownerOrSharedCondition with a strict owner-only filter in ListScheduled's Must clause:
  qdrant.NewMatch("owner", ownerOf(subj))
There is no legitimate reason for list_scheduled to surface another owner's hidden records; shared readability applies to active records only.
close_reason: Fixed: ListScheduled now owner-only (ownerOnlyCondition); shared+scheduled records no longer leak cross-actor. TestListScheduledOwnerIsolation added. Verified APPROVE.

title: search and discovery routes lack Resizable framing — MemoryDetail hardcoded width not responsive
description: The spec (design doc §Shell & navigation) requires List and Detail panes to use shadcn Resizable PaneGroup. The plan Task 10 Step 2 says search/discovery should 'mirror the observe wiring.' However, both ui/src/routes/search/+page.svelte (line 22) and ui/src/routes/discovery/+page.svelte (line 21) use a flat <div class="flex"> wrapper without any Resizable.PaneGroup. MemoryDetail has a hardcoded w-[360px] shrink-0 root div (MemoryDetail.svelte:17), so when rendered in these two routes the detail pane is always 360px with no user-resizable handle — the same non-responsive behaviour identified as bug #6 in the requirements inventory. Only the observe route correctly wraps MemoryDetail in Resizable.Pane. Fix: wrap the list + detail sections in search/+page.svelte and discovery/+page.svelte with Resizable.PaneGroup / Resizable.Pane / Resizable.Handle, mirroring the observe layout, and remove or make the w-[360px] conditional on not being inside a Resizable pane (or rely entirely on Resizable.Pane sizing).
close_reason: Wrapped search + discovery routes in Resizable.PaneGroup (list | detail) matching observe; responsive framing restored

title: CommandPalette: onsearch and onnavigate callbacks have no test coverage
description:
CommandPalette.test.ts contains exactly one assertion: that the search input is visible when open=true. The component's entire production contract — onsearch(q) fires when the user selects the search item, onnavigate(href) fires when a Go-To item is selected, and the palette closes after either action — has zero test coverage.

File: ui/src/lib/components/CommandPalette.test.ts (new file, PR adds this)
Source: ui/src/lib/components/CommandPalette.svelte lines 14–18

The onsearch/onnavigate paths are the only observable outputs of this component. A refactor that accidentally breaks the callback (e.g. swaps onsearch and onnavigate, or fails to close the palette) passes the suite with no signal. Suggested additions:
- Render with open=true, fireEvent.click or userEvent on the 'Search memories for...' Command.Item, assert onsearch was called with the correct query and open becomes false.
- Render, select an 'Observe' Go-To item, assert onnavigate was called with the expected href.
- Optionally: render with open=false, assert the input is not in the document.
close_reason: Added CommandPalette tests exercising onsearch + onnavigate callbacks (via option role)

title: Fix scope-rail overflow/overlap + Button nowrap leak (broken-looking rendering)
description: The left scope rail shows garbled, overlapping text on real data. Root cause: ScopeRail.svelte:41 renders {s.scope} with NO min-w-0/truncate, so long scope names (e.g. repo:github.com/fzymgc-house/selfhosted-cluster, discovery:repo:*) overflow the 210px rail and collide with the {s.count} span (line 42). Compounded by the shared Button base (ui/button/button.svelte:6) carrying 'inline-flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap', which leaks into the multi-line block rows used by ScopeRail AND MemoryList and fights the intended stacked layout. Fix: add min-w-0 + truncate (and a title attr) to the scope-name span; ensure the block/size=block button usages drop whitespace-nowrap/items-center so multi-line rows lay out cleanly. Acceptance: long scope names ellipsize within the rail, count stays aligned, no overlap; list rows stack without nowrap clipping. Add a component test (ScopeRail) asserting truncate class / no overflow on a long scope.
close_reason: Superseded by the plan task breakdown (engram-kco.8-.18)

title: No test for reserved-path collision (MEM_MCP_PATH=/ui/) that panics the mux at startup
description: resolveMCPPath accepts /ui/ (passes the leading-slash check), so mountMCPRoutes calls mux.Handle("/ui/", mcpHandler) after the console SPA is already registered at that pattern. Go 1.22+ (this repo: go 1.26.3) panics on duplicate ServeMux registrations, crashing the server at startup with no user-friendly message. The test suite (TestResolveMCPPath, TestMountMCPRoutes) has no case covering a path that collides with a reserved prefix (/ui/, /auth/). A test case in TestResolveMCPPath asserting that /ui/ (and /auth/) returns an error — once the sibling code finding adds reserved-prefix validation to resolveMCPPath — would catch this regression. Without it, the validation and the test coverage gap are both open. File: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/feat-mcp-path-orm/cmd/engram/mcproute_test.go (missing case), mcproute.go:20-28 (resolveMCPPath), serve.go:164-171 (UI mux registrations happen before mountMCPRoutes at line 190).
close_reason: Fixed: added reserved-path test cases to TestResolveMCPPath (/ui, /ui/, /auth/login, Connect path -> error; /uimcp lookalike allowed). RED->GREEN.

title: docs-site quickstart.md and deploy.md still claim MCP is served at the root with no path prefix
description:
Two public docs-site pages carry statements that directly contradict the new default after this PR merges.

docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/quickstart.md line 35:
  'The MCP endpoint is served at the **root** — http://localhost:8080 — with no path prefix.'

docs-site/src/content/docs/guides/deploy.md line 66:
  'The MCP endpoint is served at the root (http://host:8080), with no path prefix.'

Both statements are false after this PR. The default MCP transport is now /mcp.
A user who follows either page and registers http://localhost:8080 (or http://host:8080) as the engram MCP server URL will get a 404 instead of the MCP transport.

Fix: update both pages to state the new default endpoint is http://host:8080/mcp, and note MEM_MCP_PATH=/ as the legacy escape hatch.
close_reason: Fixed: quickstart.md + deploy.md updated to state the MCP endpoint defaults to /mcp, with MEM_MCP_PATH=/ as the legacy escape hatch.

title: UI console blank: //go:embed static excludes _app/* (SvelteKit assets 404)
description:
GH #106. The operator console at /ui serves index.html (200) but every /ui/_app/immutable/* asset 404s, so the SvelteKit SPA never mounts (blank page). Affects every released image (confirmed 0.6.1) and a local build of main.

ROOT CAUSE (empirically confirmed): internal/webauth/static.go line 14 uses a bare directory pattern:

    //go:embed static

Go's embed spec excludes files/dirs whose names begin with '_' or '.' when a *directory* is named. SvelteKit emits its entire build under static/_app/, so only static/index.html is compiled into the embed.FS; static/_app/immutable/* is silently dropped. Verified: walking the compiled staticFS yields exactly [index.html]; fs.Stat for _app/immutable/entry/start.*.js returns 'file does not exist'. The files ARE on disk and ARE git-tracked (incl. at v0.6.1) — they're just never embedded.

NOT the cause: the StripPrefix(/ui/) mount in serve.go:167 and the StaticHandler fs.Sub/handler logic are both correct (this refutes the fs.Sub-layout hypothesis in the issue comment).

FIX (one line): //go:embed static -> //go:embed all:static  (the 'all:' prefix overrides the _/. exclusion).

REGRESSION TEST: internal/webauth/static_test.go currently only asserts index.html + SPA fallback, which is why CI stayed green. Add a test that fs.Stat / GETs a real hashed _app/immutable asset through StaticHandler so an empty/underscore-excluded embed fails loudly.

ACCEPTANCE:
- //go:embed all:static in static.go
- new test fails on bare 'static' pattern, passes with 'all:static'
- GET /ui/_app/immutable/entry/start.*.js returns 200 with correct content-type
- existing static_test.go tests still pass
notes:
GH #106; refutes the fs.Sub hypothesis in the issue's own comment.
Root cause (confirmed via systematic-debugging): internal/webauth/static.go used a bare '//go:embed static' directive. Go's embed spec excludes files/dirs whose names begin with '_' or '.' when a directory is named, so the entire SvelteKit build under static/_app/ was dropped at compile time — staticFS contained only index.html. Handler/StripPrefix/fs.Sub were all correct (refutes the fs.Sub hypothesis). Secondary causes ruled out: no hash mismatch, 19 tracked == 19 on-disk (no partial commit), no junk/dotfiles (so all: is safe). Broken since #79 — affects every released image.

Fix: //go:embed static -> //go:embed all:static (TDD). Added TestStaticHandlerServesAppAssets which walks the compiled staticFS for an _app/immutable/*.js asset (no hardcoded hash), requires >=1 (RED on bare pattern), and serves it through StaticHandler asserting 200 + javascript content-type; also anchors on the stable _app/version.json. Verified: RED before / GREEN after; go test ./... exit 0 (7 pkgs); gofmt/vet/build clean; golangci-lint 0 issues; license-eye 0 invalid. Left in_progress for merge.
PR #109 opened (branch fix-ui-embed-106). Running /review-pr gate.
Review gate PASS (epic engram-gew, turn 1): code/tests/comments/simplify/slop = 0 findings; security = 1 suggestion (pre-existing cookie@0.6.0 Dependabot alert, out of scope) graduated to standalone follow-up engram-bxc. No critical/important. PR #109 ready to merge.
CI: initial 'test' job failed on a Qdrant infra flake (internal/store integration tests, 'connection reset by peer' — package untouched by this diff). Re-run went green with no code change, confirming the flake. PR #109 mergeStateStatus=CLEAN, all required checks pass. Bead left in_progress; closes at merge.
close_reason: Merged in fix-ui-embed-106 via PR #109

title: docs: 'Two auth lanes' overstates MCP bearer lane audience enforcement
description:
File: docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/auth.md, new section 'Two auth lanes: agents vs. web console'

The new introductory sentence reads:

  'engram authenticates over two independent lanes, each verifying issuer, audience, and signature on its own'

This is inaccurate for the MCP bearer lane. The audience check on that lane is OPTIONAL — it fires only when MEM_OIDC_AUDIENCE is set. The internal/auth/auth.go package doc says explicitly: 'the audience claim is checked only when an expected value is configured.' Signature, issuer, and expiry are always enforced; audience is not.

The web console lane does always pin audience to the client ID (via oidc.Config{ClientID: clientID}), but the sentence describes both lanes together and is wrong for the MCP lane.

Suggested fix — replace the sentence with:

  'engram authenticates over two independent lanes. Each verifies issuer, signature, and token expiry; audience enforcement differs by lane (see table below).'

Or, retain the compact form but qualify:

  'engram authenticates over two independent lanes, each verifying issuer, signature, and expiry on its own (the MCP bearer lane also checks audience when MEM_OIDC_AUDIENCE is set):'

This matters because the docs are the operator's primary reference for understanding the security model. Overstating enforcement could lead an operator to believe the server rejects tokens from unexpected audiences when it does not (if MEM_OIDC_AUDIENCE is unset).
close_reason: Fixed: docs-site auth.md reworded — audience now 'checked only when MEM_OIDC_AUDIENCE is set'; matches auth.go SkipClientIDCheck. Verified RESOLVED by turn-2 comment re-review.

title: Design spec (2026-06-09-engram-web-ui-design.md) config surface not updated to include MEM_UI_ISSUER
description:
The PR adds MEM_UI_ISSUER / --ui-issuer and documents it in docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/auth.md, but does not update the design-of-record spec at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-engram-web-ui-design.md.

Two specific places in that spec are now stale:

1. Auth model section (around line 320): 'authorization-code flow with PKCE against the same issuer' — this is no longer necessarily true; MEM_UI_ISSUER decouples the UI lane from MEM_OIDC_ISSUER.

2. Config surface table (around line 346): lists only 5 variables (MEM_UI_ENABLED, MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, MEM_UI_REDIRECT_URL, MEM_UI_COOKIE_KEY). MEM_UI_ISSUER is absent.

AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md both treat docs/superpowers/specs/ as design-of-record for ADR-level decisions. The connect-auth-posture-addendum explicitly cross-references this spec as the 'design-reviewer-approved web-UI spec'. Leaving the canonical spec stale while the docs-site reference is updated creates an inconsistency for future reviewers and plan-reviewers who use it as an acceptance criterion source.

Suggested fix: Update docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-engram-web-ui-design.md:
- Auth model: amend the 'same issuer' phrase to 'its own issuer (MEM_UI_ISSUER, defaulting to MEM_OIDC_ISSUER)'
- Config surface table: add a row for MEM_UI_ISSUER with purpose 'Console OIDC issuer — empty defaults to MEM_OIDC_ISSUER (single-app deployments need nothing here)'
close_reason: Fixed: spec 2026-06-09-engram-web-ui-design.md gained MEM_UI_ISSUER config row + dated #101 amendment on the 'same issuer' bullet (dated-record convention). Verified RESOLVED by turn-2 spec re-review.

title: Inline comment misattributes slog.Warn handler — span-context framing omits the real concern
description:
File: /internal/telemetry/providers.go, lines 149-151 (added in PR #103)

The inline comment reads:
  // Startup path, outside any span — plain slog (no *Context variant) is
  // correct here (see logger.go traceContextHandler convention).

The justification it offers — that omitting the Context variant is correct because there is no span — is accurate as far as it goes, but it frames the wrong question as the decisive one. The materially more important fact is which *handler* slog.Warn dispatches to at this call site.

Call chain at startup:
  serve.go:79  → telemetry.Setup(...)      // builds providers, calls buildResource
  serve.go:83  → slog.SetDefault(logger)   // installs the configured JSON/text logger

slog.Warn at providers.go:151 executes inside telemetry.Setup, which returns before slog.SetDefault runs. Therefore the warn goes to Go's default handler (the log-package-backed default slog logger), not the application's configured JSON/text/fanout handler. This means:
- The warning may be formatted differently from every other log line.
- If the operator has set MEM_LOG_FORMAT=json for structured log ingestion, this one diagnostic line is emitted in plain text and will not be parsed.
- The comment gives a reader the false impression that the logger.go traceContextHandler analysis fully justifies the choice, when the handler-identity issue is unaddressed.

Suggested fix: Either pass the logger down so the correct handler is used (architecturally cleaner), or amend the comment to acknowledge the default-handler limitation, e.g.:
  // Startup path: slog.SetDefault has not run yet, so this goes to the
  // Go default handler. No span is present either, so no *Context variant.
  // See logger.go for the traceContextHandler convention used post-setup.

Severity: important — the comment actively misleads future readers about correctness and will cause confusion when someone investigates why partial-resource warnings appear in a different format in production logs.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #103: inline comment rewritten to state the actual concern — lg is the bootstrap stdout logger and slog.SetDefault has not run at telemetry.Setup time, so a bare slog.Warn would bypass MEM_LOG_LEVEL/FORMAT. Resolved together with engram-1id.1 (same root).

title: resourceFromOptions WARN uses global slog before SetDefault; bypasses configured level, format, and OTLP sink
description:
File: internal/telemetry/providers.go, resourceFromOptions (lines 147-156)

The WARN emitted when a detector fails uses the package-level slog.Warn() call. In cmd/engram/serve.go, slog.SetDefault(logger) is called at line 83, AFTER telemetry.Setup() returns at line 79. This means the WARN fires against Go's runtime default handler — text to stderr at INFO threshold — regardless of MEM_LOG_LEVEL, MEM_LOG_FORMAT, or whether OTLP log export is configured.

Consequences:
1. The comment says 'plain slog (no *Context variant) is correct here' — that reasoning addresses trace context only, not sink/format/level. The WARN is always emitted to stderr in text format, even when the operator has configured JSON-only or a higher log level.
2. The slog.Warn call is the only operator signal for a partial-resource degradation. If an operator runs with MEM_LOG_STDOUT=false and expects all logs in OTLP, this warning is still dropped from OTLP and appears on stderr in text format — inconsistent with the rest of startup logging.
3. Not suppressible by MEM_LOG_LEVEL=error, because the global handler has not yet been replaced.

The comment in resourceFromOptions acknowledges the startup context, but does not acknowledge these sink/level discrepancies.

Suggested fix: Accept a *slog.Logger parameter in resourceFromOptions (and thread it from buildProviders, which receives cfg but constructs no logger). Alternatively, since Setup has access to the cfg, pre-build a bootstrap logger before calling buildProvidersFn and pass it down. A simpler approach: move the slog.Warn to the caller (buildProviders) after construction, using the same pattern — but buildProviders also has no logger; the cleanest fix is that buildProviders returns the error message alongside the resource and Setup (which does build the logger) emits the WARN on the configured logger.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #103: resourceFromOptions now logs via a threaded bootstrap logger (NewLogger(cfg,nil)) passed from buildProviders, honouring MEM_LOG_LEVEL/FORMAT on the stdout channel instead of the pre-SetDefault global slog default. Regression test TestResourceFromOptionsLogsPartialViaProvidedLogger asserts the warning routes through the provided logger.

title: 0.6.0: OTLP telemetry fully disabled on distroless — host.id ErrPartialResource treated as fatal
description:
GitHub issue #102 (https://github.com/seanb4t/engram/issues/102), filed by @seanb4t after verifying the 0.6.0 rollout in the fzymgc-house cluster.

PROBLEM
On the shipped distroless image, v0.6.0 disables ALL OTLP export at startup and silently falls back to stdout-only logging. distroless has no /etc/machine-id, so resource.WithHostID() cannot resolve host.id; resource.New returns a usable partial resource together with the non-fatal sentinel resource.ErrPartialResource. Engram treats that as fatal, dropping the entire OTLP provider stack (traces + metrics). Logs survive via the independent stdout slog path, which masked the regression. Every stock deployment loses OTLP export on 0.6.0 — not environment-specific. Regression of the #88 telemetry work.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed on main @42178a9)
- internal/telemetry/providers.go:114 buildResource returns resource.New(...)'s error verbatim; detector set includes resource.WithHostID().
- internal/telemetry/providers.go:37-40 buildProviders returns early on ANY non-nil buildResource error.
- internal/telemetry/telemetry.go:39-45 Setup treats any buildProvidersFn error as full fallback to stdout (NewLogger(cfg,nil)), dropping lp/shutdown.

SUGGESTED FIX
Tolerate non-fatal resource errors in buildResource (use the returned partial resource; only treat OTHER errors as fatal):

  res, err := resource.New(ctx, /* detectors */)
  if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, resource.ErrPartialResource) && !errors.Is(err, resource.ErrSchemaURLConflict) {
      return nil, err
  }
  return res, nil // res is non-nil and usable even on ErrPartialResource

Tolerating ErrPartialResource is preferred over dropping WithHostID() because it also covers partial failures of WithHost/WithContainer/WithOS in other minimal-base/restricted environments. Add a regression test (table case) asserting buildResource returns a usable resource when a detector partially fails; providers_test.go already exercises buildResource.

IMPACT / RELEASE
Shipped image is distroless, so all stock 0.6.0 deployments lose metrics+traces. Worth a patch release (0.6.1) given #88 was the headline telemetry feature.

ENVIRONMENT
engram 0.6.0, ghcr.io/seanb4t/engram:0.6.0 (distroless), linux/arm64; Kubernetes; Helm chart oci://ghcr.io/seanb4t/charts/engram 0.6.0; observability.otlpEndpoint set (in-cluster OTLP/gRPC) + secret-backed headers.
acceptance_criteria: buildResource tolerates resource.ErrPartialResource (and ErrSchemaURLConflict), returning the usable partial resource; OTLP trace+metric+log providers initialize on the distroless image with no /etc/machine-id; regression test covers a partial-detector-failure case; verified on a distroless deployment that the collector receives traces and metrics.
notes:
Root-cause confirmed against OTel SDK v1.44.0 source — and it FALSIFIES the suggested fix. hostIDDetector.Detect (host_id.go) returns a PLAIN errors.New('host id not found in: /etc/machine-id...'), NOT wrapped in resource.ErrPartialResource. The observed log 'error detecting resource: host id not found...' is that plain error wrapped only by detect()'s fmt.Errorf. So the bead's proposed guard !errors.Is(err, ErrPartialResource) is FALSE for the host.id case and would NOT fix it. (WithFromEnv DOES wrap its partial in the sentinel per env.go:27, but WithHostID does not.) Correct fix: resource.New ALWAYS returns a non-nil usable Resource (detect() in auto.go merges every successful detector and continues past the failed one), so resource detection is best-effort metadata that must never disable export (ADR engram-uxh). Fix = buildResource tolerates ALL detection errors (log at WARN + use the partial resource), and buildProviders drops its fatal 'return nil,nil,err' on resource error. Implementing via a testable resourceFromOptions seam + injected-failing-detector regression test.
FIX IMPLEMENTED (TDD, workspace fix-otlp-partial-resource off main@0.6.0). Root cause: resource detection failures were propagated as fatal — buildProviders did 'return nil,nil,err' on any buildResource error, and Setup then dropped the whole OTLP stack to stdout. The distroless trigger is WithHostID returning a PLAIN error (NOT ErrPartialResource), so the originally-suggested errors.Is guard would not have caught it.

Fix: resource detection is best-effort metadata that must never disable export (ADR engram-uxh). Added resourceFromOptions(ctx, opts...) seam in internal/telemetry/providers.go: wraps resource.New, logs ANY detection error at WARN ('partial telemetry resource; exporting with detected attributes'), and returns the always-non-nil partial resource (defensive resource.Empty() fallback). buildResource now returns *resource.Resource (no error) and delegates through it; buildProviders dropped its fatal error branch. Keeps host.id where available (VMs/baremetal), non-fatal where absent (distroless/k8s).

Regression test TestResourceFromOptionsToleratesDetectorFailure (providers_test.go) injects a failing detector via resource.WithDetectors — table covers the plain host.id-style error AND the ErrPartialResource-wrapped case — asserting the resource is non-nil and surviving attributes (service.name) are retained. Existing TestBuildResourceHasStandardAttributes updated to the new signature.

Gates (all green, evidence shown): go test ./internal/telemetry ok; go vet clean; gofmt -l clean; golangci-lint 0 issues; go build ./... ok; task license:check 0 invalid.
Review round 1 on PR #103 (epic engram-1id, PASS): code/security/slop clean; errors found the WARN routing regression (engram-1id.1 important) + comment (engram-1id.5 important). Fixed by threading a bootstrap logger NewLogger(cfg,nil) from buildProviders → buildResource → resourceFromOptions and logging through it (honours MEM_LOG_LEVEL/FORMAT; the original fatal path also used NewLogger so this restores parity); rewrote the inline comment; removed the dead nil guard (engram-1id.4). Added TestResourceFromOptionsLogsPartialViaProvidedLogger. 2 suggestions declined with rationale (engram-1id.2 err string already names detector; engram-1id.3 buildProviders partial-injection needs a seam not worth adding). Review fixes squashed into the PR commit (change lwzxlkon); re-pushed. Bead stays in_progress until merge.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #103 (squash). Closes #102.

title: InitLayerMetrics: 'nil instrument from the no-op provider' is factually wrong
description:
File: internal/telemetry/metrics.go, added lines (InitLayerMetrics doc comment)

The comment reads: "Instrument-creation errors are ignored: a nil instrument from the no-op provider still records safely."

This is factually wrong on two counts:

1. The no-op meter (metric/noop package) returns noop.Float64Histogram{} — a zero-value struct that satisfies the metric.Float64Histogram interface. It is NOT a nil interface value. Calling .Record() on a nil metric.Float64Histogram interface would panic; the noop struct is safe because it implements Record as a no-op method, not because nil is safe.

2. The real SDK meter (sdk/metric, meter.go lookupHistogram) always returns a non-nil *float64Inst even on error (return &float64Inst{measures: aggs}, err). So the 'nil instrument' case from an SDK meter also doesn't arise.

The comment misleads future readers into believing nil interface values are safe to call (they are not — that would be a nil-pointer dereference). It also copies the identical wording from the pre-existing NewToolMetrics doc comment (metrics.go line 21-23), which has the same inaccuracy.

Fix: Replace 'a nil instrument from the no-op provider still records safely' with an accurate explanation, e.g.: 'errors are only possible on invalid (duplicate-name/incompatible) instruments; the returned instrument is always a valid no-op or SDK type and safe to call regardless.' Or, more concisely: 'instrument creation errors are non-fatal; the SDK always returns a usable (possibly empty) instrument.'

Evidence: sdk@v1.44.0/resource/noop/noop.go line 126, 242; sdk/metric@v1.44.0/meter.go line 785.
notes: Downgraded important->suggestion: the CODE is safe (the OTel no-op provider returns a non-nil no-op Float64Histogram, never a nil interface; the real SDK also never returns nil), so no panic is reachable. Only the comment's phrasing ('nil instrument ... records safely') is imprecise. Doc-accuracy nit, not a correctness bug.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: store.SetVisibility and store.Delete: named-return err shadowed by if-init; deferred telemetry records errors as ok
close_reason: FALSE POSITIVE — empirically refuted: forced SetVisibility's getWritable-failure path, span status correctly = Error. 'return err' assigns the named result param before deferred closures run (Go spec), regardless of the if-init ':=' shadow. Same misread as the embed Task-3 false-positive.

title: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is now unconditional in Helm template, injecting k8s identity even when OTEL is disabled
description:
File: charts/engram/templates/memory-mcp.yaml, lines 9-32 (diff context)

BEFORE:
  {{- with .Values.observability.resourceAttributes }}
  - { name: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, value: "{{ . }}" }
  {{- end }}
  (env var only injected when resourceAttributes is non-empty AND otlpEndpoint is set — the with-block is implicitly inside the otlpEndpoint conditional chain)

AFTER:
  - name: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES
    value: "k8s.pod.name=,...{{ with .Values.observability.resourceAttributes }},{{ . }}{{ end }}"
  (ALWAYS injected, unconditionally — no guard on otlpEndpoint or any other gate)
  Plus 4 Downward API env vars (POD_NAME, POD_NAMESPACE, NODE_NAME, POD_UID) always injected.

Two behavioral changes for existing Helm users:

1. Users with otlpEndpoint UNSET (pure log-only deployments, the common dev/test case) previously had no OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES in the container. Now they always get it, populated with k8s pod identity. The Go binary uses resource.WithFromEnv() so it will pick this up and attach k8s identity to all OTel resources even with no OTLP endpoint configured. This is harmless if the no-op provider is used, but the env var is visible to the process and any tooling that reads it.

2. The 4 Downward API vars are also injected unconditionally on every pod regardless of observability configuration. This is a gratuitous env-var addition for non-observability deployments.

Suggested fix: wrap the OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES block (and the 4 Downward API vars) in the same {{- if .Values.observability.otlpEndpoint }} guard used by the other OTEL env vars:

  {{- if .Values.observability.otlpEndpoint }}
  - name: POD_NAME
    valueFrom: { fieldRef: { fieldPath: metadata.name } }
  ... (other downward API vars)
  - name: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES
    value: "k8s.pod.name=,...{{ with .Values.observability.resourceAttributes }},{{ . }}{{ end }}"
  {{- end }}

This restores the invariant that OTEL env vars only appear when an OTLP endpoint is configured, matching the pattern used for OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL added in the same PR.
notes: Downgraded important->suggestion: this is the plan's deliberate design (Task 7 / ADR engram-9tj) — pod identity belongs to the OTel resource independent of trace/metric export ('same image works on laptop/Docker/k8s'). The 4 POD_* + OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env are inert Downward-API metadata when telemetry is off (no secrets, no binary behavior change). Optionally gating behind otlpEndpoint is a refinement, not a defect.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: var layer *layerMetrics is written and read without synchronization
description: internal/telemetry/metrics.go:57 — var layer *layerMetrics is written once by InitLayerMetrics (cmd/engram/serve.go:96) and read concurrently by RecordStoreOp/RecordEmbed/RecordAuthVerify from request-handling goroutines. In production the write precedes http.ListenAndServe, so the goroutine-creation happen-before edge makes this safe at runtime. However the Go race detector will flag it: the detector tracks individual memory accesses, not goroutine-creation edges, so any test that calls InitLayerMetrics and a Record* helper from overlapping goroutines (or re-runs t.Cleanup layer=nil while another test is mid-record) will produce a data race report. The t.Cleanup(func() { layer = nil }) in metrics_test.go:136 is exactly such a site if tests ever run in parallel. Fix: replace var layer *layerMetrics with var layer atomic.Pointer[layerMetrics]; call layer.Store(lm) in InitLayerMetrics and lm := layer.Load() in each Record* helper; guards remain the same (nil load = disabled). No API change needed. This also eliminates the silent re-entrancy hazard: a second InitLayerMetrics call races with in-flight Record* reads; an atomic store is still not idempotent but at least the pointer swap is race-free.
notes: Downgraded important->suggestion: not CI-blocking (Taskfile/CI run 'go test ./...' with NO -race); production-safe via server-startup happen-before (InitLayerMetrics runs before any request goroutine); matches the pre-existing NewToolMetrics package-global pattern. atomic.Pointer[layerMetrics] is a valid hardening follow-up, not a merge blocker.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: store.SetVisibility and store.Delete: inner-scope err shadows named return, leaving span and metric in wrong state on getWritable failure
description:
In internal/store/store.go, both SetVisibility and Delete use a short-variable declaration inside the guard:

  if _, err := s.getWritable(ctx, id, subj); err != nil {
      return err
  }

The `err :=` creates a new variable scoped to the `if` block. The outer named return `err` (which the deferred telemetry closure captures) remains nil. When getWritable fails, the caller still receives the correct error via the explicit return, but:
- span.RecordError and span.SetStatus(codes.Error, ...) are never called
- RecordStoreOp records outcome="ok" instead of outcome="error"

This means every ownership-check failure on Delete and SetVisibility is invisible in traces and metrics.

Affected locations:
- SetVisibility: line ~741 (the if _, err := s.getWritable guard before the SetPayload call)
- Delete: line ~770 (the if _, err := s.getWritable guard before the client.Delete call)

Fix: replace `err :=` with assignment to the named return:
  var m Memory
  m, err = s.getWritable(ctx, id, subj)
  if err != nil {
      return err
  }
(or use a dummy discard for the Memory return and assign err directly)
close_reason: FALSE POSITIVE — empirically refuted: forced SetVisibility's getWritable-failure path, span status correctly = Error. 'return err' assigns the named result param before deferred closures run (Go spec), regardless of the if-init ':=' shadow. Same misread as the embed Task-3 false-positive.

title: client.ts: 'credentials default' implies a transport config option that does not exist
close_reason: client.ts comment corrected: cookies via fetch same-origin credentials default, not a transport option.

title: Discovery route missing MemoryDetail pane required by three-pane shell spec
description:
The spec (§Components and views, Discovery row) states: 'same shell over discovery:* scope → SearchDiscoveries; surfaces kind, summary, citations'. 'Same shell' refers to the three-pane Observe shell defined as the single layout primitive for all views.

The Search route correctly implements MemoryList + MemoryDetail panes side-by-side. The Discovery route (ui/src/routes/discovery/+page.svelte) renders only MemoryList (line 20) with no MemoryDetail pane alongside it. A user can never click a discovery record and see its detail (kind, summary, citations) in the right pane.

Affected file: ui/src/routes/discovery/+page.svelte (line 20 — no MemoryDetail component).
close_reason: Discovery route now three-pane: getMemory(sel) detailQ + MemoryDetail pane + select handler.

title: Dashboard route omits required recent-memories list (ListMemories call)
description:
The spec (§Components and views, Dashboard row) requires the Dashboard to render: 'per-scope tiles ... + a recent list (ListMemories(scope, limit=N), store-sorted CreatedAt desc)'.

The implemented ui/src/routes/+page.svelte calls only engram.listScopes({}) and renders scope tiles. There is no ListMemories call and no recent-memories list component. The second half of the Dashboard requirement is entirely absent.

The spec intent is clear: clicking a scope tile is the drill-in path, but the dashboard itself should also show a recent-records list below the tiles so operators get immediate context on landing.

Affected file: ui/src/routes/+page.svelte (lines 1-27).
close_reason: Dashboard now renders a recent-memories MemoryList (ListMemories first page) below scope tiles.

title: TS: 'next page' button in observe/+page.svelte is never disabled, allowing infinite pagination past total
close_reason: Duplicate of engram-af5.12 (observe 'next' pager has no upper-bound guard).

title: observe/+page.svelte: 'next' pagination button has no upper-bound guard and lacks test coverage
description:
ui/src/routes/observe/+page.svelte line 4167 (diff):

  <button onclick={() => navigate({ offset: params.offset + PAGE_LIMIT })}>next ›</button>

There is no guard preventing offset from advancing past `total`. When the user is on the last page and clicks 'next', the offset becomes `total` or greater. The server correctly returns an empty page (the store clamps at offset>=total), but the UI advances silently to an empty state with no indication that the user is at the end, and the 'prev' button still works (bringing them back). However, there is no maximum offset cap, so repeated clicks accumulate offset unboundedly.

More critically: this logic has zero test coverage. The observe route page is entirely untested. A regression (e.g. offset going negative, or the disable condition on 'prev' changing) would be invisible.

The test `TestListMemoriesHandlerPagesAndIsolates` in connectapi_test.go only exercises a single category-filter call; it never exercises pagination at the handler layer (no offset parameter is passed).

Suggested fixes:
1. Add an upper bound: disable 'next ›' when params.offset + PAGE_LIMIT >= (listQ.data?.total ?? 0n). This requires casting correctly between bigint and number.
2. Add at least one unit test for the observe page's pagination navigation logic (or extract the disable condition into a pure function in queries.ts and test that).
close_reason: observe 'next' disabled when offset+PAGE_LIMIT>=total.

title: SearchPalette.test.ts: onsubmit assertion is likely tautological due to Svelte 5 state + jsdom
description:
ui/src/lib/components/SearchPalette.test.ts lines 3536-3541 (diff):

The test does:
  fireEvent.input(input, { target: { value: 'ci gate' } })
  fireEvent.keyDown(input, { key: 'Enter' })
  expect(onsubmit).toHaveBeenCalledWith('ci gate')

SearchPalette.svelte uses Svelte 5 `$state`: `let q = $state(value)`. In jsdom with @testing-library/svelte, fireEvent.input does NOT update Svelte 5 reactive state the same way it updates a DOM input's .value; the component's reactive `q` variable remains at its initial value ('').  When Enter fires, onkey calls onsubmit(q) where q is still ''.

The test asserts toHaveBeenCalledWith('ci gate') but because mock.calls is checked, if the assertion framework is lenient or the call does happen with '', the test either fails outright (good) or passes vacuously if the mock is called first with '' and the assertion accidentally matches a different call.

More precisely: the test is asserting the mock was called with a specific value that the component's reactive state cannot produce via fireEvent.input in this environment. If the test currently passes, it is because onsubmit is called but with the wrong argument, and the assertion is incorrectly satisfied (or the test is silently skipped).

Suggested fix: use userEvent from @testing-library/user-event which properly triggers Svelte 5 reactive state updates, OR switch to svelte's own tick() + writable store pattern, OR assert toHaveBeenCalled() without argument if the contract being tested is only 'submit fires on Enter' (and move the value-propagation assertion to a separate test using the correct API).
close_reason: SearchPalette.test.ts rewritten with user-event to drive Svelte 5 bind:value; asserts onsubmit('ci gate'); fails-on-broken/passes-on-correct verified.

title: scopesQ error in observe/+page.svelte is silently swallowed — empty rail is indistinguishable from no-scopes
description:
ui/src/routes/observe/+page.svelte: The scopesQ (listScopes) result is passed to ScopeRail as scopes={$scopesQ.data?.scopes ?? []}. There is no {#if $scopesQ.error} branch in the template. When the request fails with CodeInternal, a network error, or any non-Unauthenticated error (which the layout onError handler does not redirect for), the scope rail renders as empty. The user cannot distinguish 'no scopes exist' from 'the backend call failed'. Because retry is disabled globally (retry:false) and there is no visible error state, the failure is permanent for that page load with zero user feedback. Suggested fix: add an error branch in the ScopeRail area — e.g. {#if $scopesQ.error}
failed to load scopes
{/if} — and/or disable the list/detail queries while scopesQ is in error.
close_reason: ScopeRail gained loading/error props; observe surfaces scopesQ.error as distinct 'failed to load scopes' state.

title: QueryCache.onError silently drops non-Unauthenticated errors with no logging or fallback
description: ui/src/routes/+layout.svelte lines 36-39: The QueryCache onError handler calls mapAuthError and, if it returns null (any non-Unauthenticated error — CodeInternal, CodeUnavailable, network failure, etc.), silently returns without logging, alerting, or storing the error anywhere. The per-page MemoryList/MemoryDetail components do propagate $q.error to a visible banner for the queries that are currently coded, but the layout-level handler is the intended global catch-point and it is completely inert for server or network errors. Any future query added to the app that does not explicitly check its own .error state will fail completely silently. Suggested fix: at minimum log the error (console.error), and consider storing it in a Svelte writable store so a toast/banner can display it at the layout level.
close_reason: QueryCache.onError now surfaces non-auth errors via global error banner (errors.ts) + console.error; auth redirect preserved.

title: Operator console 'private' visibility filter matches zero records
description:
internal/store/store.go:331-333 listFilter applies the visibility filter as qdrant.NewMatch("visibility", opts.Visibility). The operator console (ui/src/lib/components/ScopeRail.svelte:26-28) offers a 'private' option whose value is the literal string 'private', which flows to ListOptions.Visibility='private'.

But private records are NEVER stored with visibility=='private'. The store-memory handler (internal/server/tools.go storeMemory) never sets Visibility, so private records carry Visibility=="" (empty). Update/SetVisibility only ever write "" or "shared" (store.go:524-558). The literal 'private' string is only used in *_test.go seed data, never in production write paths.

Result: selecting the 'private' visibility filter in the console issues NewMatch("visibility", "private") which matches no real records, so the list comes back empty. The filter silently returns nothing instead of private records.

Fix options: (a) map the UI 'private' value to an empty-string match (qdrant.NewIsEmpty/NewMatch "") in listFilter, or (b) translate 'private' to "" at the connectapi/handler boundary, or (c) change ScopeRail's private option value to "" — but note "" already means 'all' in ListOptions, so a dedicated sentinel + remap in listFilter is the cleaner fix. Add a store_test case that seeds a private (Visibility=="") record and asserts the 'private' filter returns it.
close_reason: Private filter now matches empty-visibility records (MustNot shared); test added; isolation preserved on real Qdrant.

title: store.List signature change is Go-binary-breaking for external importers
description:
The public method Store.List in internal/store/store.go changed its signature from:

    List(ctx, scope, subj, limit uint64) ([]Memory, error)

to:

    List(ctx, scope, subj, opts ListOptions) ([]Memory, uint64, bool, error)

This is a breaking change for any caller that imports internal/store directly. Within this repo all call sites (connectapi.go, tools.go, store_test.go) are updated in the same PR, so in-repo consumers compile correctly. However, the package path is internal/, which in Go means the package is NOT part of the public API surface for third-party importers (Go enforces the internal/ boundary). Since no external consumer can legally import internal/store, this is not a public API break.

RISKY dimension: if any downstream fork or plugin violates the internal boundary (e.g., by vendoring with a replace directive), that consumer will break. The PR has no deprecation notice or migration doc for such consumers.

Recommendation: no action required for first-party consumers; the change is properly in-repo co-evolved. If the project has or plans downstream plugins that embed or fork the store package, add a CHANGELOG note about the signature change.
close_reason: False positive: internal/ package is not importable outside the module (Go enforced); all in-repo callers (tools.go, connectapi.go, tests) are updated in this same PR. No breakage.

title: deploy job rebuilds from source instead of promoting the build job's artifact
description: .github/workflows/docs-site.yaml: the deploy job (which needs: build) runs pnpm install && pnpm build independently rather than downloading the dist/ artifact produced by the build job. This creates two problems: (1) the artifact actually deployed to Cloudflare Workers is a different build than the one verified by the build job — in theory a re-build between job scheduling could produce a different output; (2) it doubles CI time and pnpm cache churn. Fix: in the build job, add an 'actions/upload-artifact' step that uploads ./dist/; in the deploy job replace the install+build steps with 'actions/download-artifact' before the wrangler deploy step.
close_reason: Fixed: deploy job now downloads the build job's tested docs-site-dist artifact (checkout supplies wrangler.jsonc) instead of rebuilding — tested==deployed, built once. Re-review verified the artifact path resolves to docs-site/dist where wrangler.jsonc's assets.directory points.

title: pnpm/action-setup SHA pinned to v6 lineage but version comment says # v4
description: .github/workflows/docs-site.yaml uses pnpm/action-setup@b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 with the comment '# v4'. However, the commit b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1 is 13 commits ahead of v6.0.0 and 28 commits behind v6.0.8 — it is firmly in the v6 lineage, not v4. The version comment is the project's audit trail for SHA pins (per convention: SHA-pinned actions with # vN comments). A stale/wrong comment defeats the purpose of the audit trail. Fix: update the comment to '# v6' (or pin to the exact v6.x.y tag SHA and note that version).
close_reason: Not a bug — verified pnpm/action-setup tag v4 is an annotated tag (f40ffcd9) dereferencing to exactly b906affcce14559ad1aafd4ab0e942779e9f58b1, so the pin and '# v4' comment are correct. (pnpm/action-setup's latest major is v4; the 'v6 lineage' read conflated the action version with pnpm's own version.)

title: Deployment contract gap: MEM_UI_* / MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_* env vars absent from Helm chart values and template
description:
The PR introduces five new server configuration parameters (MEM_UI_ENABLED, MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, MEM_UI_REDIRECT_URL, MEM_UI_COOKIE_KEY) that activate the web UI auth lane. None of them appear in:
- charts/engram/values.yaml  (no ui: or oidc.clientId etc. stanza)
- charts/engram/templates/memory-mcp.yaml  (no corresponding env: entries)

The existing OIDC parameters (MEM_OIDC_ISSUER, MEM_OIDC_AUDIENCE, MEM_OIDC_RESOURCE_METADATA) are all Helm-native (values.yaml memory.oidc.* + conditional env blocks in the template). The new parameters follow the same pattern in code but have no Helm counterpart.

Impact: An operator using the Helm chart (the primary deployment mechanism per the chart README and the live cluster pattern referenced in values.yaml) cannot activate the web UI without injecting raw env vars out-of-band (e.g. via valuesObject or a separate Secret). This is a deployment contract gap: the feature ships but is not deployable via the chart's own contract. The MEM_UI_COOKIE_KEY value also needs Secret-backed injection (it is a 32-byte AES key), which the chart's existing secretKeyRef pattern already supports for MEM_LITELLM_KEY — making the omission especially inconsistent.

Suggested fix: Add a memory.ui stanza to values.yaml (enabled: '', clientID: '', redirectURL: '', clientSecret/cookieKey as secretKeyRef-backed entries mirroring the litellm.keySecret pattern) and conditional env blocks in the template. This also means MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET and MEM_UI_COOKIE_KEY should never be plaintext values in values.yaml — they need the secretKeyRef treatment.
close_reason:
Deferred to engram-vmy
engram-vmy (chart wiring ships with SPA/deployment plan)

title: Breaking: Connect/EngramService RPC surface silently removed for existing anonymous callers on upgrade
description:
The PR flips mountConnect(nil) from 'mount with anonymous resolver' to 'not mounted at all' (R1). This is intentional (closes the anonymous Connect exposure), but it is a breaking behavioral change for any existing consumer of the Connect/EngramService HTTP RPC surface that was relying on the previously-anonymous mount.

Location: internal/server/connectapi.go lines 134-157 (before/after the mountConnect change); cmd/engram/serve.go line 139 (log says 'Connect API not mounted').

Who is affected: Any tool, script, or client that calls /engram.v1.EngramService/* RPCs directly (e.g. via grpc-web, connect-go client, or buf curl) on a deployment that previously had the Connect surface accessible without credentials. On upgrade to this build without MEM_UI_* configuration, every such call returns HTTP 404 rather than an unauthenticated response.

What is missing: There is no CHANGELOG entry, no deprecation notice in the flag help text, and no upgrade note in the PR description distinguishing 'headless mode now removes the Connect surface' from the old behavior. The PR body names R1 but frames it as a security fix, not as a removal of a previously-usable RPC path. Operators who relied on anonymous Connect (e.g. for internal tooling using the read API) will see 404s with no hint that the feature requires MEM_UI_* activation.

Suggested fix: Add an upgrade note to CHANGELOG or the PR description: 'Before this release, the Connect/EngramService RPC surface was always mounted (anonymous bucket). After this release it is only mounted when the web UI auth lane is active (MEM_UI_* or --oidc-client-id/--ui-cookie-key etc). Existing consumers must either enable the UI lane or migrate to MCP tool calls.' A one-line note in serve.go's log is already present; the gap is in operator-facing documentation.
close_reason: Breaking change signaled via PR title (feat!) + BREAKING CHANGE body section for release-please/squash-merge

title: Session type seals refresh token into browser cookie, exposing long-lived credentials on cookie leak
description:
File: internal/webauth/session.go

The Session struct carries both Access (bearer token) and Refresh (long-lived refresh token) as exported fields sealed into the browser cookie:

    type Session struct {
        Sub     string    `json:"sub"`
        Access  string    `json:"at"`
        Refresh string    `json:"rt"`
        Expiry  time.Time `json:"exp"`
    }

The AES-GCM envelope protects against forgery, but the entire payload — including the refresh token — travels to the browser and back with every request. If the sealed cookie value is ever captured (proxy logs, browser devtools export, XSS that can read Set-Cookie response header before HttpOnly takes effect, or a future non-HttpOnly cookie path), both the access token and the refresh token are compromised. A refresh token is effectively a long-lived credential that allows minting new access tokens until it is revoked.

The minimum viable payload for authorization is Sub + Expiry. Access and Refresh are only needed when engram needs to call downstream APIs on behalf of the user (the 'future write phase' mentioned in comments). At that point they should be kept server-side (encrypted at rest in Qdrant or a short-lived cache) and fetched on-demand, not shipped to the browser.

Suggested fix: remove Access and Refresh from Session for the initial landing; add them back only when the write-phase downstream call lands, at which point they should be stored server-side rather than in the cookie. If the stateless-cookie design constraint (D4) is a hard requirement, the refresh token at minimum should be omitted from the cookie and the access token should be dropped once it is no longer needed for the current request cycle.
close_reason: Fixed in fix batches A/B/C (commits prnnnpny/topslrmx/optxkuuw); review gate PASS on all 17

title: Login handler's two 500 paths have no server-side log
description:
File: internal/webauth/handlers.go lines 51-59 (Login handler).

Two error paths return HTTP 500 without any slog call:
1. json.Marshal(flowState{...}) failure (lines 51-54): theoretically impossible for a struct with only string fields, but if it ever fires there is no log.
2. h.codec.sealBytes(fs) failure (lines 56-59): this calls io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, ...) internally; rand.Reader exhaustion or read error would hit this path with no server-side trace.

The exchange path in Callback logs, but neither Login 500 path does. Consistent logging of all 500 paths is expected under this project's 'never silently open' principle.

Suggested fix: add slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "login flow seal failed", "err", err) before each http.Error call for the 500 cases.
close_reason: Fixed in fix batches A/B/C (commits prnnnpny/topslrmx/optxkuuw); review gate PASS on all 17

title: Callback Seal failure (500) has no server-side log
description:
File: internal/webauth/handlers.go lines 137-145 (Callback handler).

After h.auth.exchange() succeeds and h.codec.Seal() is called, any error from Seal returns HTTP 500 with http.Error(w, "internal error", ...) but no slog call. The exchange failure on line 131 is correctly logged with slog.WarnContext, making the Seal failure path inconsistent: an operator debugging a 500 in the callback handler gets no log evidence that the Seal step specifically failed.

This is the silent 500 previously noted as engram-2av.11.

Suggested fix: add slog.ErrorContext(r.Context(), "session seal failed", "err", err) immediately before the http.Error call on line 144.

title: Callback tampered/corrupt flow cookie path has no test
description:
handlers.go:107-110 handles a flow cookie that fails unsealBytes (tampered, replayed from a different key rotation, or bit-flipped). This branch returns 400 but is never exercised by any test. The callback test suite covers missing-cookie (r.Cookie fails) and state-mismatch, but not the intermediate case where the cookie is present but the AEAD open fails.

Location: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/drain-epic-engram-2av/internal/webauth/handlers.go lines 107-110

Why it matters: the flow cookie carries the PKCE verifier — corrupting it is the closest an attacker can get to injecting a verifier without a server secret. The branch is security-relevant (fail-closed). A future refactor that accidentally swaps the error branch with the happy path would go undetected without a test.

Suggested test (in handlers_test.go):
  func TestCallbackRejectsCorruptFlowCookie(t *testing.T) {
    h := testHandler(t)
    rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/auth/callback?code=x&state=s", nil)
    req.AddCookie(&http.Cookie{Name: flowCookieName, Value: "not-valid-base64-aead"})
    h.Callback(rec, req)
    if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
      t.Fatalf("status=%d want 400 (corrupt flow cookie)", rec.Code)
    }
  }
close_reason: Fixed in fix batches A/B/C (commits prnnnpny/topslrmx/optxkuuw); review gate PASS on all 17

title: Callback missing-code path (code=="") has no test
description:
handlers.go:124-128 rejects an auth-code callback with no `code` query parameter (`http.StatusBadRequest`). No test exercises this branch. The callback guard suite covers missing-flow-cookie and state-mismatch but omits the missing-code case entirely.

Location: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/drain-epic-engram-2av/internal/webauth/handlers.go lines 124-128

Why it matters: an IdP can send an error response to /auth/callback without a code (e.g., user denied consent sends ?error=access_denied with no code). Without coverage this branch could silently change behaviour — e.g. if the empty-code check were accidentally removed, the code would pass an empty string to exchange(), which would silently fail at the IdP network call rather than failing fast at the handler boundary.

Suggested test (in handlers_test.go):
  func TestCallbackRejectsMissingCode(t *testing.T) {
    h := testHandler(t)
    fs, _ := json.Marshal(flowState{State: "s", Verifier: "v"})
    sealed, _ := h.codec.sealBytes(fs)
    rec := httptest.NewRecorder()
    req := httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, "/auth/callback?state=s", nil) // no code
    req.AddCookie(&http.Cookie{Name: flowCookieName, Value: sealed})
    h.Callback(rec, req)
    if rec.Code != http.StatusBadRequest {
      t.Fatalf("status=%d want 400 (missing code)", rec.Code)
    }
  }

title: Connect handler bypasses otelhttp and accessLog middleware
description:
In cmd/engram/serve.go the Connect routes are mounted on the mux before otelhttp and accessLog are applied; otelhttp and accessLog only wrap the MCP handler, which is then added as the '/' catch-all. Requests to /engram.v1.EngramService/* hit the Connect handler directly, bypassing both the OpenTelemetry HTTP span (otelhttp.NewHandler) and the access log / auth-failure counter (accessLog / tm.RecordAuthFailure). This means Connect API calls produce no HTTP traces and no access-log entries — the observability gap is not just a future concern, it is a gap on day 1.

The fix is to wrap the mux itself (not the per-handler chain) with otelhttp and accessLog, or to apply the middleware inside mountConnect. The PR description notes the observability parity issue as a follow-up, but at the current routing structure it is silently missing from the running binary, not merely unimplemented.

Location: cmd/engram/serve.go lines 95-104 + internal/server/connectapi.go mountConnect.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-2ft (Connect auth-posture follow-up) which already tracks wrapping the Connect path in the accessLog/otelhttp chain. accessLog's auth-failure semantics are MCP-bearer-specific; correct fix belongs with the cookie/OIDC lane.

title: 'buf breaking --against main' fails because proto/ is new (no baseline on main)
description: The 'buf' CI job fails on the 'buf breaking (vs main)' step with: 'Failure: Module "path: "."" had no .proto files'. This is expected on the first PR that introduces proto/: the against-main baseline has no proto files, so buf has no prior schema to diff against. The buf job is intentionally non-required (the PR description notes 'Promote the buf CI job to a required check' as a follow-up), so this does not block merge. However the job is also unconditionally structured to run breaking checks; for the proto-bootstrap commit the check is inherently vacuous. Fix options: (a) add 'continue-on-error: true' on the breaking step only for the bootstrap commit, (b) accept the failure for this PR since the job is non-required, or (c) skip breaking check when no prior proto exists (buf supports '--error-format text' and 'exit-code 0' on empty baseline). This is tracked as a follow-up in the PR description.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-3df. Non-required job; self-heals once main has proto/ post-merge.
