title: ADR engram-kyz decision text not updated to reflect anonymous-bucket read restriction
description:
Location: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram/docs/adr/engram-kyz-sharing-grants-read-but-never-write-read-write-gate-asymmetr.md line 17.

What's wrong: ADR engram-kyz states in its Decision section: 'getReadable admits owner==sub OR visibility=="shared"' — stated as an unqualified invariant with no authenticated-only qualifier. The PR changes GetReadable so that when sub=="" (anonymous), the rule is owner=="" only (not owner==sub OR shared). This is a behavioral divergence from the ADR's stated load-bearing contract.

The ADR context section does mention 'other authenticated callers', but the Decision text itself omits that qualifier — and the Decision section is what tooling and future contributors read as the binding rule.

The PR correctly fixes code and updates CLAUDE.md/README, but does not update the ADR. Per the project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md conventions, 'if the change contradicts an ADR, a new ADR (or update) should be proposed.' No new ADR was proposed and the existing one was not amended.

Suggested fix: Update ADR engram-kyz Decision section to read: 'getReadable admits owner==sub OR visibility=="shared" for authenticated callers (sub != ""); anonymous callers (sub=="", auth disabled) are restricted to owner=="" only. getWritable and ownedOrAbsent require owner==sub.' This makes the anonymous-bucket restriction a named, first-class part of the contract, consistent with the code and docs.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #54 docs commit: ADR engram-kyz addendum added (anon-caller read restriction) + rendered; TestAnonBucketDiscoveryReadIsolation docstring uses anonymous-bucket terminology.

title: ownerOrSharedCondition/README/test comments conflate 'ownerless bucket' (owner="") with 'ownerless' (missing key)
description:
Files: internal/store/store.go (ownerOrSharedCondition comment), README.md (Isolation paragraph), internal/store/store_test.go (TestAnonBucketReadIsolation inline comment, TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers docstring in tools_test.go)

This PR introduces the term 'ownerless bucket' in multiple places to refer to the anonymous-caller read domain (records with owner==""). However, the existing ownerlessFilter() function uses 'ownerless' to mean a DIFFERENT thing: records with a MISSING owner key (pre-isolation records). ownerlessFilter() explicitly documents: 'NewIsEmpty matches a missing, null, or empty-array owner payload but NOT an explicit empty string.'

Conflated uses introduced in this PR:

1. internal/store/store.go, ownerOrSharedCondition godoc:
   'the anonymous bucket is the single ownerless bucket, not a back-door to all shared records'
   — 'ownerless bucket' here means owner=="", but 'ownerless' elsewhere means missing key.

2. README.md, Isolation paragraph:
   'Anonymous callers (auth disabled) see only the ownerless bucket'
   — Same conflation in user-facing documentation.

3. internal/store/store_test.go, TestAnonBucketReadIsolation inline comment:
   '// ownerless record — simulates pre-upgrade / auth-disabled records (eu8.14).'
   — The record has Owner: "" (explicit empty), not a missing key. This is the
   anonymous bucket, not the pre-upgrade ownerless scenario. (The eu8.14 false-claim
   is filed separately as a critical finding.)

4. internal/server/tools_test.go, TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers docstring:
   'return ownerless records but NOT owner-stamped shared records'
   — The seeded 'ownerless' record has Owner: "", not a missing key.

The ambiguity is dangerous: a reader familiar with ownerlessFilter's definition of 'ownerless' could incorrectly conclude that anonymous callers can reach pre-isolation records, when they cannot.

Suggested fix: Introduce distinct terminology. Use 'anonymous bucket' or 'auth-disabled bucket' for owner=="" records, reserving 'ownerless' / 'pre-isolation' for records with a missing owner key. For example:

ownerOrSharedCondition godoc:
  'the anonymous bucket (owner=="") is NOT a back-door to all shared records'

README:
  'Anonymous callers (auth disabled) see only their own bucket (owner=="") and cannot read shared records.'

TestAnonBucketReadIsolation:
  '// auth-disabled record (owner=="")'

TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers:
  'return auth-disabled-bucket records (owner=="") but NOT owner-stamped shared records'
close_reason: Fixed in docs commit on PR #54 (tppmwnkp): CLAUDE.md/README/store.go/test doc+comment accuracy — anonymous-bucket vs missing-key terminology disambiguated, false eu8.14 reachability claim corrected, operator migration note added, TOCTOU diagnostics + unicode banners fixed. No logic change.

title: Anonymous read isolation tightening is a behavioral breaking change to the stable MCP tool contract
description:
## Finding

**File:** internal/store/store.go — ownerOrSharedCondition / GetReadable
**File:** internal/server/tools.go (handlers delegate to store)

### What changed

Before this PR, ownerOrSharedCondition("") produced:

  Should:[owner=="", visibility=="shared"]

Anonymous callers (sub=="", auth disabled) could therefore read any record marked visibility=="shared", regardless of who owns it.

After this PR, ownerOrSharedCondition("") produces:

  Must:[owner==""]

Anonymous callers now see only ownerless records (owner==""). The same tightening is applied in GetReadable via an explicit sub=="" guard.

### Why this is an important behavioral change to a stable contract

CLAUDE.md declares the tool contract (search_memory / list_memory / get_memory / search_discovery) STABLE. This PR changes the observable result set for anonymous callers across all four read operations. Any deployment that has:

1. OIDC disabled (no --oidc-issuer), AND
2. Records with owner != "" that are marked visibility=="shared" (e.g., written when auth was previously enabled, then auth was disabled — a valid migration path described in the README)

...will silently see those shared records disappear from search_memory / list_memory / get_memory / search_discovery results after upgrade, with no error returned to the caller. The caller receives a smaller result set or ErrNotFound — indistinguishable from those records not existing.

### Is it justified?

Yes. The old behavior violated the documented intent: the README has always said "readable by any *authenticated* caller" and the commit message explicitly identifies the prior behavior as "more permissive than intended." This is a legitimate security fix: anonymous callers should not be able to reach other actors' shared records.

### Is it documented sufficiently for operators?

Partially. The README is updated in this PR diff to explicitly state the new restriction. The PR uses fix: commit prefixes, so release-please will surface entries in CHANGELOG under Bug Fixes. However:

- CLAUDE.md's memory contract section still says only "No issuer → single anonymous bucket" with no mention of the new restriction on shared records for anonymous callers. Operators who rely on CLAUDE.md as the authoritative contract reference will not see the change.
- There is no migration guide for the specific scenario: was-auth-enabled → auth-disabled with owner-stamped shared records in the store.

### Suggested fix

1. Add a sentence to the CLAUDE.md memory contract's Isolation block: "Anonymous callers (sub=="") see only the ownerless bucket — the shared read grant requires an authenticated subject."
2. Add an operator note to the README Upgrading section (or a new section) for the mixed-auth scenario: if a deployment had authentication enabled, wrote shared records, then disabled authentication, those shared records will become unreadable to anonymous callers after this upgrade.

The change itself is correct and should merge; the gap is documentation coverage for the operator audience.

No logic change.

title: Handler-level read-isolation tests absent for anonymous caller restriction
description:
The acceptance criteria for engram-99z.13 explicitly requires 'handler+store tests'. Three new store-layer tests (TestAnonBucketReadIsolation, TestAnonBucketWriteSemantics, TestAnonBucketDiscoveryReadIsolation) cover the restriction thoroughly at the store layer. However, no handler-level test was added in internal/server/tools_test.go that exercises an MCP tool call (searchMemory, list, get_memory) with sub=='' and verifies that a shared record owned by an authenticated user is denied.

The existing TestOwnerFromContextNoToken (tools_test.go:205) only asserts ownerFromContext returns ("", nil) — it does not call any store operation. TestUpdateMemoryPreservesSharingHandler seeds an anon-owned record but does not test the new restriction. The tools_test.go comment at line 203 explicitly defers this as the 'handler-isolation gap' due to the go-sdk unexported context key constraint.

While the store tests provide strong functional confidence and the go-sdk injection limitation is real, the acceptance criteria is not fully satisfied. A handler-level integration test using testDeps (which calls the real store with Qdrant via testcontainers) could seed shared records and call d.st.GetReadable / d.st.Search directly with sub=='' as a proxy, or structure a handler call through an anonymous context. This gap should be resolved or formally acknowledged as an exception in the bead.

File: internal/server/tools_test.go (no new test added for anonymous read restriction via handler path)
notes:
Root cause: STALE review finding. Filed at turn:1 of PR #57's review, when the diff lacked handler-level anonymous read-isolation tests. The tests were added in a LATER turn of the SAME PR (#57) before merge, but the finding bead stayed open.

Resolution: NO CODE CHANGE NEEDED — the acceptance criteria ('handler+store tests' for the anonymous sub=='' restriction) is fully satisfied on current trunk by tests committed in 1db7978 (PR #57), internal/server/tools_test.go:
  - TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers (l.257): seeds an owner-stamped (Owner:'sub-owner') Visibility:'shared' record + an anon-bucket (Owner:'') record, then asserts an anonymous context (context.Background() -> sub=='') gets the ownerless record but NOT the shared one through the searchMemory handler, the listMemory handler, and store.GetReadable (the get_memory path — the bead explicitly blessed the d.st.GetReadable proxy; there is no deps.getMemory method, get is served by GetReadable directly). Positive + negative assertions both present.
  - TestAnonReadIsolationDiscoveryHandler (l.347): same for the discovery read path.
  - TestAuthedCrossActorSharedReadHandlers (l.578): authed cross-actor shared-read via the new authedContext(t,sub) test seam (RequireBearerToken round-trip with a stub verifier — the seam that injects a verified sub past the go-sdk's unexported context key).
All three PASS against ephemeral Qdrant (testcontainers). Verified 2026-06-09 in workspace engram-99z-14-handler-iso (off trunk #57): go test ./internal/server -run 'TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers|TestAnonReadIsolationDiscoveryHandler|TestAuthedCrossActorSharedReadHandlers' -> PASS.

Also removed a stray phase:design label (a review-pr aspect:spec tooling artifact; this is implementation-class work, not design-lifecycle).

Note: sibling bead engram-9je (handler cross-actor isolation, 'needs test seam for sub injection') appears similarly satisfied by authedContext + TestAuthedCrossActorSharedReadHandlers — worth a quick check when it comes up.

Recommendation: close as resolved-by-existing-coverage (no branch to merge).

title: Helm chart cannot inject OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS documented in README
description:
The README observability table (README.md line 104) documents OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS as a supported env var for passing auth tokens to a remote OTLP collector. However, charts/engram/values.yaml has no corresponding key (e.g. observability.otlpHeaders) and charts/engram/templates/memory-mcp.yaml has no env-var injection for OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS.

Impact: Helm users who need to authenticate to a remote OTLP collector (e.g. Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb) cannot do so through chart values. They must fall back to patching the Deployment directly or using a valuesObject override with raw env entries — neither of which is documented. The README implies it works out of the box via chart configuration.

Fix: Add observability.otlpHeaders: "" to values.yaml and a corresponding {{- with .Values.observability.otlpHeaders }} - { name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, value: "{{ . }}" } {{- end }} block in memory-mcp.yaml, matching the pattern used for otlpEndpoint and resourceAttributes.

title: README claims OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is honored but resource.WithFromEnv() is never called
description: README.md Observability section (line 105, 43) documents OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES as 'Extra resource attributes, e.g. deployment.environment=prod', and the table row implies setting this env var works. However, internal/telemetry/providers.go:buildProviders calls resource.New(ctx, resource.WithAttributes(semconv.ServiceName(...), semconv.ServiceVersion(...))) with only explicit attributes — there is no resource.WithFromEnv() or resource.WithProcess() call. The OTel Go SDK's resource.New does not automatically merge OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES unless WithFromEnv() is explicitly included as a detector. The env var is silently ignored at runtime. Fix: add resource.WithFromEnv() to the resource.New(...) option list in providers.go, or remove OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES from the README table until it is wired.

title: Setup's buildProviders-error fallback (silent degradation to stdout) is never tested
description:
telemetry.Setup (internal/telemetry/telemetry.go:33-37) has a deliberate error-recovery branch: when buildProviders returns an error it silently falls back to a stdout-only logger and returns noopShutdown — never propagating the error to the caller.

This branch has 0% coverage (Setup overall is 63.6%, but only the non-error path through buildProviders is exercised by TestSetupEnabledBuildsProvidersAndShutsDown which succeeds because the OTLP exporter doesn't dial eagerly).

The fallback is the contract that 'telemetry must never be a hard startup dependency.' If a regression causes buildProviders to succeed when it shouldn't (or the fallback path itself is broken — e.g. returning err instead of nil), the server either silently drops logs or unexpectedly refuses to start.

Fix: inject a failing buildProviders by temporarily using a cancelled context or an invalid endpoint that causes synchronous failure, then assert Setup returns a non-nil logger, a nil error, and a working noopShutdown.

title: fanoutHandler methods (Enabled/Handle/WithAttrs/WithGroup) have 0% coverage — logging silently drops records if fanout is broken
description:
The fanoutHandler in internal/telemetry/logger.go is the core dispatch mechanism used when both stdout AND an OTLP log provider are active. All four interface methods — Enabled, Handle, WithAttrs, WithGroup — show 0.0% coverage per the coverage profile.

The fanout constructor itself is called (100%), but the returned handler's methods are never exercised because no test passes a non-nil LoggerProvider to newLoggerTo. This means a regression in fanout dispatch (e.g. a handler-index bug, a missing Clone, or a WithAttrs that drops an attribute) would not be caught.

The fanout handle path contains a real behavior difference from a single-handler path: it calls r.Clone() to avoid record sharing between handlers, and it only calls Handle when h.Enabled returns true. Neither of these is verified.

Fix: add a test that passes a second slog.Handler (e.g. a slog.NewJSONHandler to a second bytes.Buffer) as a fake LoggerProvider or via newLoggerTo with a non-nil lp stub, then asserts both handlers receive the record.

Affected file: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/observability/internal/telemetry/logger.go lines 73-107

title: accessLog panics on nil authFailureFunc — unguarded required parameter
description:
File: cmd/engram/httplog.go

accessLog(authFail authFailureFunc, observe func(int)) calls authFail unconditionally on 401/403 responses (lines 39, 41) but has no nil guard. The observe parameter is explicitly documented as 'nil in production' and is guarded (line 43: if observe != nil). authFailureFunc carries no such note and is never guarded.

The type authFailureFunc is defined as a function type that callers can pass as nil, making the nil-panic path reachable from any caller that doesn't know the convention. In contrast, the concrete call site in serve.go always passes tm.RecordAuthFailure (non-nil), so the bug is latent, not live — but any future test or alternate wiring that passes nil will panic on the first 401 or 403.

The asymmetry between the two parameters (observe is nil-safe, authFail is not) also makes the API confusing: both have the same syntactic form but only one is nil-tolerant.

Fix options:
1. Add a nil check: if authFail != nil { authFail(...) }
2. Provide a no-op default: if authFail is nil, substitute a no-op (makes the parameter truly optional)
3. Document and enforce non-nil in the type or constructor (e.g., panic on nil at accessLog call time, not at request time)
close_reason: Fixed in round 1; review-gate PASS

title: withAuth os.Exit(1) on OIDC init failure contradicts spec error-handling contract
description:
The design spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-observability-logging-telemetry-design.md, Error handling section) explicitly states: 'Startup fatal errors (store init, verifier init) switch from log.Fatalf to slog.Error + explicit os.Exit(1) from main, after attempting a telemetry flush, so the failure record is not lost.'

The implementation in cmd/engram/serve.go:130-132 calls os.Exit(1) directly inside withAuth, which is called from runServe after the deferred telemetry shutdown is registered. os.Exit bypasses all deferred functions, so the telemetry flush never runs and any buffered log records (including the slog.Error failure line itself) are silently dropped from the OTLP batch.

This is a direct contradiction of the spec's stated design intent for verifier-init failures. The Register refactoring explicitly returns an error so runServe can flush and exit cleanly; withAuth must be given the same treatment.

Suggested fix: change withAuth to return (http.Handler, error), handle the error in runServe (consistent with the Register pattern three lines above). The deferred shutdown then runs on return, flushing the failure record before the process exits.

File: cmd/engram/serve.go:120-135
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-07-observability-logging-telemetry-design.md, Error handling section, line 254-256.

title: http.Server WriteTimeout=60s severs long-lived MCP SSE streams
description:
cmd/engram/serve.go:274-281: the new http.Server sets WriteTimeout: 60s and IdleTimeout: 120s. WriteTimeout caps the entire response-write duration. The MCP Streamable HTTP protocol uses long-lived SSE streams (the standalone GET stream for server-initiated messages stays open indefinitely). The go-sdk v1.6.1 streamable handler does NOT clear the connection write deadline (no SetWriteDeadline via ResponseController — verified absent in mcp/streamable.go), so any SSE stream is force-closed after 60s. The prior code used http.ListenAndServe with no timeouts, so this is a behavioral regression for streaming clients.

Suggested fix: set WriteTimeout: 0 (rely on ReadHeaderTimeout + IdleTimeout + the graceful-shutdown context for bounding), or have the handler clear the per-request write deadline for SSE. ReadHeaderTimeout (10s) already mitigates slowloris, so WriteTimeout is the dispensable one here.

Location: cmd/engram/serve.go:274-281.
close_reason: Fixed in round 1; review-gate PASS

title: statusWriter wrapper breaks SSE flushing in MCP Streamable HTTP handler (missing Unwrap)
description:
cmd/engram/httplog.go: the accessLog middleware wraps the ResponseWriter in *statusWriter, which embeds http.ResponseWriter but does not implement Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter. The MCP go-sdk v1.6.1 StreamableHTTPHandler flushes SSE via http.NewResponseController(w).Flush() (mcp/streamable.go:1070-1072). http.ResponseController descends through wrappers only via an Unwrap() method; because statusWriter has none, Flush() returns ErrNotSupported and is silently ignored (best-effort). Result: the standalone SSE GET stream's headers are never flushed (go-sdk Issue #410 path) and streamed events are buffered, so clients hang waiting for the stream to open. This is a functional regression introduced by inserting accessLog between otelhttp and the MCP handler.

Fix: add a passthrough so ResponseController can descend:
  func (w *statusWriter) Unwrap() http.ResponseWriter { return w.ResponseWriter }

Location: cmd/engram/httplog.go:132-140 (statusWriter type + WriteHeader).
close_reason: Fixed in round 1; review-gate PASS

title: buildDepsFromEnv doc comment lists env vars it no longer reads directly

title: delete_all silently skips pre-migration records, returning 'scope cleared' for zero deletions
description:
**Location:** internal/store/store.go — DeleteAll (lines ~409-419)

**What is wrong:**
DeleteAll filters by NewMatch("scope", scope) AND NewMatch("owner", sub). Pre-migration records have no owner key in Qdrant, so NewMatch("owner", sub) never matches them regardless of the value of sub. The Delete call succeeds against 0 matched points, and the MCP handler returns 'scope cleared' — a success response — even though no records were actually deleted.

This creates a silent accumulation hazard: an operator running a teardown cycle (e.g., end-of-session cleanup, test cleanup) after upgrade but before migration will believe all records have been deleted, but the pre-migration records persist in the collection indefinitely. They are also invisible to reads (see companion critical finding), so they accumulate unreachably with no operator signal.

**Evidence:** DeleteAll at store.go line 409-419 uses only NewMatch("owner", sub) — no fallback for absent owner key, no IsEmpty branch, no count-before-delete check.

**Affected tool:** delete_all

**Suggested fix:**
Option A (safe): Add a secondary pass in DeleteAll using NewIsEmpty("owner") when sub=="", or always include an additional condition that also deletes records with no owner key. Example: extend the filter with a Should clause matching either (owner==sub) or IsEmpty(owner) when sub=="".
Option B (simpler): Log a warning if the migration is still pending (startup check as described in the companion critical finding) so operators are alerted before performing teardown operations.
Option C: Return a non-nil error or a count in the response (MCP result carries the text message; changing it to 'scope cleared (0 records)' would make the silence visible).
close_reason: Fixed in 'fix: address PR #38 review findings' (uyvoknto); review-gate PASS.

title: getWritable owner-equality check breaks down when auth disabled (sub == "")
description:
File: internal/store/store.go — getWritable (line 329), and callers Update, Delete, SetVisibility.

The invariant getWritable aims to enforce is: only the record's owner may write.
The check is: m.Owner != sub → deny.

When OIDC auth is disabled, ownerFromContext returns "", so sub == "". Any record stored in the anonymous bucket has Owner == "". The check m.Owner != sub evaluates to "" != "" == false, so the deny branch is never taken. This means every anonymous caller can overwrite or delete every other anonymous-bucket record — the write-isolation invariant does not hold in the no-auth mode.

The design doc calls this the "single anonymous bucket" and says isolation requires authentication, so the behaviour is documented. However, the invariant gap is not surfaced at the type level or at the call site — getWritable silently stops protecting when sub is empty.

Blast radius: single-user self-hosted service where auth is usually enabled; low in practice. But the contract of getWritable is "caller must own the record" with no carve-out for the empty-sub case, making it a latent correctness hazard if multi-user no-auth deployments arise.

Suggested fix (proportionate):
  if sub == "" {
      return m, nil  // anonymous bucket: all callers share ownership; guard is opt-in with OIDC
  }
  if m.Owner != sub { ... }

Or document the precondition on getWritable explicitly: '// sub=="" bypasses owner check (anonymous bucket)'.
close_reason: Fixed in 'fix: address PR #38 review findings' (uyvoknto); review-gate PASS.

title: MigrateSetOwner: Count→SetPayload is non-atomic; reported stamp count may be wrong
description:
File: internal/store/store.go — MigrateSetOwner()

The function calls Count() then SetPayload() as two separate Qdrant RPCs with no transaction or lock between them. The filter (qdrant.NewIsEmpty("owner")) is re-evaluated at SetPayload time, not snapshotted, so:

1. Records written between Count and SetPayload that have no owner will be stamped (silently, correctly migrated) but not reflected in the returned cnt. The caller (and the CLI output) prints "stamped owner=X onto N records" where N came from Count but the actual number stamped may be higher.

2. Records whose owner key is removed between Count and SetPayload would be stamped — unlikely in practice but consistent with the non-atomic pattern.

For a one-time migration tool the security impact is low, but the inaccurate count printed to the operator ("stamped ... onto N records") is misleading and makes idempotency verification unreliable.

Suggested fix: drop the Count pre-check entirely. Qdrant's SetPayload with a filter is effectively atomic for the stamp operation itself. Replace the Count+SetPayload pair with a single SetPayload call, then verify idempotency by re-counting. Or: keep Count only for the early-exit optimization (cnt==0 → skip) and add a comment warning that the returned count is approximate, not exact.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-v31 (moved out of review epic engram-eu8)

title: No handler-layer isolation test: cross-actor rejection for delete/update/set_visibility/get_memory tools
description:
tools_test.go contains exactly one isolation-related test (TestUpdateMemoryPreservesSharingHandler) and it only exercises the anonymous-sub (owner="") path. There is no handler-layer test that:

- Calls updateMemory with a context carrying sub="sub-A" against a record owned by "sub-B" and asserts ErrNotFound is returned.
- Calls the delete_memory handler function with a non-owner sub and confirms the record survives.
- Calls the set_visibility handler with a non-owner sub and confirms rejection.
- Calls the get_memory handler (GetReadable path) with a non-owner sub for a private record.

The store-layer unit tests (TestDeleteOwnerGate, TestUpdateOwnerGateAndSharedFlag, TestSetVisibilityOwnerGate, TestGetReadableOwnerGate) cover these paths at the store level, but the handler code in tools.go introduces the ownerFromContext() extraction step between the MCP call and the store. If ownerFromContext were broken (returned "", or was wired to actorFromContext by mistake), the store tests would still pass while every isolation invariant silently collapsed at the HTTP boundary.

Affected file: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram/internal/server/tools_test.go

Suggested fix: add a TestIsolationHandlers test that builds two deps (or reuses one with two contexts carrying different mcpauth.TokenInfo.Extra["sub"] values), stores a private record under sub-A, then calls d.updateMemory / d.st.Delete / d.st.SetVisibility / d.st.GetReadable from a sub-B context and asserts ErrNotFound in each case. Also tests that sub-B cannot overwrite a discovery with a client-supplied id owned by sub-A (OwnedOrAbsent path).
close_reason: Deferred to engram-9je (moved out of review epic engram-eu8)

title: updateMemory embeds before ownership check — non-owner triggers external embedder call
description:
Location: internal/server/tools.go — func (d *deps) updateMemory()

The handler calls em.Embed() first, then passes the resulting vec to st.Update() which calls getWritable() for the ownership gate. If the caller does not own the record, getWritable() returns ErrNotFound — but by that point an HTTP roundtrip to the embedder has already been made.

This is an efficiency issue but also a minor correctness concern: a non-owner can cause the server to make authenticated calls to the embedding service (potentially against a rate-limited or metered endpoint) before the gate fires.

The old code fetched the record via st.Get() before embedding, then re-embedded. That was the correct order: check existence/access first, embed only if the write will succeed.

Fix: reorder so getWritable (or a lightweight ownership pre-check) runs before the embed call. One clean approach is to call st.getWritable directly in the handler or expose a lightweight CanWrite method, then embed only on success.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-dcu (moved out of review epic engram-eu8)

title: update_memory tool Description omits new shared field — agents cannot discover sharing via schema
description:
Location: internal/server/tools.go — the update_memory AddTool call (unchanged in this PR).

The PR adds Shared *bool to updateArgs and wires it through st.Update(), but leaves the tool Description as "Replace a memory's content in place (re-embeds).". An MCP client reading the tool schema to decide how to use the tool cannot discover that update_memory can also toggle visibility.

The jsonschema tag on the Shared field ('omit to keep current visibility; true=shared, false=private') is present in the struct, and MCP frameworks may surface it via the schema. However the top-level Description string is the primary signal agents use to reason about a tool's capability.

Fix: update the Description to mention the optional shared field, e.g.: "Replace a memory's content in place (re-embeds). Optionally set shared=true/false to toggle visibility; omit to preserve current sharing state."
close_reason: Fixed in 'fix: address PR #38 review findings' (uyvoknto); review-gate PASS.

title: Reads not actor-filtered: scope reads (incl. cross_spine) expose all actors' records
description: Re-filed from engram-f7h.3 (PR #27 review finding, deferred to the authz design). engram applies NO per-actor read filter on any tool; cross_spine=true returns every actor's discoveries across all scopes, and even a single-scope read returns all actors' records in that scope (actor is an audit field, not an access filter). Acceptance criterion for per-actor authorization (engram-99z): filter reads by actor and define cross_spine semantics under isolation (my records across my scopes). Origin: engram-f7h.3 (closed; re-filed here). Design owner: engram-99z.
close_reason: Fixed by engram-99z / PR #38: Search+List use ownerScopeFilter(scope,sub); SearchDiscovery appends ownerOrSharedCondition(sub) and keeps it in the cross_spine (empty-scope) path — my+shared semantics. Covered by TestSearchDiscoveryOwnerIsolation + TestSearchListOwnerIsolation. Residual hardening tracked separately (engram-99z.13 empty-sub, engram-xic fail-closed).

title: Writes not actor-gated: client-supplied id enables cross-actor overwrite
description: Re-filed from engram-f7h.2 (PR #27 review finding, deferred to the authz design). store_discovery — and the pre-existing updateMemory — accept a client-supplied id and Upsert in place with NO check that the existing record's actor matches the caller. Any authenticated caller who knows/guesses another actor's record UUID can overwrite it, reattributing it to themselves. Acceptance criterion for per-actor authorization (engram-99z): gate id-overwrite/update writes by actor-match. Origin: engram-f7h.2 (closed; re-filed here). Design owner: engram-99z.
close_reason: Fixed by engram-99z / PR #38: storeDiscovery gates client-supplied id via OwnedOrAbsent(id,sub) before upsert; updateMemory/delete/set_visibility gate via getWritable (owner-strict, shared never writable). Covered by TestUpdateOwnerGateAndSharedFlag + owner-gate tests. Residual: engram-dcu (gate-before-embed in updateMemory), engram-1ih (TOCTOU).

title: citationArg.Kind jsonschema description implies enforcement that does not exist
description:
File: internal/server/tools.go, line 120.

The jsonschema tag on citationArg.Kind reads:
  `jsonschema:"file|commit|url|repo"`

This reads as an enumeration constraint. An agent (or developer) using the tool schema will interpret it as meaning only those four values are accepted. However, validateStoreDiscovery (lines 145-159) applies no validation on citation.Kind whatsoever — any non-empty string is silently stored and persisted to Qdrant.

The store.Citation.Kind field comment (store.go line 278) also states '// file | commit | url | repo' with the same implied constraint.

The mismatch between the documented constraint and the absent validation means:
- Agents may store records with invalid kinds (e.g. 'blob', 'pr') while believing they are schema-compliant.
- Future consumers relying on the enumeration invariant (e.g. aging logic keyed on kind) will encounter unexpected values.

Fix options (pick one):
1. Add kind validation to validateStoreDiscovery: if c.Kind not in {file,commit,url,repo} return error.
2. Change the tag to a non-enumerative description (e.g. jsonschema:"source kind: file, commit, url, or repo") and note it is advisory, making clear no server enforcement occurs.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #28 — per-citation kind/ref validation + fromPayload nil-guard

title: storeDiscovery id-replace branch (supplied ID path) is untested
description:
In internal/server/tools.go the storeDiscovery handler has an explicit id-replace branch (lines 195-198):

    id := a.ID
    if id == "" {
        id = uuid.NewString()
    }

The supplied-ID path (where a.ID != "") is the in-place replace contract documented in the SKILL.md (search-before-store then re-supply the id). No test exercises this path.

TestDiscoveryRoundtrip in internal/store/store_test.go does supply an explicit ID to store.Upsert directly, but it never calls (*deps).storeDiscovery, so the handler-level id-passthrough is not tested.

A bug here (e.g. id is zeroed or replaced with a fresh UUID regardless of a.ID) would silently create duplicates rather than updating, breaking the replace-in-place contract and causing unbounded accumulation of stale discoveries.

Suggested fix: In any unit test for storeDiscovery, add a sub-case supplying a fixed ID and assert the returned ID equals the supplied value.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #29 (size limits, scope-prefix, log hygiene, dedupe, SKILL.md id, handler integration tests)

title: storeDiscovery/searchDiscovery handler methods have no test coverage
description:
Neither (*deps).storeDiscovery nor (*deps).searchDiscovery is called by any test in this PR. The unit tests in internal/server/tools_test.go only exercise the pure-function helpers validateStoreDiscovery and effectiveDiscoveryScope. The handler methods themselves — which perform embed, citationArg-to-store.Citation conversion, Memory struct assembly (Source hardcoded to agent-inferred, Category to discovery), and Upsert — are completely uncovered.

Concretely uncovered paths in internal/server/tools.go:
- storeDiscovery lines 183-212: embed call, citation loop, Memory assembly, Upsert
- searchDiscovery lines 249-264: embed call, SearchDiscovery dispatch

A regression to the citationArg->store.Citation field mapping (e.g. swapped Locator/Pin) or to the hardcoded Source/Category fields would not be caught by any CI test.

Suggested fix: Add unit tests using a stub embedder and stub store (the project already has testStore gating on MEM_QDRANT_TEST_ADDR). A pure unit test with a minimal in-process fake for em.Embed and st.Upsert/SearchDiscovery would confirm the handler contracts without requiring Qdrant, consistent with the existing unit/integration split.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #29 (size limits, scope-prefix, log hygiene, dedupe, SKILL.md id, handler integration tests)

title: fromPayload silently appends empty Citation{} for non-struct list items
description:
File: internal/store/store.go, lines 157-165 (fromPayload citation loop)

When a citations list item in the Qdrant payload is not a struct value (e.g. a null, number, or string element — possible from a corrupt write, a future schema migration, or a misbehaving client), item.GetStructValue() returns nil. GetFields() on a nil *Struct returns nil (per structpb: 'if x != nil { return x.Fields }'). Subscripting a nil map (f["kind"]) returns the zero *Value (nil), and GetStringValue() on nil returns "". No error is returned; no item is skipped.

The result is that a malformed payload element is silently appended to m.Citations as Citation{Kind:"", Ref:""} — a vacuous record indistinguishable from intentional data. The caller has no way to know a citation was unreadable.

Fix: add a nil-guard before appending:
  sv := item.GetStructValue()
  if sv == nil {
      continue  // or log a warning and continue
  }
  f := sv.GetFields()
  m.Citations = append(m.Citations, Citation{...})

This matches the existing nil-guard pattern used for the tags list (line 138: 'if lv := v.GetListValue(); lv != nil').
close_reason: Fixed in PR #28 — per-citation kind/ref validation + fromPayload nil-guard

title: citationArg.Ref not validated — empty anchor stored silently
close_reason: Fixed in PR #28 — per-citation kind/ref validation + fromPayload nil-guard

title: search_discovery cross_spine=true exposes all actors' discoveries (broken access control)
description:
Location: internal/store/store.go SearchDiscovery(), lines 347-368 (PR diff); internal/server/tools.go searchDiscovery(), lines 249-265.

When cross_spine=true (scope == ''), SearchDiscovery omits the scope filter and returns all category=discovery records from the entire collection. No actor/identity filter is applied. In a multi-tenant deployment (multiple OIDC-authenticated users sharing one engram instance), any caller can read every other actor's discoveries from every repo by issuing search_discovery with cross_spine=true.

The design intent documented in SKILL.md describes cross_spine as 'span every discovery scope' but does not acknowledge the multi-tenant data leak. The current store layer has no per-actor filter capability, so all records are fully readable by any authenticated peer.

Impact: In a single-user deployment this is moot. In a shared instance (e.g., team or multi-project), discoveries may contain proprietary architecture knowledge, behavioral claims about internal code, or repo URLs the caller should not see.

Suggested fix options (in order of preference):
1. Add an actor filter to SearchDiscovery: when auth is enabled (actor != ''), constrain results to actor == callerActor even in the cross_spine case. This matches the write-side model where actor is always stamped.
2. If cross_spine is intentionally world-readable (shared knowledge base), document it explicitly as a security model decision so operators are aware.
3. At minimum, log a WARN when cross_spine is used so operators can audit usage.
notes: Deferred to design bead engram-99z (per-actor authz). Not cross_spine-specific: scope-based model has no per-actor read filter on any tool. Acceptance criterion of the authz epic.
close_reason: Re-filed as engram-2kw under the authz design (engram-99z); deferred theme-4 finding.

title: store_discovery: client-supplied ID enables cross-actor record overwrite
description:
Location: internal/server/tools.go storeDiscovery(), lines 195-212 (PR diff).

When a.ID is non-empty, storeDiscovery uses it verbatim as the Qdrant point ID and calls Upsert, which replaces the existing record in-place. There is no check that the existing record's Actor matches the caller's verified identity. Any authenticated caller who knows (or guesses) the UUID of another actor's discovery can overwrite it: the replacement carries the new caller's Actor from context, silently changing attribution.

The same pattern exists in updateMemory (pre-existing), but this PR introduces it for discoveries, which are intended to be citation-backed and trusted.

Attack: Actor A stores discovery with id=X. Actor B calls store_discovery with id=X and different content/citations. X is now overwritten with B's content; original understanding is lost.

Suggested fix: Before Upsert with a supplied ID, call st.Get(ctx, id) and verify existing.Actor == actorFromContext(ctx) (or existing.Actor == '' when auth is disabled). Return a permission error if they differ. Alternatively, remove the client-supplied-ID path and expose a separate replace_discovery(id, ...) tool that enforces ownership.
notes: Deferred to design bead engram-99z (per-actor authz). Not a discovery-local fix: engram is authn-only today, single-user, intended model is private-per-author. updateMemory shares this property.
close_reason: Re-filed as engram-ir1 under the authz design (engram-99z); deferred theme-4 finding.

title: Missing regression-test coverage: storeRuleArgs/listRulesArgs jsonschema tags not exercised by TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic
description:
internal/server/tools_test.go's TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic (added specifically to catch bad 'jsonschema' struct tags before they panic at production server startup — mcp.AddTool panics synchronously via toolForErr/jsonschema-go's For[T] when a tag is malformed, see modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk@v1.6.1 mcp/server.go:503-509) enumerates every existing tool's arg type (storeArgs, searchArgs, listArgs, idArgs, updateArgs, scopeArgs, storeDiscoveryArgs, searchDiscoveryArgs, setVisibilityArgs, scheduleArgs, listScheduledArgs) but was not extended for the two new tool arg types added in this PR: storeRuleArgs and listRulesArgs (internal/server/rules.go:25-37), which are registered via mcp.AddTool in internal/server/tools.go Register() (store_rule, list_rules).

I manually verified the new jsonschema tags are well-formed under the installed github.com/google/jsonschema-go v0.4.3 (plain description strings, no leading 'WORD=' pattern, required-vs-optional correctly driven by omitempty presence matching the documented argument tables in docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md), so nothing is broken today. But the project's own established safety net for this exact failure class (a malformed jsonschema tag crashing the whole MCP server at startup) does not cover these two new, PR-introduced types, so a future edit to storeRuleArgs/listRulesArgs that introduces a bad tag would not be caught until prod startup.

Suggested fix: add store_rule and list_rules cases to TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic in internal/server/tools_test.go, following the existing check(...) pattern for the other 11 tools.
close_reason: Duplicate of engram-sysc.2 (TestToolArgSchemasDoNotPanic not extended for store_rule/list_rules)

title: fetch==0 short-circuit comment in store.go List() describes an unreachable 'explicit zero-width request' path
close_reason: Fixed: fetch==0 comment now describes only the reachable Limit==0/empty-set case. Commit lzyn.

title: list_rules multi-scope aggregation and >50 curation-advisory branch are untested
description:
internal/server/rules.go:184-224 (listRules) has two behaviors the design spec's Testing section explicitly enumerates as required but that internal/server/rules_test.go's TestListRulesHandler never exercises:

1. Multi-scope aggregation (rules.go:198-219, the 'for _, sc := range a.Scopes' loop). TestListRulesHandler always calls listRules with Scopes: []string{scope} (a single scope). The spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-rule-memory-kind-design.md:283) lists 'multi-scope' as a required list_rules integration-test dimension alongside completeness/ordering/shapes/tags-AND (all of which ARE covered). If the aggregation loop had a bug — e.g. only returning the last scope's results, or double-counting shared IDs across scopes — no test would catch it.

2. The >50-rules-per-scope curation-smell advisory (rules.go:160 ruleThreshold=50, and the len(ms) > ruleThreshold / 'curation smell — ...' branch at rules.go:209-211,220-222). This is real, spec-required business logic (also explicitly named in the spec's Testing section) with zero coverage — no test ever seeds more than 3 rules in a scope, so the threshold-crossing branch and the exact advisory string format are entirely unverified. A regression here (e.g. an off-by-one on the threshold, or a broken Sprintf) would ship silently since it only affects the human-readable textResult, not the structured {rules} payload asserted by existing tests.

Fix: extend TestListRulesHandler (or add new test functions) to (a) seed rules into two distinct rule:* scopes and call listRules with both in a.Scopes, asserting results from both scopes are present and correctly attributed; and (b) seed >50 rules in one scope and assert the returned advisory string contains 'curation smell' and the correct scope/count, while confirming the {rules} payload itself is unaffected (len(rules) still equals the seeded count).

title: update_memory (shared=false) can un-share a rule, bypassing the set_visibility rules-always-shared guard
description:
PR #290 adds a set_visibility guard (internal/server/tools.go:889-891) that rejects any visibility change on a category=rule record, enforcing the rules-are-always-shared invariant. The same PR adds a rule guard to update_memory (internal/server/tools.go:792-796), but that guard only validates the summary; it does NOT block a visibility change. update_memory accepts Shared *bool (tools.go:378) and passes it to store.Update (internal/store/store.go:1268-1275), which sets Visibility to empty-string (private) when shared=false.

Impact: a caller who owns a rule can call update_memory with id=<rule> and shared=false to silently convert their always-shared rule into a private record, bypassing the set_visibility rejection added in this same PR. The rule then disappears from every other authenticated caller list_rules result and session-start Rules index while still carrying category=rule (an inconsistent state). Ownership is still enforced (FetchForUpdate), so the blast radius is the caller own rule — a design-integrity / incomplete-enforcement gap (OWASP A04 Insecure Design), not a cross-owner authz breach; hence suggestion severity.

Suggested fix: extend the rule guard in updateMemory to also reject a visibility change on a rule (mirror the set_visibility guard). Inside the cur.Category==rule block, if a.Shared != nil and *a.Shared is false, return the same delete-the-rule-instead error; or force the rule to stay shared. Add a rules_test.go case asserting update_memory cannot un-share a rule.

title: New item-N test comments bare-reference the short_id design-spec's numbered acceptance criteria
description:
This PR introduces a new test-comment convention not used elsewhere in the codebase: bare 'item N' references to the numbered acceptance-criteria list in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-short-id-handle-design.md (lines 220-281 of that doc), with no mention of which document the number refers to. Sites:

- internal/store/store_test.go:2701 -- '// >reindexBatch records so the cursor loop pages more than once (item 25).'
- internal/store/store_test.go:2605 -- trailing '// item 30' on a check() call.
- internal/server/tools_test.go:1390 -- '// item 4: another owner's private record -> ErrNotFound (404, not 403; no leak)'
- internal/server/tools_test.go:1403 -- '// item 5: another owner's shared record -> readable'

A grep across the rest of the repo turns up zero other 'item N' test comments, confirming this is new, not an established idiom. The item numbers do correctly match the design doc's list today (verified), but the reference is a bare number with no file path -- a reader who doesn't already have that spec doc open has no way to resolve what 'item 4' or 'item 30' means, and the reference will silently rot if that doc is ever renumbered, split, or archived (the same class of problem as a bare ticket-ID back-reference in source). Most of these comments are still self-explanatory without the number (the surrounding prose/check-label already describes the case), so this is low-severity, but the 'item 30' trailing comment on store_test.go:2605 adds nothing beyond the traceability marker.

Suggest either dropping the bare item-N tags (the inline descriptions already carry the rationale) or, if traceability to the spec is valued, naming the doc explicitly, e.g. '(design-spec item 25)' or a doc-relative reference.

title: Awkward/grammatically broken phrasing in two short_id doc edits
description:
Two prose edits added by this PR read as broken/ambiguous sentences:

1. docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/memory-record.md line 15 (Short ID row): 'Short, case-insensitive handle; accepted anywhere an id is, minted on creation' -- this is missing a word after 'an id is'. It reads as a dangling clause (an id is... what?). Almost certainly meant 'accepted anywhere an id is accepted; minted on creation'.

2. skill/engram/skills/migrating-from-beads/SKILL.md line 50: 'each beads key -> engram id (its short_id is the compact handle to cite, or deduped into <id> / dropped), and confirm which beads keys were forgotten.' The parenthetical mixes two unrelated things under one 'or': (a) a note that the short_id is the compact handle to cite, and (b) the alternate dispositions 'deduped into <id>' / 'dropped' that apply to the outer 'each beads key -> engram id' mapping, not to the short_id aside. As written it reads like citing the short_id is offered as an alternative outcome to dedup/drop, which isn't the intent.

Neither is a factual error, but both will read as confusing/ungrammatical to a future reader of these reference docs. Suggest tightening the wording, e.g. memory-record.md: 'Short, case-insensitive handle; accepted anywhere an id is accepted; minted on creation.' migrating-from-beads/SKILL.md: 'each beads key -> engram id (cite its short_id as the compact handle), or deduped into <id> / dropped, and confirm which beads keys were forgotten.'

title: C-15: backfill-short-ids CLI skips this package's established pure-function-plus-behavior-test pattern
description: Pattern C-15 (stylistic discontinuity). Every other operator-CLI command in cmd/engram/ that prints a dry-run-vs-live summary extracts the string-building logic into a small pure function and unit-tests its actual output: migrate.go's buildRemapSource + TestRemapOwnerFlagValidation (migrate_test.go, table-driven, asserts the returned OwnerRemapSource), reindex.go's reindexSummary + TestReindexSummary (reindex_test.go, asserts dry-run vs live wording/content), and summarize.go's summarizeSummary + TestSummarizeSummary (summarize_test.go, asserts 'dry-run'/count wording). cmd/engram/backfill.go (new in this PR) instead inlines the dry-run/live cmd.Printf branching directly in the cobra RunE closure (lines ~42-46: 'if backfillDryRun { cmd.Printf("[dry-run] would backfill %d record(s)\n", n) } else { cmd.Printf("backfilled %d record(s)\n", n) }'), and the accompanying cmd/engram/backfill_test.go contains exactly one test, TestBackfillCmdHasDryRunAndTimeoutFlags, which only asserts Flags().Lookup("dry-run")/Lookup("timeout") are non-nil -- it never exercises RunE or the dry-run/live wording, unlike every sibling test file in the same package. This is the one file in cmd/engram/ that breaks a 3-for-3 local convention, the classic 'generated in isolation from a different context window than its neighbors' tell. Suggested fix: extract a small pure function (e.g. backfillSummary(n uint64, dryRun bool) string) mirroring reindexSummary/summarizeSummary, call it from RunE, and replace or supplement TestBackfillCmdHasDryRunAndTimeoutFlags with a table-driven test asserting the dry-run vs live wording, matching TestReindexSummary/TestSummarizeSummary's shape. Severity: suggestion -- no functional bug, the current wording is visibly correct, but the test as written would not catch the branches being swapped.

title: backfill-short-ids CLI test only checks flag registration; RunE message-formatting logic is untested (unlike sibling CLI commands)
description:
cmd/engram/backfill_test.go (new file, PR #288) contains a single test, TestBackfillCmdHasDryRunAndTimeoutFlags, which only asserts the two cobra flags are registered:

  if backfillShortIDsCmd.Flags().Lookup("dry-run") == nil ||
     backfillShortIDsCmd.Flags().Lookup("timeout") == nil { t.Fatal(...) }

This does not exercise backfillShortIDsCmd's RunE closure (cmd/engram/backfill.go) at all: the dry-run vs apply message-formatting branch ("[dry-run] would backfill %d record(s)" vs "backfilled %d record(s)"), the --timeout wiring into context.WithTimeout, and the StoreFromEnv error path are all untested.

This deviates from the project's own convention for sibling operator CLI commands, which extract their RunE logic into a plain function and unit-test it directly:
- cmd/engram/reindex_test.go: TestReindexSummary tests reindexSummary(...) for both dry-run and real-run message content.
- cmd/engram/prune_test.go: TestPruneCutoffAppliesGracePeriod tests pruneCutoff(...) arithmetic.
- cmd/engram/migrate_test.go: TestRemapOwnerFlagValidation tests buildRemapSource(...) validation logic via a table of cases.

backfill.go inlines its message formatting directly in the RunE closure with no extracted, testable function, so unlike its siblings there is no way to unit-test the dry-run/apply message content short of invoking the full cobra command (which would need Docker/Qdrant). Suggested fix: extract a small pure function (e.g. backfillSummary(n uint64, dryRun bool) string) mirroring reindexSummary's pattern, and test it directly; this also makes the CLI output easier to keep in sync with the docs-site upgrade guide's example output.

Low risk (message text only, no business logic), but a real, evidenced convention deviation for changed/new test code.

title: Ambiguous-short_id error path (ErrAmbiguousShortID) is untested at every MCP/Connect handler call site
description:
ResolvePointID returning ErrAmbiguousShortID (design doc boundary/edge-matrix item 12, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-short-id-handle-design.md) is tested at the store layer only: TestResolvePointIDAmbiguous in internal/store/store_test.go forces two records to share a short_id (bypassing MintShortID) and asserts store.ResolvePointID returns ErrAmbiguousShortID.

None of the six handler call sites that invoke ResolvePointID -- get_memory, update_memory, delete_memory, set_visibility, store_discovery-replace (internal/server/tools.go), and Connect GetMemory (internal/server/connectapi.go) -- have a test confirming what happens when ResolvePointID itself returns ErrAmbiguousShortID instead of ErrNotFound. Concretely:

- getMemory/updateMemory/deleteMemory/setVisibility (tools.go) only special-case errors.Is(err, store.ErrNotFound) from ResolvePointID's downstream gate; the ResolvePointID call's own error (including ErrAmbiguousShortID) is returned unwrapped via the leading "if err != nil { return ..., err }" branch. Untested whether the MCP framework surfaces this sensibly to a caller.
- connectapi.go's GetMemory explicitly handles ErrNotFound and ErrInvalidArgument from ResolvePointID but falls through to CodeInternal for anything else (including ErrAmbiguousShortID) -- this mapping is not covered by any test.

This is explicitly flagged as "an invariant violation; never expected" in the design doc, so likelihood is low, but the design doc treats it as a real defensive case worth its own boundary-matrix item (12) specifically because a silent pick would be dangerous. Given six independent call sites each need their own ResolvePointID invocation per the design ("every independent call site must invoke ResolvePointID itself"), at least one end-to-end handler test exercising the ambiguous branch (e.g. forcing a duplicate short_id via direct Upsert, then calling d.getMemory or a.GetMemory) would confirm the error propagates without panicking or being mis-mapped to a misleading not-found/success response.

title: storeMemory/scheduleMemory/storeDiscovery return two unnamed same-typed strings (id, shortID) with no compiler-enforced order
description:
This PR changes the signature of three internal/server handler functions from (string, error) to a bare (string, string, error):

- internal/server/tools.go: func (d *deps) storeMemory(ctx, a storeArgs) (string, string, error)
- internal/server/tools.go: func (d *deps) scheduleMemory(ctx, a scheduleArgs) (string, string, error)
- internal/server/tools.go: func (d *deps) storeDiscovery(ctx, a storeDiscoveryArgs) (string, string, error)

Both leading return values are `string` (the record's UUID `id` and its new `short_id`), positionally ordered, with no named returns and no distinguishing type. Every call site (3 handler bodies + the 3 mcp.AddTool closures in Register, e.g. `id, sid, err := d.storeMemory(ctx, a)` then `map[string]string{"id": id, "short_id": sid}`) must get the order right by convention alone; the compiler cannot catch a transposition (e.g. `sid, id, err := ...`). Because both values are exported directly into the MCP tool's JSON result and text message, a future swap would silently return a memory's short_id where callers expect its id (and vice versa) to every store_memory/schedule_memory/store_discovery caller — the highest-traffic write path in the service — without any type error.

Current call sites (internal/server/tools.go lines ~484-501, ~510-535, ~538-620, ~717-723, ~726-732, ~775-781) all order the tuple correctly and are covered by tests (e.g. TestStoreMemoryMintsAndReturnsShortID, TestStoreDiscoveryMintsThenReplacePreservesShortID), so there is no live bug today — this is a latent-risk API smell introduced by this PR, not a pre-existing pattern (no prior function in this codebase returned two positional same-typed strings).

Suggested fix (no new type/ceremony needed, consistent with the codebase's preference for simple concrete types): give the three functions named returns, e.g. `func (d *deps) storeMemory(ctx context.Context, a storeArgs) (id, shortID string, err error)`. This self-documents the tuple at the signature and doc-comment level without requiring a wrapper struct, matching the named-return style already used throughout internal/store/store.go (e.g. ResolvePointID, MintShortID, BackfillShortIDs).

title: MintShortID's collision-retry loop has no bounded attempt limit or explicit exhaustion error
description:
internal/store/store.go:1457-1500, MintShortID:

    for {
        cand, genErr := gen()
        ...
        n, countErr := s.client.Count(ctx, &qdrant.CountPoints{... Filter: short_id==cand ...})
        ...
        if n == 0 { ... return id, nil }
    }

The retry loop has no maximum attempt count and no dedicated 'exhausted N attempts' error. Its only termination guarantee, absent an actual free candidate, is the ambient ctx eventually failing the Count RPC (deadline/cancellation) -- there is no independent bounded-retry safety net.

In practice this is not a live bug: at 50 bits of entropy (10 Crockford chars) a real collision is astronomically unlikely, and the design doc (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-short-id-handle-design.md) explicitly accepts the residual TOCTOU collision risk with ErrAmbiguousShortID as the safety net at resolution time. But that safety net governs resolving a duplicate after the fact -- it does not bound minting attempts. If a bug elsewhere ever caused Count to spuriously return non-zero for every candidate (e.g. a stale/misconfigured short_id payload index, or a caller passing a pre-populated 'seen' map that happens to collide with live data), MintShortID would spin issuing live Qdrant RPCs indefinitely rather than failing fast with a clear diagnostic. Its behavior would then depend entirely on whether the caller's context has a deadline -- the MCP storeMemory/scheduleMemory/storeDiscovery call sites (internal/server/tools.go) pass the request's own context, which is not guaranteed to carry one, unlike the CLI backfill path, which does (--timeout, default 5m).

Suggested fix (defense-in-depth, matching the file's own philosophy of surfacing anomalies rather than looping silently -- see the ErrAmbiguousShortID comment 'surfaced rather than silently resolving to an arbitrary point'): cap the loop at a small bounded attempt count (e.g. 20) and return a descriptive sentinel error such as 'exhausted N attempts to mint a unique short id' on exhaustion, rather than relying solely on ambient context cancellation.

Severity is suggestion, not important: there is no concrete evidenced failure today, only a robustness/observability gap in an already very-low-probability code path.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-8em7 (moved out of review epic)

title: BackfillShortIDs paging test uses 300 records, not the >1000 the design's matrix item 25 specifies
description: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-06-short-id-handle-design.md boundary/edge test matrix item 25 (Backfill section) states: 'Paging: >1000 points backfilled via scroll.' The implemented test, internal/store/store_test.go TestBackfillShortIDs (around line 2696), only creates 300 records ('const total = 300'), with the in-code comment '>reindexBatch records so the cursor loop pages more than once (item 25)' — reindexBatch is 256 (store.go, 'const reindexBatch = 256'), so 300 records crosses exactly one page boundary (2 pages total), not the multi-page-at-scale scenario (>=4-5 pages) the spec's '>1000' figure implies. The cursor-advance property (offset = next) is exercised, so this is not a functional gap, but it is a literal shortfall against the matrix's stated test criterion — a subtler off-by-one or watermark bug surfacing only on the 3rd+ page would not be caught by the current test. Suggest bumping the fixture to something closer to the matrix's stated >1000 (e.g. 4-5x reindexBatch) so the paging test matches the documented boundary condition, or updating the design doc's matrix if 300/2-pages was intentionally judged sufficient.

title: storeDiscovery replace path does a redundant second Get to read the existing short_id
description:
internal/server/tools.go storeDiscovery() (replace-in-place branch, ~lines 577-590). On the a.ID != "" replace path the handler now performs two full point retrievals of the same record before writing:

1. d.st.OwnedOrAbsent(ctx, pointID, subj) — internally calls s.Get(ctx, id) (see internal/store/store.go OwnedOrAbsent) to load the record and check ownership, then discards the Memory and returns only an error.
2. d.st.Get(ctx, pointID) — an immediate second full Get whose sole purpose is to read existing.ShortID into carriedShortID.

(For short-id input there is also a preceding ResolvePointID Scroll, so the replace path is Scroll + Get + Get.) The second Get is redundant: OwnedOrAbsent already fetched the full Memory (ShortID included) but its signature returns only error, so the value is thrown away and re-fetched.

Impact: low — discovery replace is a deliberate, infrequent agent operation, not a hot path, and correctness is fine (a delete race between the two Gets degrades to a benign re-create). Flagging as cross-commit cleanup, not a blocker.

Suggested fix (optional): give the store a single owner-gated fetch that returns the Memory (e.g. reuse FetchForUpdate/getWritable, or add an OwnedOrAbsent variant returning (Memory, error)) and read ShortID from that one result, collapsing the two reads into one. Keep the existing no-leak re-wrap of ErrNotFound with a.ID.

title: Reject malformed rule summaries (newline/oversize/cleared); never silently normalize
description:
## Context

The rules index design requires every rule summary to render as exactly one
terminal line — the summary IS the index entry. Multi-line, oversized, or
cleared summaries could be rejected outright or silently fixed up.

## Decision

`store_rule` and the `update_memory` rule-guard reject any rule summary that
contains a newline/carriage return or exceeds 256 bytes, and reject clearing a
rule's summary. Nothing is silently truncated or normalized. The shared check
lives in `validateRuleSummary`, called by both the store path (pure, unit-tested)
and the update handler (which already holds the fetched record).

## Rationale

- The one-line index-entry contract depends on the summary being exactly one
  physical line; silent munging would corrupt the index unnoticed.
- Matches engram's existing reject-over-silently-handle posture (cf. ADR
  engram-ddiw) applied to format validation rather than edit-drift.
- A rule with no index line is not a valid rule, so clearing is disallowed
  outright.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Reject with explicit error (chosen):** the index never needs truncation
  logic; bad input surfaces at write time.
- **Silently normalize/truncate (rejected):** never rejects a write, but munges
  caller intent invisibly and truncation risks silently cutting the operative
  clause of a rule.

## Consequences

- Positive: every index entry is provably one line, no renderer truncation
  needed; bad input surfaces at write time, not later as a corrupted index.
- Negative: callers must resubmit on rejection; validation logic is shared
  across `store_rule` and the `update_memory` rule-guard.
- Neutral: extends the general explicit/correctable posture (ADR engram-ddiw) to
  a new format-validation case.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Session-start surfaces rules as a progressive-disclosure index, not full-content injection
description:
## Context

The session-start hook must guarantee every rule is visible to a new session
without the context cost scaling with rule content size. A compact index versus
full-text injection was the design fork.

## Decision

The `session-start-memory-recall` hook calls `list_rules` for the spine's
`rule:repo:*` scope (plus `rule:project:*` when `ENGRAM_PROJECT` is set) and
renders a one-line-per-rule index (`short_id — summary [tags]`) above the
recent-10 digest. Full rule text is fetched on demand via
`get_memory(short_id)` when the agent is about to act in a rule's concern area;
it is never bulk-injected. When `list_rules` returns nothing, the section is
omitted entirely.

## Rationale

- Context cost must stay near-zero regardless of rule count for guaranteed
  surfacing to remain viable.
- Single-line summary enforcement means the renderer needs no truncation logic.
- Full text is only needed when acting in a rule's concern area, not uniformly
  at session start.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Progressive-disclosure index (chosen):** context cost ~1 line per rule, 0
  when none exist; full text pulled on demand.
- **Full-content injection at session start (rejected):** never needs a
  follow-up call, but causes unbounded context bloat as the rule set grows,
  defeating the guaranteed-surfacing goal.

## Consequences

- Positive: session-start cost stays flat regardless of content size; the index
  is omitted entirely (zero cost) when no rules exist.
- Negative: the agent must make a follow-up `get_memory` call before acting on a
  rule; an agent may act on the summary alone without following up.
- Neutral: `list_rules` compact-by-default / `full=true` opt-in mirrors the
  existing recall-summary convention (ADR engram-ambu).
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Rules are always-shared with server-set immutable visibility; set_visibility rejects rules
description:
## Context

The `rule` memory kind is the single ground-truth invariant set for a repo or
project scope. If an owner could hide an individual rule via `set_visibility`,
two actors reading the same rule scope would see different normative content,
undermining the guarantee that a scope has one authoritative rule set. The
design needed a firm posture on whether a rule's visibility can ever diverge
from `shared`.

## Decision

`visibility=shared` is server-set and immutable for every rule (`category=rule`).
The `set_visibility` MCP handler rejects any call targeting a rule with an
actionable error ("rules are always shared — delete the rule instead"). The
rejection lives in the handler: it reads the record via `GetReadable` (since
`ResolvePointID` returns only the UUID) and runs the category check before the
write-ownership gate, so the actionable message wins over an owner-only
`ErrNotFound`.

## Rationale

- A privately-hidden rule would let two actors see different ground truth in the
  same scope, which defeats the core "one rule set per scope" guarantee.
- Reuses the existing shared-read grant (`ownerOrSharedCondition`, ADR
  engram-kyz) with zero new authorization code.
- Personal exceptions belong in ordinary `preference` memories, not disguised
  private rules.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Always-shared, server-set, immutable (chosen):** single ground truth per
  scope for every reader; reuses ADR engram-kyz; no new authz surface.
- **Default-shared but owner-overridable (rejected):** lets an owner hide a
  specific rule, but a privately-hidden rule fragments the scope's ground truth
  across readers, contradicting "one rule set per scope."

## Consequences

- Positive: single source of truth per scope, unconditionally; no new authz surface.
- Negative: no per-rule privacy short of deletion; the `set_visibility` handler
  must pre-fetch the record (a new `GetReadable` read) to learn the category.
- Neutral: mixed anonymous/authenticated deployments still see different rule
  sets per the existing shared-read posture (unchanged behavior).
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Resolve short_id at the handler layer, not inside store methods
description:
## Context

Every by-id operation (get / update / delete / set_visibility / discovery-replace, plus the Connect GetMemory RPC) must accept either a full UUID or a short_id. The design had to choose whether resolution lives inside the UUID-only store methods or is performed once by each calling handler before invoking those methods unchanged.

## Decision

Add one owner-agnostic Store.ResolvePointID method and call it explicitly from each of the 6 by-id call sites (5 MCP tools + Connect GetMemory) before the existing, unchanged store gates — rather than making the store methods short_id-aware.

## Rationale

- Avoids signature changes to every UUID-only store mutator (Get, GetReadable, Delete, SetVisibility, FetchForUpdate, OwnedOrAbsent).
- Keeps authorization enforcement solely in the existing downstream ownership gates, preserving the engram-xa6 404-not-found invariant (resolution itself is owner-agnostic and leaks nothing a UUID guess would not).
- The trade-off is made explicit: correctness now depends on every by-id call site remembering to resolve first.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Resolve once per handler, then call existing UUID-only store methods (chosen):** store methods and their ownership gates stay unchanged; no signature churn. Cost: resolution is not inherited — each of the 6 call sites must invoke ResolvePointID itself.
- **Resolve inside each store mutator (rejected):** resolution would automatically cover every caller, but requires threading the resolved id back across every UUID-only store method; OwnedOrAbsent (error-only return) in particular could not hand back the resolved id needed by store_discovery's replace path without a signature change.

## Consequences

- Positive: no store method signatures change; ownership gates (GetReadable, OwnedOrAbsent, and the rest) stay untouched.
- Negative: 6 independent call sites each carry the resolve-first obligation; a by-id tool added later that skips ResolvePointID silently reintroduces the raw-UUID-only failure until a short_id is used against it.
- Neutral: resolution applies no authz itself — it only maps a handle to a UUID; the ownership check remains fully downstream.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Encode short_id as 10-char Crockford base32
description:
## Context

Memory records need a short, pasteable handle because agents were hand-truncating the 36-char UUID into invalid prefixes that fail at the Qdrant boundary. The handle must be short, fixed-length, and resistant to LLM copy errors; no ordering semantics are wanted. ULID and Sqids were evaluated as alternative encodings before settling on Crockford base32.

## Decision

short_id is a 10-char lowercase Crockford base32 token (~50 bits of entropy), not a ULID and not a Sqids-encoded integer. Generation draws uniformly from crypto/rand; lookup canonicalizes input (i/l→1, o→0, lowercase) before an exact-match filter.

## Rationale

- ULID's only distinguishing feature (time-sortability) is explicitly unwanted, and at 26 chars it is barely shorter than a UUID.
- Sqids encodes integers reversibly — a problem this design does not have; using it would require minting and plumbing a random integer per record, wasting its reversibility and adding a dependency for no benefit.
- Crockford's alphabet (case-insensitive, no ambiguous 0/O or 1/I/L) directly targets the observed failure mode: ambiguous glyphs and case drift in LLM-copied tokens.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Crockford base32, 10-char lowercase (chosen):** same length class as the alternatives with case-insensitivity and an unambiguous alphabet; needs a write-time uniqueness check and lookup-time canonicalization.
- **ULID (rejected):** 26 chars (negligible gain over UUID); only edge is unwanted sortability; de-ordered it is just a base32 token.
- **Sqids (rejected):** encodes integers, not random tokens; reversibility is wasted here and it adds a dependency.

## Consequences

- Positive: a fixed-length handle removes the truncation temptation that caused the original bug; case/glyph-tolerant lookup absorbs common LLM copy errors.
- Negative: every lookup needs Crockford canonicalization before the exact-filter match; the write path needs a collision check-and-retry loop.
- Neutral: no ordering/sortability semantics — created_at already covers that (PR #253).
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs
