title: Validate data-plane fields only; listen_addr is a serve-local guard
description:
## Context

All engram commands (serve, reindex, migrate, prune) load the same Config struct. Some fields are universal data-plane fields consumed by every command (qdrant.addr, qdrant.collection, embed.model, embed.dim, openai.base_url); others are serve-specific (server.listen_addr), optional (openai.api_key, oidc.*, ui.*), or handled by subsystems (log.*). A shared Config.Validate run at every entrypoint must not trip admin commands on config they do not use.

## Decision

Config.Validate checks exactly five universal data-plane fields: qdrant.addr (host:port, port 1-65535), qdrant.collection (non-empty), embed.model (non-empty), embed.dim (uint > 0), openai.base_url (non-empty, http/https URL). server.listen_addr is guarded by a one-line non-empty check in runServe only. Optional fields (openai.api_key) and subsystem- or elsewhere-validated fields (oidc.*, ui.*, log.*) are excluded.

## Rationale

- Every command consumes the five data-plane fields, so validating them universally is always correct.
- listen_addr is serve-specific and has a flag that can force-empty it (--listen-addr "" silently binds :http); admin commands bind no listener, so coupling them to it would be artificial.
- Excluding optional and subsystem-validated fields avoids penalizing local Ollama deployments that need no API key, and avoids double-validating OIDC/UI creds already checked by resolveUIConfig.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Data-plane fields only, with a serve-local listen_addr guard (chosen):** admin commands pass with a minimal valid config; the listen_addr footgun is caught locally in runServe where the context is clear.
- **Validate all non-optional fields including serve-local ones (rejected):** reindex/migrate/prune would fail validation on listen_addr even though they never bind a listener — artificial coupling between admin commands and serve-specific config.

## Consequences

- Positive: admin commands never fail on serve-specific config they do not consume; the validated field set is stable and enumerated in one place.
- Negative: listen_addr validation lives in runServe, not Config.Validate — a reader checks two locations for the full validation surface.
- Neutral: Validate intentionally applies stricter rules than its consumers (port range 1-65535; http/https scheme) to turn late or opaque failures into early, named startup errors.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Keep config.Load assembly-only; validate via a separate Config.Validate()
description:
## Context

engram's config pipeline uses koanf to assemble a typed Config struct (registry defaults, then the ENGRAM_ env layer, then a changed-flags overlay). Validation rules (addr parsing, dim parsing, URL well-formedness) were scattered across StoreFromEnvNoEnsure, EmbedderFromEnv, and resolveUIConfig, each with different error shapes and timing. A prior decision (engram-edv, closed wontfix) established that config.Load panics on a malformed koanf layer because that signals a programming error; operator config typos must surface as returned errors, never panics.

## Decision

config.Load remains assembly-only and never validates operator config values. Well-formedness is checked by a separate, pure Config.Validate() method invoked from the startup / store-construction path, not folded into Load. (The exact call site — a single choke point in StoreFromEnvNoEnsure that covers serve, reindex, migrate, and prune — is an implementation detail settled in the plan.)

## Rationale

- Preserves the Load invariant that justifies EmbedderFromEnv's panic-on-Load-error (engram-edv): a Load error means a malformed koanf layer (a programming error), never operator input.
- Operator misconfiguration must produce ordinary returned errors, never panics — folding validation into Load would conflate the two failure modes.
- A pure Validate function is independently testable with table-driven unit tests and carries no I/O risk.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Separate explicit Config.Validate() after Load (chosen):** preserves Load's invariant and EmbedderFromEnv's panic contract; pure and exhaustively testable.
- **Fold validation into config.Load (rejected):** breaks the "Load only fails on a malformed koanf layer" invariant; would reopen engram-edv by reclassifying EmbedderFromEnv's panic; conflates programming-error vs operator-misconfiguration failure modes.

## Consequences

- Positive: clear semantic boundary (Load = assembly, Validate = correctness); Validate is pure (no I/O) and exhaustively unit-testable; EmbedderFromEnv's panic contract remains valid and untouched.
- Negative: every store-building path must reach Validate (mitigated by the single choke point plus per-path tests).
- Neutral: the existing double-config.Load in serve is a known wart, not entangled by this decision and left as a separate follow-up.
notes: addendum: As of PR #186 (bead engram-mbnw, merged 2026-06-23) the exported EmbedderFromEnv function was removed — its sole production caller, the reindex command, now builds the embedder via the new server.StoreAndEmbedderFromEnvNoEnsure, which loads+validates config once through loadAndValidate and returns errors. The references in Rationale / Alternatives / Consequences to 'EmbedderFromEnv's panic-on-Load-error' as a live, preserved contract are therefore HISTORICAL: that panic site no longer exists, and the reindex embedder path now surfaces a config.Load error as a RETURNED error (consistent with buildDepsFromEnv for serve) rather than panicking. The core decision is UNCHANGED and still holds: config.Load stays assembly-only and Config.Validate() remains the separate validation step. The engram-edv rationale (a Load error means a malformed koanf layer = programming error) also still holds — it is simply no longer surfaced via a panic on the reindex path.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Centralized config validation (Config.Validate)
description: Deferred from PR #139 finding engram-ii6.6 (important). config.Load empty-env-preserves-default matches retired EnvOr semantics (no regression). Reviewer suggests a startup pass failing loudly when required non-flag fields (ENGRAM_QDRANT_ADDR, ENGRAM_OPENAI_BASE_URL) resolve to empty. Behavior change beyond rename scope; needs a required-vs-optional field policy.
design:
Needs a short spec/ADR before implementation — defines a required-vs-optional config-field policy. Open questions to resolve in design:
1. Required-field set: ENGRAM_QDRANT_ADDR and ENGRAM_OPENAI_BASE_URL are candidates, but both carry non-empty registry defaults and only resolve empty if forced via a changed CLI flag (the flag overlay bypasses config.Load's empty-preserves-default guard). So 'required' really means 'reject explicitly-emptied'. Confirm the set.
2. ENGRAM_OPENAI_API_KEY: required or optional? Local Ollama/no-auth embedders need no key — likely optional. Decide.
3. Validation location: config.Load is shared by serve, reindex, migrate. Put the check in serve startup (not Load) so admin commands don't fail on unrelated empties. Confirm.
4. Error shape: fail-fast with a clear 'required config X is empty' message at startup.
notes:
Decision (Sean, 2026-06-14): worth doing, but design/spec required first — do NOT drain as-is. Blocked pending the required-vs-optional policy above. edv (sibling finding) closed wontfix.
grounding/probe registry.go: qdrant.addr (default localhost:6334) and openai.base_url (default http://localhost:4000) have NO Flag and a non-empty Default. With config.Load's empty-env-preserves-default TransformFunc, neither can resolve to empty via env, and with no flag they can't be force-emptied either. The bead's named 'required non-flag fields' are effectively unreachable-empty.
grounding/probe tools.go StoreFromEnvNoEnsure: qdrant.addr is ALREADY fail-fast validated — net.SplitHostPort(cfg.Qdrant.Addr) + strconv.Atoi(port) error on empty/malformed at serve startup ('invalid ENGRAM_QDRANT_ADDR'). embed.dim ALREADY validated via strconv.ParseUint. So empty/garbage qdrant.addr/dim are NOT silent today.
grounding/probe serve.go: UI/OIDC cred emptiness already handled by resolveUIConfig (fail-fast). Residual genuinely-unguarded risks: (a) openai.base_url empty -> fails at first embed HTTP call, not startup (but unreachable-empty); (b) server.listen_addr has a flag so --listen-addr '' CAN force empty -> http.Server binds ':http' silently. Both low-likelihood.
Scope decision (Sean): Option C — broader config validation. Build a single Config.Validate() run at startup with uniform aggregated errors, centralizing well-formedness (qdrant addr/collection, embed model/dim, openai base_url). Supersedes the narrow empty-only framing.

Reviewer verified all grounding claims true against code. Next: writing-plans.

title: TestResolveUIConfigUIIssuerOverrides does not assert got.Enabled, leaving implied-on path untested
description:
File: cmd/engram/uiconfig_test.go, TestResolveUIConfigUIIssuerOverrides (lines 57-68).

The old table-driven test had an explicit case: 'creds present, flag unset -> on (UI issuer defaults to MCP issuer)' that asserted wantOn: true. The replacement test TestResolveUIConfigUIIssuerOverrides passes Enabled: "" (zero value) with full creds, but only asserts got.Issuer — it does not assert got.Enabled == true. This means the 'creds present with no explicit Enabled flag → UI activates' path (the implied-on semantics) is no longer directly verified by any test.

The fix is a one-line addition:

  if !got.Enabled || got.Issuer != "https://ui" {
      t.Errorf(...)
  }

This is a clarity/maintainability finding: the missing assertion means the spec's implied-on rule (present creds without explicit 'true' activate the UI) could regress silently. The function itself is correct; the test coverage gap is what's filed here.

title: C-6: Padded struct doc comments restate field names in internal/config/config.go
description:
Pattern C-6 (padded docstring): five of the seven new *Config type comments in internal/config/config.go add no information beyond the type name and field names.

Affected lines (all in the new file, internal/config/config.go):
- ServerConfig (line 11): 'holds the HTTP server settings (listen address, MCP mount path)' — restates fields ListenAddr and MCPPath.
- QdrantConfig (line 17): 'holds the Qdrant connection address and memory collection name' — restates fields Addr and Collection.
- EmbedConfig (line 23): 'holds the embedding model name and its vector dimension' — restates fields Model and Dim.
- LogConfig (line 44): 'holds the logging level, format, and stdout toggle' — restates fields Level, Format, Stdout.

All four comments state exactly and only what reading the struct definition already conveys. They appear in a uniform pattern across all seven structs (uniform comment density across trivially-named fields), which is a C-6 tell.

OIDCConfig and UIConfig comments do add some genuine value (grouping context about MCP bearer lane vs web-UI credentials) and are not implicated.

Fix: delete the four restating comments (ServerConfig, QdrantConfig, EmbedConfig, LogConfig) or replace with something non-trivial (e.g. a note about why Dim is string, or the invariant that empty string preserves the registry default). Either way, a careful human author would not commit four consecutive godoc lines that say nothing beyond the field names.
close_reason: Deferred to engram-lp1 (moved out of review epic)

title: registry field struct uses positional literals, breaking single-source-of-truth invariant on field reorder
description:
File: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/drain-epic-engram-xv9/internal/config/registry.go, lines 25-46.

The field struct (Key, Env, Legacy, Flag, Default) is initialized using positional struct literals across all 20 registry entries, e.g.:

  {"server.listen_addr", "ENGRAM_LISTEN_ADDR", "MEM_LISTEN_ADDR", "listen-addr", ":8080"}

This is directly at odds with the stated purpose of the registry as the single source of truth. If a new field is inserted into the struct definition — say, a Description string after Key — every registry entry compiles without error but with every field shifted right by one (Env receives the Legacy value, Legacy receives the Flag name, etc.). The bug is entirely silent at compile time and produces nonsense env-var mappings at runtime.

Since field has five fields of the same type (string), Go has no positional-vs-keyed safety net here; the compiler accepts both forms.

Suggested fix: switch all registry entries to keyed literals:

  {
    Key:     "server.listen_addr",
    Env:     "ENGRAM_LISTEN_ADDR",
    Legacy:  "MEM_LISTEN_ADDR",
    Flag:    "listen-addr",
    Default: ":8080",
  },

This is a one-time mechanical change and golangci-lint's exhaustruct linter (or govet's -composites check) can enforce it going forward.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #139 (review-gate PASS); see commit 'test,docs(config): address PR #139 review findings'

title: config_test.go: TestLoadDefaults does not isolate from ambient ENGRAM_* env vars
description:
internal/config/config_test.go — TestLoadDefaults calls Load(nil) without clearing ENGRAM_* variables from the process environment first. If CI or the developer's shell has any ENGRAM_OPENAI_BASE_URL, ENGRAM_EMBED_MODEL, or ENGRAM_LISTEN_ADDR set (plausible given they are commonly configured for local dev), the assertions compare against the env value rather than the registry default, producing a false-passing test for the wrong value. The same applies to TestLoadEnvOverridesDefault: it does not ensure other ENGRAM_* vars from the ambient environment don't interfere with unverified fields.

Suggested fix: Add t.Setenv calls to clear the three keys the test checks (and ideally all ENGRAM_* vars that have defaults) before calling Load(nil). Example:
  t.Setenv("ENGRAM_OPENAI_BASE_URL", "")
  t.Setenv("ENGRAM_EMBED_MODEL", "")
  t.Setenv("ENGRAM_LISTEN_ADDR", "")

This ensures the test is asserting registry defaults and not an ambient override. The koanf TransformFunc already converts empty strings to no-ops (preserving defaults), so clearing with t.Setenv("") is the correct approach.

title: StoreFromEnvNoEnsure returns bare config.Load error without callsite context
description: In internal/server/tools.go, StoreFromEnvNoEnsure (around line 59-62), when config.Load(nil) fails, the error is returned bare: 'return nil, 0, err'. Every other error return in this same function wraps with context (fmt.Errorf("invalid ENGRAM_EMBED_DIM..."), fmt.Errorf("invalid ENGRAM_QDRANT_ADDR..."), fmt.Errorf("qdrant client: %w"...)). The config.Load errors internally wrap their cause (e.g. 'config defaults: ...', 'config env: ...', 'config unmarshal: ...'), so the error chain is not empty, but the callsite (StoreFromEnvNoEnsure) provides no framing. A diagnostician seeing 'config env: ...' in a reindex failure has no indication it came from StoreFromEnvNoEnsure. Fix: wrap with fmt.Errorf("store config: %w", err).

title: Breaking config renames ship with a fatal legacy-env startup guard
description:
## Context

Renaming env vars pre-1.0 is cheap by release-please's minor-bump policy, but a *silent* rename — where the old var is ignored and the server falls back to a default — is a dangerous footgun: a partially-migrated deploy silently uses wrong embeddings or connects to the wrong Qdrant instance with no error signal. The same problem recurs for any future hard break.

## Decision

`config.CheckLegacy()` runs at root `PersistentPreRunE` and fails fast and **fatally** when any retired `MEM_*` var is present in the environment, printing the exact `old → new` mapping. There is no dual-read shim. The guard is derived from the same field registry as the config loader, so it cannot drift from the actual renames, and it is deleted at 1.0 by removing the registry's `Legacy` column.

## Rationale

- Pre-1.0 hard breaks are cheap (release-please minor bump); a dual-read shim would keep the leaked/confusing names alive indefinitely for no long-term gain.
- A fatal guard converts "silently wrong embed results" into an immediate, operator-actionable error with the exact rename instructions.
- `PersistentPreRunE` scope covers every subcommand (`serve`, `reindex`, `migrate-set-owner`, `prune-expired`), all of which share the same env surface.
- A registry-derived guard cannot drift from the actual renames; removing the `Legacy` column at 1.0 deletes the guard with zero residual debt.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Dual-read shim (accept both old and new names)** — zero-downtime, backward compatible, but keeps the leaked names alive indefinitely, doubles the documented/tested surface, and must be removed eventually anyway. Rejected.
- **Warning log only (non-fatal)** — operators see the message without a hard stop, but warnings are routinely ignored in production and the silent-fallback footgun is only partially mitigated; a misconfigured deploy can run silently wrong for days. Rejected.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** no silent misconfiguration is possible — wrong deploys fail immediately with actionable output; establishes a reusable policy that hard breaks in engram must be loud, never silent fallbacks; the guard self-destructs at 1.0 by design.
- **Negative:** partially-migrated deploys hard-fail at startup; operators must rename all vars before restarting.
- **Neutral:** `root.Execute()` already prints `Error: <msg>` and exits non-zero, so `PersistentPreRunE` integrates cleanly with no extra plumbing.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Name embedder connection vars by protocol, not implementation
description:
## Context

`MEM_LITELLM_URL` and `MEM_LITELLM_KEY` baked a specific proxy product (LiteLLM) into public env var names, even though the server only ever required an **OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` endpoint**. Ollama, vLLM, TEI, and OpenAI itself all speak the same wire protocol. The name confused readers of the code and docs and tied a generic project to one operator's homelab topology.

## Decision

Rename the embedder connection vars to `ENGRAM_OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `ENGRAM_OPENAI_API_KEY`, where "OpenAI" names the **wire protocol** (the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` API), not the vendor. The embedder model/dimension vars keep the `ENGRAM_EMBED_` stem (`ENGRAM_EMBED_MODEL`, `ENGRAM_EMBED_DIM`).

## Rationale

- Mirrors the OpenAI SDK's own canonical env vars (`OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`), giving operators a familiar mental model; the SDK documents `base_url` as the mechanism for OpenAI-compatible APIs.
- "OpenAI" in the var name describes the protocol; the docs make explicit that any compatible backend (Ollama, vLLM, TEI, OpenAI, LiteLLM) is valid.
- Two clean families: `ENGRAM_OPENAI_*` is the protocol connection; `ENGRAM_EMBED_*` is engram's embedding choice. The OpenAI SDK has no env var for model, so grouping model under `OPENAI_` would invent a non-standard name.
- `embed.New`'s signature is already provider-neutral (`baseURL, apiKey, model`); only call sites and var names change.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep `MEM_LITELLM_URL` / `MEM_LITELLM_KEY`** — no migration cost, but leaks an operator-specific implementation detail into a generic project's public interface and confuses users not running LiteLLM. Rejected.
- **`ENGRAM_EMBED_URL` / `ENGRAM_EMBED_KEY` (fully generic stem)** — no vendor association at all, but does not align with the established OpenAI SDK canonical var names, sacrificing discoverability for users who already know `OPENAI_BASE_URL`. Rejected.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** the public interface no longer exposes an operator-specific implementation detail; any OpenAI-compatible backend is a first-class citizen without renaming; alignment with OpenAI SDK canonical vars aids discoverability.
- **Negative:** breaking rename for all existing deployments using `MEM_LITELLM_*` (mitigated by the legacy guard); the `OPENAI_` prefix may still suggest vendor lock-in to uninformed readers, so docs must clarify it names the protocol.
- **Neutral:** `embed.New`'s signature is unchanged; impact is limited to call sites and env var names.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Unify config under ENGRAM_ prefix via koanf internal/config
description:
## Context

Engram's 23 env vars carried a `MEM_*` prefix — a vestige of a prior name — inconsistent with the binary, Helm chart, skill, and brand. Config reads were scattered across `server.EnvOr`, getenv closures in `cmd/engram`, and `internal/telemetry/config.go`, with no single registry, making renames expensive and drift-prone. The project mandates cobra with **no viper**; koanf is the lightweight, modular realization of the required env-first + flag-override layered model.

## Decision

Introduce `internal/config` (koanf v2) with a single field registry as the sole owner of all `ENGRAM_*` keys, their defaults, the env→koanf-path transform, and the legacy-env guard. Config is loaded as koanf layers — registry defaults, then the `ENGRAM_` env layer, then a changed-CLI-flags overlay — and unmarshalled into a typed nested `*Config`. Env-only consumers call `config.Load(nil)`; `serve` passes `cmd.Flags()`. Retire `server.EnvOr`.

## Rationale

- koanf is the lightweight, modular realization of the project's existing env-first + flag-override requirement without viper.
- A single field registry makes renames a one-line edit; the env transform, defaults, and legacy guard all derive from it and cannot drift.
- An explicit env→key-path mapping (not a blind `_`→`.` rewrite) prevents over-splitting (e.g. `BASE_URL` → `base.url`).
- A changed-flag-only overlay gives flags-override-env precedence while never letting an unset flag clobber an env value — the property the PR #105 UI-issuer fix had to hand-roll.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Keep scattered EnvOr / getenv reads, rename in place** — minimal diff, no new dependency, but every future rename touches every call site and the key catalogue has no single owner; transform/defaults/guard drift is unchecked. Rejected.
- **Adopt viper** — widely known, built-in env+flag+file, but explicitly prohibited by CLAUDE.md's cobra/no-viper convention. Rejected.

## Consequences

- **Positive:** all config keys owned in one place; future renames are one-line registry edits; consumers receive a typed nested `*Config` with no ambient getenv calls; changed-flag-only override is correct by construction.
- **Negative:** new koanf v2 dependency; all existing `EnvOr`/getenv call sites must migrate to consume `*config.Config`.
- **Neutral:** CLI flag names are unchanged (only env-based deployments migrate); a file-based config provider is out of scope but possible later.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Bump esbuild to >=0.28.1 in docs-site (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr)
description: Dependabot HIGH: esbuild <0.28.1 (transitive via astro/vite) in docs-site/pnpm-lock.yaml — build-time RCE via malicious NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY in esbuild's Deno module. Pre-exists epic engram-45i; surfaced by the PR #133 review (engram-o8e.1) but out of scope for that docs-content PR. Fix: pnpm update esbuild (or add an override) in docs-site/, verify build, separate PR.
notes:
Root cause: esbuild <0.28.1 (GHSA-gv7w-rqvm-qjhr, build-time RCE via malicious NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY) was pulled into docs-site transitively at TWO versions — 0.27.7 (vite, via astro) and 0.27.3 (wrangler, exact pin). 'pnpm update esbuild' CANNOT fix it: vite declares esbuild ^0.27.0 (=>=0.27.0 <0.28.0 on a 0.x dep), so 0.28.1 is out of range — the candidate-fix hypothesis was wrong; an override is the actual remediation.

Fix (docs-site/, separate change): pnpm overrides { esbuild: ^0.28.1 } in pnpm-workspace.yaml forces both consumers to 0.28.1 (latest GA). Per user directive, also bumped all docs-site deps to latest GA: astro ^6.4.6->^6.4.8 (6.4.8 is latest GA; astro 7.x is alpha/beta only), sharp ^0.35.0->^0.35.2, wrangler 4.101.0->4.103.0 (which ships esbuild 0.28.1 natively, so the override only forces vite now). @astrojs/starlight already at latest GA 0.40.0. astro 6.4.8 still resolves vite 7.3.5 (esbuild ^0.27.0), so the override remains required.

Supply-chain note: sharp 0.35.2 + wrangler 4.103.0 were <36h old at bump time, so pnpm appended them + 26 @img/sharp-* platform binaries + miniflare to minimumReleaseAgeExclude in pnpm-workspace.yaml (documented pattern; CI doesn't enforce the age gate). Trades a noisier exclude list for latest-GA pins.

Verified: rg shows NO esbuild <0.28.1 left in pnpm-lock.yaml (only 0.28.1); 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile' (CI step 1) = Already up to date; 'pnpm build' (astro build, CI step 2) = green, 12 pages. Diff = 3 files (package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, pnpm-workspace.yaml). docs-site/ is yamlfmt-excluded + license-header paths-ignored, so no other gate touched.
UPDATE (final, supersedes the latest-GA-as-is note above): per operator choice, trimmed the age-gate bypass. sharp 0.35.2->0.35.1 and wrangler kept at 4.101.0 (both gate-clean, >36h), so NO <36h entries were added to minimumReleaseAgeExclude — that list is back to trunk's contents (only astro@6.4.6->6.4.8 pin updated). Kept: esbuild ^0.28.1 override + astro ^6.4.8 (latest GA). wrangler's esbuild 0.27.3 is forced to 0.28.1 by the override (wrangler runs esbuild only at deploy, never in astro build). Final diff = 3 files: package.json (astro ^6.4.8, sharp ^0.35.1), pnpm-workspace.yaml (+overrides block only), pnpm-lock.yaml (net -260 lines: two esbuild 0.27.x collapse to one 0.28.1). Re-verified: NO esbuild <0.28.1 in lockfile; frozen-lockfile install + astro build both green (12 pages). Gotcha learned: 'rm pnpm-lock.yaml && pnpm install' does a FRESH latest-resolve that grabs sharp 0.35.2 (then the age gate rejects it, writing no lockfile) — the correct minimal path is 'jj restore --from trunk() docs-site/pnpm-lock.yaml' then a plain (conservative) 'pnpm install', which keeps gate-clean 0.35.1 and applies only the override+astro bump.

title: RunCommand: btn.textContent capture includes whitespace, restoring trimmed text would differ
description:
In docs-site/src/components/landing/RunCommand.astro, the copy-button script captures the original label at line 51:

  const originalText = btn.textContent ?? 'Copy';

The button markup (line 10-13) contains the text node with surrounding whitespace:
  <button ...>
    Copy
  </button>

In most browsers btn.textContent will be '\n      Copy\n    ' (the raw text node), not 'Copy'. After the click handler sets btn.textContent = 'Copied' and later restores it to originalText, the label restores correctly visually (browsers collapse whitespace for display) but the DOM text node is inconsistently whitespace-padded vs the 'Copied' value.

A simpler and more explicit approach: hardcode the label constant or trim it:
  const originalText = btn.textContent?.trim() ?? 'Copy';

This is a minor clarity issue rather than a visible bug, but the current code is easy to misread as capturing a clean 'Copy' string when it does not.

File: docs-site/src/components/landing/RunCommand.astro:51
close_reason: Won't fix (non-issue): the handler restores the exact captured originalText incl. its whitespace, so the label round-trips correctly; trimming is unnecessary.

title: RunCommand copy button missing explicit :focus-visible rule (WCAG 2.4.7)
description:
File: docs-site/src/components/landing/RunCommand.astro

The spec (Accessibility & correctness section) states the Copy button must have an accessible name and a visible 'Copied' confirmation. The accessible name is present (aria-label). However, .lp-run-copy has no explicit :focus-visible rule.

The epic lessons (engram-45i) explicitly record: 'custom landing card-link components that set text-decoration:none + a :hover affordance MUST also add a :focus-visible rule — the site CSS has NO global a:focus-visible outline for landing content (WCAG 2.4.7).' FeatureCards and PathCards (both <a> elements) correctly implement :focus-visible. The copy button is a <button> element which retains a UA-provided default focus ring, so this is not a hard WCAG failure — but the landing page has a CSS reset pattern that suppresses default styling, and consistency with the focus-visible treatment applied to the other two interactive elements is missing.

Suggested fix in RunCommand.astro:
  .lp-run-copy:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--sl-color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }
close_reason: Fixed: added .lp-run-copy:focus-visible (2px accent ring), consistent with the cards.

title: cat-discovery reuses exact retired GitHub-green hex values from brand spec palette swap
description:
File: ui/src/app.css lines 16, 28

The brand spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-13-engram-brand-identity-design.md, palette table) explicitly retired #1a7f37 (light) and #3fb950 (dark) as 'borrowed GitHub greens' from --primary/--ring. The --cat-discovery token introduced in this PR uses those exact same hex values.

No ADR or spec text explicitly prohibits reusing these values for category tokens, and green is a genuinely distinct hue from the rest of the palette (violet/blue/orange/magenta), so the bead's 'distinct hue' requirement is technically satisfied. However, reusing the exact retired-primary hex for a new semantic token introduces a semantic collision risk: any reader of app.css who knows the brand history may assume --cat-discovery is the old primary leaking back in. The spec language is 'replaces the borrowed GitHub greens' -- using them for a different token reintroduces Primer green as a first-class palette entry under a different name.

Suggested fix: choose a green that is not the Primer green pair -- e.g. a more saturated or teal-shifted green that is clearly distinct from the retired primary while still reading as 'discovery/exploration'. This avoids false positives in any future grep for the retired hex values and keeps the 'retired GitHub greens' retirement clean.
close_reason: Fixed: retuned --cat-discovery to teal #0d9488/#2dd4bf, off the retired GitHub greens #1a7f37/#3fb950.

title: hardcoded category list in app.css.test.ts is not derived from the Category type in queries.ts
description: ui/src/app.css.test.ts line 23 hard-codes the category list as ['convention', 'gotcha', 'decision', 'preference', 'discovery']. The authoritative definition of the four memory categories lives in ui/src/lib/queries.ts (the Category type / CATEGORIES const). The fifth entry, 'discovery', is a render-only category not in that type. There is no compile-time or runtime link between the two: adding a fifth Category to queries.ts (e.g. 'observation') would require a matching CSS token and a test update, but neither is enforced. The test would stay green while the new category renders with a transparent dot. The test comment explains why the CSS cannot be imported (Tailwind/vite empties it), but the category list itself could be extracted to a shared constant (e.g. a RENDERABLE_CATEGORIES const in a shared module or in the test itself referencing queries.ts) so that a future addition cannot be silently missed. Criticality: 4 — no immediate regression, but a maintenance trap that will reproduce the exact bug this PR fixes if a new category is added.
close_reason: Fixed: exported CATEGORIES from queries.ts; test now derives RENDERABLE_CATEGORIES = [...CATEGORIES, 'discovery'] from the source of truth.

title: Gate dashboard category-breakdown bar on a listScopes API extension
description:
## Context

The operator-console dashboard was mocked with a per-scope category-breakdown bar (stacked proportions of convention/gotcha/decision/preference). The existing listScopes RPC (ui/src/routes/+page.svelte) returns only {scope, count} — no per-category breakdown is available without a backend change. The brand-identity round is presentation-only.

## Decision

The category-breakdown bar is dropped from the dashboard; the dashboard shows scope-id (via ScopeChip), a count pill, and a violet accent stripe only. Exposing per-category counts (a listScopes response extension or a new endpoint) is deferred to a future bead.

## Rationale

listScopes returning {scope, count} is the binding contract; the UI cannot fabricate per-category proportions without real data. Rendering placeholder/empty bars would mislead operators and undermine the explicit, zero-junk design intent of the memory contract. Any future category-breakdown UI thus requires a corresponding listScopes API extension, decoupling it from this brand/visual round.

## Alternatives Considered

(1) Drop the bar, count-only (CHOSEN): no backend change, ships within presentation-only scope, no dummy data. (2) Extend listScopes / add a per-category-counts endpoint: enables the richer dashboard but couples a visual PR to a backend API change and expands review surface. (3) Client-side aggregation via search/list calls: N+1 per scope, prohibitively expensive, wrong data layer for a summary.

## Consequences

POSITIVE: dashboard PR ships presentation-only with no backend review burden; the API gap is documented as a clear future bead scope. NEGATIVE: dashboard is less information-dense than the mockup — category distribution requires navigating to Observe. NEUTRAL: the promoted category palette (dots/chips) still appears in Observe + memory list/detail; the dashboard is the only surface that loses a category signal.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Ship engram wordmark as outlined SVG paths, not a webfont
description:
## Context

The engram brand lockup renders a distinctive wordmark in the header of the embedded SvelteKit SPA (vendored into the Go binary via go:embed, ADR engram-0lu) and on the Astro/Starlight docs site. Any external font fetch introduces a network dependency, FOUT risk, and bundle weight that the self-contained SPA design explicitly avoids.

## Decision

The engram wordmark is shipped as outlined SVG paths embedded in the lockup SVG asset (brand/engram-lockup.svg, copied into ui/src/lib/assets/ and inlined via a ?raw import in BrandMark.svelte), NOT as live webfont text. UI and docs body typography are unaffected.

## Rationale

Preserves the self-contained-SPA guarantee from engram-0lu — no font fetch, no runtime network dependency for brand rendering. The identical lockup SVG is reused by both the SPA and the docs site, eliminating per-surface font-loading config. Brand type is distinct from UI/body type; outlined paths make that boundary explicit in the asset tree.

## Alternatives Considered

(1) Live webfont (woff2 at runtime): editable as real text but adds a fetch + FOUT and violates engram-0lu self-containment. (2) System/generic sans fallback: no extra assets but no brand differentiation and OS-variant rendering. (3) Outlined SVG paths (CHOSEN): zero network dependency, no FOUT, identical cross-surface render; cost is that wordmark edits need vector tooling.

## Consequences

POSITIVE: SPA renders correctly in air-gapped/restricted-network deployments with no extra config; no FOUT on the header lockup (mark + wordmark on first paint). NEGATIVE: wordmark edits require SVG path tooling not a font swap; a typeface change means regenerating the lockup SVG. NEUTRAL: body/UI typography on both surfaces is managed independently and unaffected.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Reindex span omits engram.skipped on success, hiding skip-heavy migrations in traces
description:
File: internal/store/store.go — Reindex deferred telemetry block (lines ~1196-1201)

The success branch of the deferred span closure records engram.scanned and engram.upserted but not engram.skipped:

    span.SetAttributes(
        attribute.Int64("engram.scanned",  int64(res.Scanned)),
        attribute.Int64("engram.upserted", int64(res.Upserted)),
    )

ReindexResult.Skipped was introduced in this same PR as a first-class result field, and the CLI output reports it. Operators using distributed traces (e.g. Grafana Tempo) cannot distinguish a clean run from one where a large share of points were silently skipped (no content) because the span carries no evidence of skipped points.

Suggested fix: add attribute.Int64("engram.skipped", int64(res.Skipped)) to the same SetAttributes call.
close_reason: Fixed: engram.skipped added to Reindex success span attributes

title: Reindex doc-comment 'owner==""' anonymous-bucket claim conflates missing-owner with empty-owner
description:
File: internal/store/store.go, Reindex doc-comment lines 1168-1172 (in diff).

The comment states:
  'does NOT synthesize an owner key on a pre-isolation record — a Memory round-trip
   would write owner=="" and silently drop it into the anonymous bucket.'

The intent is correct but the phrasing conflates two distinct states:
- Pre-isolation records: *missing* the 'owner' key entirely (invisible to all reads per CLAUDE.md)
- Anonymous bucket: records with owner=="" (readable by unauthenticated callers)

A Memory round-trip of a missing-owner point would produce owner=="" (GetStringValue returns "" for a missing key), which moves the record from 'invisible' to 'anonymous bucket' — a silent promotion of visibility, not just a semantic label change. The comment says 'drop it into the anonymous bucket' which could mislead a reader into thinking this is a safe no-op (the record was already visible), when in fact it changes the record's visibility from none to world-readable-by-unauthenticated-callers.

Suggested wording clarification: replace 'drop it into the anonymous bucket' with 'promote it from invisible (missing owner key) into the anonymous bucket (owner==""), making it world-readable by unauthenticated callers'.

title: No per-batch progress output during reindex — only final summary printed
description:
The acceptance criterion 'Progress/count output' is only partially met. The reindex command emits a single final line after the entire operation completes (cmd/engram/reindex.go:86-87). For a large collection with a remote embedder, the operator sees no feedback during the potentially long wall-clock window bounded by --timeout (default 30m). The bead acceptance criteria field explicitly lists 'Progress/count output' as a requirement alongside the other items that are fully implemented. GitHub issue #117 frames it as a nice-to-have, but the bead's ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA section elevates it to required scope.

Evidence:
- cmd/engram/reindex.go:81-88: only two Printf calls, both after st.Reindex() returns
- internal/store/store.go:1232-1260: the scroll loop accumulates res.Scanned/Upserted but emits nothing; no progress callback or channel is threaded through ReindexOptions

Suggested fix: pass a progress callback (e.g. func(scanned, upserted uint64) in ReindexOptions, or a simple io.Writer) and print a line every N points or after each batch page. Even printing 'processed N/? records...' after each 256-point scroll page would satisfy the criterion and is consistent with the operator-facing design intent. Alternatively, if the project treats this as nice-to-have per issue #117 wording (not per bead acceptance), the bead acceptance field should be updated to reflect that distinction before merge.
close_reason: Deferred to follow-up engram-5xa (suggestion; important findings fixed in PR #123)

title: EmbedFunc callback type vs interface: func type is the right seam here, but nil-check is the only guard
description:
File: internal/store/store.go (line 1138), internal/store/store.go (line 1204)

EmbedFunc is defined as a function type (func(ctx context.Context, content string) ([]float32, error)) rather than a single-method interface. The choice is defensible — embed.Client.Embed already has the exact signature, the test supplies a bare function literal (embed4), and the store package correctly stays embedder-agnostic.

However, the only invariant enforced on the EmbedFunc parameter is a nil check in Reindex() (line 1204: 'if embed == nil'). A nil EmbedFunc panics if not caught; a non-nil but semantically broken implementation (e.g., always returns a vector of the wrong length relative to opts.Dim) is not detectable at the type boundary.

The nil check is necessary and present, so this is not a bug. The observation is: if the project ever needs to mock or swap embedders at the store level (beyond test-only function literals), a small interface — type Embedder interface { Embed(ctx context.Context, text string) ([]float32, error) } — would make dependency injection explicit and enable interface-nil safety (interface nil vs concrete nil). embed.Client already satisfies such an interface without modification.

This is a low-urgency suggestion. The current func-type approach is idiomatic Go for a single-method callback; the only real gap is that interface nil-check is marginally safer than func nil-check in some injection patterns. File only if there is an active plan to grow the Embedder abstraction; otherwise leave as-is.
close_reason: Deferred to follow-up engram-5xa (suggestion; important findings fixed in PR #123)

title: reindex --timeout default 30m silently ignored when reindexTimeout==0 branch is unreachable
description: In cmd/engram/reindex.go the flag default for --timeout is 30*time.Minute, so reindexTimeout is never 0 at invocation unless the operator explicitly passes --timeout 0. The guard 'if reindexTimeout > 0' therefore always fires by default, making the "0 disables" semantics non-obvious from the flag help text alone. This is not a breaking change but the help text 'max wall-clock for the reindex (0 disables)' implies a zero-default path that is unreachable without explicit opt-in. Suggestion: document that 0 must be set explicitly, or change the default to 0 and let operators opt in to a bounded run. No consumer contract is broken.

title: ReindexResult missing Skipped counter leaves silent discard of empty-content points unobservable
description:
File: internal/store/store.go (lines 1152-1155, 1237-1244)

ReindexResult carries only Scanned and Upserted. The reindex loop at line 1237 extracts content via p.Payload["content"].GetStringValue() — GetStringValue() returns "" on a missing or non-string key, silently passing an empty string to the embedder. When an embedder accepts empty input without error, Scanned and Upserted both increment, and the operator has no signal that those points were effectively re-embedded with a zero-content vector. When a separately-filed finding (empty-content guard) is addressed by skipping empty-content points, the gap in ReindexResult becomes a real observability hole: Scanned - Upserted would not account for skips, and the operator would have no count of how many points were left behind.

Suggestion: Add a Skipped uint64 field to ReindexResult and increment it whenever a point is not upserted (whether due to empty content, a future filter, or any other skip path). The CLI output in cmd/engram/reindex.go line 86 already formats Upserted/Scanned; a Skipped > 0 warning line costs nothing and closes the observability gap.

This is a type-shape suggestion in scope per the review task; it intentionally does not duplicate the empty-content correctness finding already filed.
close_reason: Fixed: ReindexResult.Skipped added and surfaced in CLI output

title: ReindexOptions: Target and Dim lack smart-constructor enforcement — zero values are silently valid at construction
description:
File: internal/store/store.go (lines 1143-1148, 1195-1207)

ReindexOptions is a plain exported struct with all fields public and zero-valued by default. The two required-by-semantics fields — Target (empty string invalid) and Dim (zero invalid) — carry no compile-time or construction-time guard. Validation is deferred to Reindex() deep inside the call, meaning:

1. A caller can construct ReindexOptions{DryRun: true} and pass it without noticing Target and Dim are zero — the error surfaces only at call time, not at the struct literal.
2. The cmd/engram/reindex.go caller handles the Target check itself (line 47-49) and separately calls Reindex(), creating a split-validation pattern where the CLI and the store each partially validate.

Go idiom for this: either a NewReindexOptions(target string, dim uint64) constructor that returns (ReindexOptions, error) validating those two required fields up front, or keeping the current open-struct approach but documenting clearly that Validate() is called by Reindex (the doc comment does say 'required', which partially mitigates). The current approach is not a bug-enabler today (Reindex() does guard), but it invites future callers to pass a zero-dim options struct and get a runtime error rather than a compile-time or early-call-site error.

Suggestion: Add a NewReindexOptions(target string, dim uint64, opts ...func(*ReindexOptions)) (ReindexOptions, error) constructor, or at minimum a (ReindexOptions).Validate() method the caller can call at the point of construction. The CLI in cmd/engram/reindex.go could then call opts.Validate() immediately after building the struct, unifying the split validation.
close_reason: Deferred to follow-up engram-5xa (suggestion; important findings fixed in PR #123)

title: dialTestClient duplicates testStore's client-dialing boilerplate
description:
File: internal/store/reindex_test.go:40-58 vs internal/store/store_test.go:80-101

dialTestClient (new in this PR) duplicates the skip-check, net.SplitHostPort, strconv.Atoi, and qdrant.NewClient boilerplate that already exists in testStore. The only difference is dialTestClient returns the bare *qdrant.Client while testStore wraps it in a *Store.

This violates DRY within the same package's test helpers. If the Qdrant client construction changes (config options, TLS, etc.), both functions need updating.

Suggested fix: have dialTestClient call the shared dialing logic that testStore also uses, e.g. extract a dialTestQdrant(t) helper that returns *qdrant.Client, and have both dialTestClient and testStore call it.

title: Missing payload key 'content' silently re-embeds empty string
description:
File: internal/store/store.go (Reindex), line ~1237

  content := p.Payload["content"].GetStringValue()

If a point in the source collection has no 'content' key (e.g., a discovery record or a legacy record with a different schema), p.Payload["content"] returns a nil *qdrant.Value and GetStringValue() returns "". The embed function is then called with an empty string, producing a semantically meaningless vector that is silently written to the target.

The 'verbatim payload carry-through' design intent covers unknown keys correctly, but the implicit dependency on 'content' being present (and non-empty) for re-embedding is undocumented and has no guard. A pre-condition check or at minimum a log warning when content is empty would surface this at runtime before writing a junk vector.

Suggested fix:
  content := p.Payload["content"].GetStringValue()
  if content == "" {
      // log/warn: skipping point %s with empty content
      res.Scanned++
      continue
  }
Or return an error so the operator knows which record is problematic.
close_reason: Fixed: Reindex skips empty-content points (no garbage vector) + ReindexResult.Skipped counter; TestReindexSkipsEmptyContent

title: Reindex input-validation guard clauses have no test coverage
description:
Store.Reindex has four fast-fail guard clauses (store.go:1195-1206): empty Target, Target==source, Dim==0, nil embed. None of these are exercised by the test suite. While they are low-risk (they return synchronous errors before touching Qdrant), they are new exported-API contracts. A table-driven unit test covering each guard would be cheap (no Qdrant needed if the store is constructed but guards fire before the first network call — though currently dialTestClient is required). At minimum the 'target==source' guard is worth a test since it protects against silently overwriting the live collection.

title: Add 'engram reindex' — re-embed memories into a new-dimension collection (gh#117)
description: Add a CLI subcommand 'engram reindex [--target <collection>] [--source <collection>] [--dry-run] [--timeout 30m]' that re-embeds every stored memory into a (new-dimension) target collection, enabling embedder/model migration. Today the only migrate verb is migrate-set-owner; switching embedders to a different output dimension currently has no path because Qdrant vector dimension is immutable and cross-model vectors aren't comparable. Memories are fully reconstructable from Qdrant payloads (content + metadata retained), so reindex scrolls source -> re-embeds content with the currently-configured embedder -> upserts (same id, new vector, same payload verbatim) into target, leaving source untouched for operator cutover via MEM_QDRANT_COLLECTION. Tracks GitHub issue #117.
design: Reuses cmd/engram/migrate.go cobra shape (signal.NotifyContext + --timeout). Required building blocks not yet present: (1) Store has no unfiltered scroll-all — List applies ownerScopeFilter and MigrateSetOwner avoids reads entirely; add a paginated ScrollAll primitive returning (id, content, payload) over Qdrant offset cursor. (2) Cross-collection write — Store holds a single 'collection' field and Upsert targets s.collection; add a store.Reindex(ctx, target, embed, dim) method or construct a second store.New(qc, target) sharing the client. (3) Embedder not exposed from env — extract server.EmbedderFromEnv() mirroring StoreFromEnv (buildDepsFromEnv currently builds it unexported and bundled with the store). (4) Document that StoreFromEnv runs EnsureCollection on the source at the new dim — harmless no-op since source exists. Target collection created at MEM_EMBED_DIM, distance Cosine. Fail-closed on embedder error (never write a zero/garbage vector).
acceptance_criteria: engram reindex creates target collection at MEM_EMBED_DIM (Cosine) if absent; re-embeds every source point's content with the configured embedder; upserts same id + new vector + verbatim payload into target; leaves source untouched. --dry-run reports count without writing. --timeout bounds wall-clock and is Ctrl-C cancellable. Embedder errors abort without writing garbage vectors. Progress/count output. Unit/integration test covering round-trip into a second collection.
notes:
Driving use case: move embeddings off contended local ollama to a hosted ZDR embedder, optionally upgrading bge-m3 -> stronger model. Same-model/same-dim swaps need no reindex (just repoint URL); only dimension-changing upgrades need this. Resumable/idempotent (skip points already in target with matching content hash) is a nice-to-have follow-up.
Triage (solving-a-bead Phase 2): approach concrete, single-bead, route to TDD. Design fork resolved by evidence: payload()<->fromPayload() round-trip is LOSSY in an authz-relevant way (a pre-isolation record lacking the owner key returns Owner=='' and would be re-written into the anonymous bucket; newer recall-window keys not_before/not_after add more drift surface). Therefore reindex carries the RAW qdrant payload map verbatim (extract only 'content' for embedding) rather than a Memory round-trip. This keeps *qdrant.Value encapsulated in store, so the implementation is a single store.Reindex(ctx, opts, embedFn) method using s.client against the target collection (candidate #2 'second store.New' discarded; #1 adopted). Pagination via client.ScrollAndOffset (returns next_page_offset). EnsureCollection refactored to an internal named helper so the target can be created at MEM_EMBED_DIM/Cosine. Embedder exposed via new server.EmbedderFromEnv() (extracted from buildDepsFromEnv); store stays embedder-agnostic via the callback. Fail-closed: embed error aborts before any write. --source is a nice-to-have; acceptance requires only --target/--dry-run/--timeout.
IMPLEMENTED (solving-a-bead Phases 3-4, TDD, left in_progress per ADR fhsk-hj3; closure at merge).

Changes:
- internal/store/store.go: new Store.Reindex(ctx, ReindexOptions{Target,Dim,Batch,DryRun}, EmbedFunc) (ReindexResult{Scanned,Upserted}). Scrolls source via client.ScrollAndOffset (paginated cursor, WithVectors=false), re-embeds payload['content'] with the callback, upserts (same id, new vector, RAW payload map verbatim) into target. Fail-closed: embed error aborts before any write. EnsureCollection refactored to delegate to internal ensureCollection(ctx,name,dim) so the target is provisioned at MEM_EMBED_DIM/Cosine.
- internal/server/tools.go: extracted exported EmbedderFromEnv() *embed.Client from buildDepsFromEnv (which now calls it); lets the CLI re-embed with the same configured embedder.
- cmd/engram/reindex.go: 'engram reindex --target <c> [--dry-run] [--timeout 30m]' mirroring prune.go (signal.NotifyContext + timeout). Source = MEM_QDRANT_COLLECTION (StoreFromEnv); target dim = MEM_EMBED_DIM.

Tests (internal/store/reindex_test.go, testcontainer Qdrant): roundtrip proves dim change (3->4), verbatim payload incl. an UNKNOWN key preserved and NO synthesized owner key on a pre-isolation point, source untouched; dry-run writes nothing; embed-error fails closed (0 points written). Note: Qdrant L2-normalizes Cosine vectors on store — test compares against the normalized embedder output.

title: P-9/P-10: hedging voice and tailing negation in Scheduling section
description:
Pattern: P-9 (tailing negation) + P-10 (filler hedge), corroborated by P-5 (em-dash density). File: skill/engram/skills/curating-memory/SKILL.md, new ## Scheduling section.

FINDING:

The added prose deviates from the terse imperative voice that the surrounding skill and its siblings use throughout. Two clustered tells:

1. P-10 — 'Reach for `schedule_memory` instead of `store_memory` when...' The existing skill uses hard imperatives ('Call', 'Use', 'Run', 'Pass'). 'Reach for' is a softening filler that a human editing to match the established voice would cut. Compare: discovering/SKILL.md 'Run `search_discovery` for the area first'; promoting-memory/SKILL.md 'Use the Memory spine scope'. No sibling uses 'Reach for'.

2. P-9 — 'scheduling controls *when* a durable fact is active, and is never a reason to store transient state.' The negative tailing clause restates a constraint already stated positively at the top of the same file ('DO NOT STORE: transient state'). A terse author would omit the restatement or write 'Scheduling controls timing only — the junk taxonomy still applies.' The 'and is never a reason to...' construction is a classic AI hedge that pads around a fact already asserted.

Corroborating: two em-dashes in paragraph 1 (one inside parentheses: '...not_before (RFC3339; hidden from recall until then — deferred reveal)'), where all three sibling skills use zero em-dashes.

SUGGESTED FIX:
- Paragraph 1, sentence 1: 'Use `schedule_memory` instead of `store_memory` when a durable fact should not be recalled yet, or should expire after a point in time.'
- Drop the tailing negation clause; let the existing junk-taxonomy section carry it.
- Replace the nested em-dash inside parentheses with a colon or move to the parenthetical: 'not_before (RFC3339): hidden until then (deferred reveal)'.
close_reason: Fixed: 'Reach for'->'Use'; replaced re-hedge with 'controls when a durable fact is active, not whether it is durable'; trimmed nested-parenthetical em-dashes.

title: SKILL.md omits --older-than DUR flag from engram prune-expired CLI reference
description:
The new Scheduling subsection in skill/engram/skills/curating-memory/SKILL.md (line 57) documents the operator CLI as:

  engram prune-expired

Both canonical sources give the full form with its optional flag:
- CLAUDE.md (line 72): engram prune-expired [--older-than DUR]
- docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md (line 77): engram prune-expired [--older-than DUR]
- cmd/engram/prune.go confirms: --older-than is a real flag with meaningful semantics (0 = prune any past not_after; non-zero = grace period before pruning)

The omission is not a factual misstatement but it is an incomplete reference relative to the canonical sources. An operator reading SKILL.md to understand the prune workflow would be unaware of the grace-period flag. Since SKILL.md is agent-facing guidance (agents do not run CLI commands), the practical impact is low, hence suggestion severity.

Suggested fix: update line 57 to match the canonical form:
  with the `engram prune-expired [--older-than DUR]` CLI.

title: Scheduling section omits that active windowed records recall normally via search_memory/list_memory
description:
File: skill/engram/skills/curating-memory/SKILL.md, new 'Scheduling (temporal validity windows)' section.

The new section correctly describes the out-of-window case (records hidden from recall, surfaced via list_scheduled), but does not mention that active windowed records — those whose current time falls within their not_before/not_after window — surface normally via search_memory and list_memory, identical to unscheduled records.

Both canonical sources are explicit: CLAUDE.md line 70-71 ('active windowed records surface normally via search_memory/list_memory') and docs-site tools.md line 113 ('Active windowed records surface via list_memory/search_memory, not here'). An agent reading only the new SKILL.md section could conclude that list_scheduled is required to find any scheduled record, which is wrong for in-window records and would cause missed recalls.

Suggested fix: add one sentence after the existing out-of-window paragraph, e.g.: 'Active windowed records — those whose current time falls within the not_before/not_after window — surface normally via search_memory and list_memory, identical to unscheduled records; list_scheduled reveals only the hidden ones.'

title: list_scheduled tool docs claim 'your windowed memories' but ownerOrSharedCondition includes other owners' shared records
description:
Files: docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md (list_scheduled section), internal/server/tools.go (list_scheduled tool description), CLAUDE.md.

Multiple places describe list_scheduled as returning 'your windowed memories':
- tools.md: 'List your windowed memories the recall gate is hiding.'
- tools.go MCP tool Description: 'List your windowed memories the recall gate is hiding'
- store.go godoc for ListScheduled: 'for management (review/reschedule/delete)'

However, ListScheduled uses ownerOrSharedCondition(subj), which for an authenticated caller returns records matching EITHER owner==sub OR visibility==shared. This means other authenticated users' shared-but-hidden (scheduled or expired) records are also visible to the caller.

The 'your windowed memories' framing implies exclusive ownership, but the actual scope is 'your own plus any shared windowed records from other owners.' The godoc's 'management (review/reschedule/delete)' framing is also misleading since callers cannot write other owners' records even if they can read them here.

Suggested fix: update the tool description and docs to something like: 'List windowed memories the recall gate is hiding — your own and any shared records you can read.'
close_reason: Fixed: ListScheduled now owner-only (ownerOnlyCondition); shared+scheduled records no longer leak cross-actor. TestListScheduledOwnerIsolation added. Verified APPROVE.

      storeArgs

      NotAfter  string `json:"not_after,omitempty" jsonschema:"RFC3339; drop from recall at this time"`
  }

Then scheduleMemory body fields (a.Content, a.Scope, etc.) stay unchanged. The MCP JSON schema generator and json.Unmarshal both handle embedded structs correctly in Go's standard library and in typical schema reflection libraries. Verify the schema generation output is unchanged before merging.

title: prune-expired CLI --older-than grace period has no test coverage
description:
The new cmd/engram/prune.go command is entirely untested at the CLI layer. The store-level TestPruneExpired only exercises PruneExpired(ctx, now) — equivalent to --older-than=0 (prune everything past). The --older-than flag's grace semantics (before = time.Now().Add(-pruneOlderThan)) are never exercised.

Specific gaps:
1. A record whose not_after lapsed 30min ago should SURVIVE a run with --older-than=1h.
2. A record whose not_after lapsed 2h ago should be PRUNED with --older-than=1h.
3. The CLI output format ('pruned N expired record(s) (not_after < T)') is never checked.

The CLI command is thin (7 lines of business logic in RunE) but the --older-than computation is the feature's stated safety mechanism for operators. A unit or integration test for pruneExpiredCmd.RunE with a controllable clock and a real Qdrant store would close this gap.

File: internal/store/store_test.go TestPruneExpired (only tests grace=0)

title: not_after==now boundary instant untested (epoch-second truncation edge)
description:
The recall gate uses activeWindowConditions with Range{Gt: sec} for not_after — meaning a record expires AT not_after (exclusive upper bound). Payload round-trip stores not_after as time.Unix(t.Unix(), 0), which truncates sub-second precision. The parseWindow validator also uses !t.After(now), so not_after==now is rejected at schedule time.

Both boundary behaviors (gate exclusivity at now, schedule-time rejection at now) are untested. Existing tests use well-separated values (+/-24h from fixed). A test should:
1. Set fixed clock to T. Store a record with not_after=T. Assert it does NOT appear in Search/List (expired AT T, not after).
2. Verify parseWindow rejects not_after==now (already covered by past-not_after test, but the exact-equality case is an unexercised Qdrant Range boundary that could mask an off-by-one in the Lte vs Lt distinction between gate and prune).

File: internal/store/store.go:338-352 (activeWindowConditions, Range{Gt})
File: internal/store/store.go:700-702 (PruneExpired, Range{Lt})
File: internal/server/tools.go:219 (parseWindow, !t.After(now))

title: scheduleMemory validation uses wall clock (time.Now) while store recall gate uses injected WithClock clock
description:
File: internal/server/tools.go (scheduleMemory, line 338); internal/store/store.go (WithClock, New)

The store.Option/WithClock functional option correctly injects a clock into the Store so tests can exercise active/scheduled/expired boundaries deterministically. However, the validation in scheduleMemory calls parseWindow(a, time.Now().UTC()) with a hardcoded wall-clock value rather than the store's injected clock (or any shared clock source).

This creates a split-clock scenario: the recall gate (activeWindowConditions, scheduledStateCondition) operates on s.now(), but the 'not_after must be in the future' pre-check at schedule time uses real wall time. In production this is harmless. In tests, a fixed clock injected via WithClock will not affect the schedule-time validation, so tests that freeze time to a past or future instant (e.g., to simulate an already-expired not_after being stored) cannot do so end-to-end through the handler path.

The structural inconsistency is also a minor invariant-design smell: the temporal validity concept is split across two different time sources in the same request path.

Suggested fix: Either thread the clock through deps so scheduleMemory can use it, or accept that schedule-time validation is always wall-clock and document the intentional split. Either is defensible; the current state is undocumented inconsistency.
close_reason: Deferred (suggestion severity, non-blocking) to follow-up engram-d3k.

title: ScheduledState string type allows invalid values to silently fall through to ScheduledPending in scheduledStateCondition
description:
File: internal/store/store.go (scheduledStateCondition, ~line 556)

ScheduledState is declared as 'type ScheduledState string', which means any arbitrary string is a valid ScheduledState at compile time. The external API boundary is correctly guarded: listScheduled in tools.go (line 441-449) validates the raw string and returns an error for unknown values before constructing a ScheduledState.

However, the store-layer function scheduledStateCondition uses a 'default: // ScheduledPending' branch. Any internal caller that constructs an invalid ScheduledState value (typo, future refactor, test helper) will get silently misbehaving query behavior — treating the invalid value as ScheduledPending and returning wrong results — rather than an error.

The blast radius is currently low because there is only one call site (ListScheduled), which is only reached via the validated listScheduled handler. But the store's public ListScheduled API signature accepts ScheduledState without validation, so future callers are exposed.

Suggested fix: Have scheduledStateCondition return (condition, error) and error on unrecognised values, or add a Validate() method to ScheduledState and call it at the top of ListScheduled. Either approach closes the silent-fallback gap at the store boundary rather than relying solely on the handler layer.
close_reason: Deferred (suggestion severity, non-blocking) to follow-up engram-d3k.

title: list_scheduled missing cross-actor isolation test for private scheduled records
description:
OWASP A01 / A09 — Missing regression test for cross-actor isolation on list_scheduled.

Location: internal/store/store_test.go (TestListScheduledStates) and internal/server/tools_test.go

The store-level filter in ListScheduled (store.go:597-600) is correct: it uses ownerOrSharedCondition(subj) as a Must condition, which prevents actor B from reading actor A's private scheduled records. However, there is no test that exercises the cross-actor boundary for this specific path — analogous to TestAuthedCrossActorSharedReadHandlers and TestSearchListOwnerIsolation for normal Search/List.

TestListScheduledStates (store_test.go:1558) uses only a single actor (sub-A). TestListScheduledTool (tools_test.go) also uses a single actor. Neither test verifies that Authenticated('sub-B').listScheduled() cannot see Authenticated('sub-A')'s private scheduled record.

Risk: If a future refactor of ListScheduled accidentally drops the ownerOrSharedCondition clause (e.g. by rebuilding the filter inline), the isolation regression would go undetected.

Suggested fix: Add a store-level test seeding actor A's private scheduled record and actor A's shared scheduled record, then asserting actor B's ListScheduled sees the shared one but not the private one. Mirror the pattern of TestSearchListOwnerIsolation at store_test.go:385 and TestAuthedCrossActorSharedReadHandlers at tools_test.go:683.
close_reason: Fixed: ListScheduled now owner-only (ownerOnlyCondition); shared+scheduled records no longer leak cross-actor. TestListScheduledOwnerIsolation added. Verified APPROVE.

title: scheduleMemory uses wall-clock time.Now() directly, not an injectable clock
description:
internal/server/tools.go scheduleMemory (line 338): parseWindow is called with time.Now().UTC() hardcoded. The Store layer correctly has an injectable clock via WithClock/s.now(), but the server-layer validation in parseWindow (which checks not_after is in the future) bypasses this injection and always uses wall clock.

This is an architectural inconsistency: tests that want to assert boundary behavior for not_after validation at the server layer (e.g., a not_after exactly equal to now) cannot control the clock at the server layer. The TestScheduleMemoryValidation test works around this by using dates far in the past ('2000-01-01') or far in the future ('2031-01-01'), avoiding the need for clock control.

The deps struct could carry a clock func (or reuse d.st's clock via a getter), and parseWindow could accept it as a parameter. This would make the server-layer not_after validation testable at the second boundary and keep the design consistent. Low urgency (the workaround is fine for current tests), but worth aligning before the clock injection pattern becomes load-bearing elsewhere.

title: P-8: PR description contains AI process self-narration that a human author would strip
description:

Location: PR #113 description, second paragraph.

title: C-6: summary.test.ts fixture produces a dangling ')' — fabricated test data artifact
description:
Pattern: C-6 (fabricated/inauthentic test data)

File: ui/src/lib/summary.test.ts, line 7

The test fixture is:
  input:    'GOTCHA (agentgateway path) must match'
  expected: 'agentgateway path) must match'

The regex in summary.ts strips the opening paren (`GOTCHA (`) but leaves the orphaned `)`. The expected value has a dangling close-paren that would never appear as a sensible content summary in the UI. A human crafting this test would have used input that gives a clean expected result, e.g. input `'GOTCHA: agentgateway path must match'` → expected `'agentgateway path must match'`, or `'GOTCHA (agentgateway) path must match'` with a closing paren that stays. The artifact signals the test data was generated without tracing the output through the regex first.

Fix: pick a fixture that demonstrates the strip without producing a broken string. Either use a colon variant (no open-paren to leave orphaned) or close the paren before additional words: e.g. input `'GOTCHA (path must match)'` / expected `'path must match)'` at least reads as intentional, or better: `'GOTCHA: path must match'` → `'path must match'`.
close_reason: Not a defect: the dangling ')' is the correct output of stripping 'GOTCHA (' from the plan's verbatim fixture; ')' is genuinely part of the remaining content

1. loading=true branch (line 18): renders 'loading…' — not tested.

File: ui/src/lib/components/MemoryDetail.test.ts
Source: ui/src/lib/components/MemoryDetail.svelte lines 12, 18-23

The notFound distinction matters because a missing record is a normal UI state (user navigates to a deleted memory) while a generic error warrants a different message. Both are untested, so a copy/paste regression or inverted condition would pass the suite undetected.

title: observe/+page.svelte: disabled listQ renders misleading 'no memories' Empty state before scope is chosen
description:
ui/src/routes/observe/+page.svelte: the listQ is created with 'enabled: !!pp.scope' (line 28). When a user first lands on /observe with no scope in the URL, the query is disabled and listQ.data is undefined. MemoryList receives memories=[] loading=false error=null and renders its Empty state: 'no memories / nothing in this scope / filter'.

This message is wrong — there ARE memories, the user simply hasn't selected a scope yet. The MemoryList Empty copy implies filtering produced zero results, which confuses first-time users.

Fix options:
- Pass a 'disabled' or 'placeholder' prop to MemoryList so it can render 'select a scope from the sidebar' instead of the empty-results copy.
- Or, in observe/+page.svelte, conditionally render a prompt when !params.scope instead of always rendering MemoryList.
close_reason: Deferred to follow-up engram-2b0 (non-blocking suggestions)

title: Dead $derived 'scope' rune in search/+page.svelte shadows itself and is never consumed
description:
ui/src/routes/search/+page.svelte line 9 declares:

  const scope = $derived(page.url.searchParams.get('scope') ?? '');

This reactive declaration is dead. The only place 'scope' could be used — the searchQ factory on line 13 — immediately re-declares its own 'const scope = page.url.searchParams.get(...)' that shadows the outer one. The template (line 23) does not reference 'scope' directly either.

The outer $derived therefore runs on every URL change but its value is never read, silently wasting a reactive derivation and misleading readers who assume it feeds the query.

Fix: remove line 9. The factory's inner read is sufficient and already reactive because createQuery takes an options function.
close_reason: Removed dead $derived scope var in search/+page.svelte

title: Adopt shadcn semantic tokens; retire bespoke eg-*/--cat-* layer
description:
## Context

The v1 console was built with a hand-rolled theme: custom eg-* Tailwind utilities, raw inline style attributes, and a bespoke --cat-* CSS variable set. ADR engram-e38 adopted shadcn-svelte + Tailwind v4 with a custom .dark/@theme block (the terminal/dev-dark direction). Operating the console against real data revealed the bespoke layer is thin, inconsistent, and duplicates what shadcn's standard semantic token system (background/foreground/card/muted/border/primary/…) provides for free. The redesign commits to shadcn's standard token vocabulary for light + dark, retaining only the four category accent hues as named variables within that system.

## Decision

Replace app.css with shadcn's standard semantic token set (light :root + .dark) and remove all eg-* utility classes and raw inline style attributes; retain the four category accent hues (--cat-convention/gotcha/decision/preference) as theme variables expressed within the shadcn token system. The migration is incremental — done per-component during each rewrite, not a big-bang pass — so intermediate states remain valid builds.

## Rationale

- Eliminates a parallel token vocabulary not understood by vendored shadcn primitives, removing a translation burden that grows with each new component.
- shadcn's standard tokens cover every visual role already needed (background, card, muted, border, primary, destructive, ring); the bespoke set was a subset reimplemented under different names.
- Per-component migration keeps diffs reviewable and CI stable.
- Supersedes engram-e38's custom .dark/@theme-block direction; the all-sans product aesthetic replaces the terminal/dev-dark aesthetic for the operator console.

## Alternatives Considered

- Extend and fix the bespoke eg-*/--cat-* layer — no migration cost, but continued divergence from shadcn's token assumptions; every new vendored primitive needs manual token mapping. (rejected)
- Keep eg-* utilities and alias --cat-* onto shadcn tokens via CSS — smaller surface, but two token vocabularies coexist; aliases rot as primitives evolve. (rejected)
- Adopt shadcn standard semantic tokens; retire eg-*/--cat-* — broad mechanical migration, but vendored components work with no translation layer and theming follows shadcn tooling. (CHOSEN)

## Consequences

Positive: all vendored shadcn components (sidebar, resizable, card, badge, command, …) work against their own token assumptions with zero translation; light/dark theming follows documented shadcn tooling; one token vocabulary instead of two (lower contributor load).
Negative: broad mechanical migration touching every existing component file; partial departure from the terminal/dev-dark visual direction established in engram-e38.
Neutral: category accent hues are preserved but reparented into the shadcn token system; migration is incremental so intermediate states are valid builds.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs
