title: Design: holistic operator-console redesign (shadcn-svelte + modern, real-data-driven)
description: Short design pass for the console redesign before implementing the hierarchy/list/detail/layout children. Decide: typography scale + whether to keep full monospace or mono-for-data/sans-for-chrome; list-row anatomy (category chip vs prefix, summary ellipsis, timestamp/recency, tag handling, selected/hover affordance, density/zebra); detail-pane layout (structured header, readable body, metadata block, time precision); responsive 3-pane behavior (flexible widths, min/max, narrow-viewport collapse). Produce docs/superpowers/specs/<date>-operator-console-redesign-design.md. Run via dev-flow:brainstorming. Blocks the redesign implementation children below.
notes:
REFRAMED to a holistic ground-up presentation redesign (user direction 2026-06-12: 'rethink the entire presentation... lean more heavily into shadcn-svelte + modern design', designing against real deployed data + screenshots). Foundation confirmed: components.json CLI-initialized (default style, neutral base, cssVariables), bits-ui 2.18 + tailwind-variants + cn(clsx+tailwind-merge) + mode-watcher + Tailwind v4 all installed; only button/checkbox/select vendored of ~50 registry primitives. REQUIREMENTS INVENTORY (the screenshot findings this design must resolve — siblings engram-kco.1/.3/.4/.5/.6/.7): scope-rail overflow/overlap (ScopeRail:41 no truncate) + Button nowrap leak (button.svelte:6); list-row redundant category (gotcha·GOTCHA), hard 80-char slice no ellipsis, dangling ·visibility, no recency timestamp, tag overflow; no visual hierarchy (13px mono wall, 1px-border rows); detail pane fixed 300px cramped wall, unformatted, date-only; non-responsive fixed 210/300px panes; non-actionable 'retry' text; raw long scope strings. CANDIDATE shadcn mapping (to validate in design): Resizable panes, Sidebar+Tooltip rail, Badge chips, ScrollArea+Card+Separator, Command (⌘K), Skeleton, DropdownMenu/Avatar; mono-for-data + sans-for-chrome; adopt standard shadcn theme tokens (supersede the custom eg-*/--cat-* layer in app.css). The piecemeal impl beads (.1/.3/.4/.5/.6/.7) stay gated on this bead and will be SUPERSEDED by plan-to-beads output after the design converges.
grounding/web: shadcn-svelte llms.txt (https://www.shadcn-svelte.com/llms.txt, fetched 2026-06-12). Current registry confirms the components to build on — Layout/Nav: Resizable (panes), Sidebar, Scroll Area, Separator, Tabs, Navigation Menu, Breadcrumb. Overlays: Command (⌘K palette), Dialog, Drawer, Sheet, Dropdown Menu, Tooltip, Popover, Hover Card. Feedback: Badge, Empty (empty states), Skeleton, Spinner, Sonner (toasts), Alert, Progress. Display: Card, Item (versatile row primitive), Data Table (TanStack Table), Table, Pagination, Avatar, Kbd, Typography, Chart (LayerChart, for a future Dashboard), Aspect Ratio. Key guides to follow at impl: Theming (CSS-variable tokens — adopt standard set, retire custom eg-*/--cat-*), Tailwind v4 migration, components.json, CLI add. Per-component docs at shadcn-svelte.com/docs/components/<name>.md. STANDOUT picks vs the findings: Item for list rows, Empty for empty states, Data Table+Pagination over the server's existing offset pagination, Kbd for ⌘K, Resizable for the responsive 3-pane.
grounding/skill: shadcn-svelte skill conventions (enforced) — the redesign MUST adopt: semantic tokens (bg-background/text-muted-foreground/etc) RETIRING the custom eg-*/--cat-* layer + raw inline styles in app.css; component composition over custom markup (Card.Header/Title/Content/Footer, Empty for empty states, Badge for chips, Skeleton/Spinner for loading, Separator over <hr>, Field.FieldGroup for the filter form); cn() for conditional classes; truncate shorthand; flex gap-* (no space-*); size-* for equal dims; no manual dark: overrides; no z-index on overlays. components.json currently has NO iconLibrary set -> add @lucide/svelte; icons in buttons via data-icon (no sizing classes). style='default' (could explore newer presets via the design-system builder --preset). Component-doc convention: read shadcn-svelte.com/docs/components/<name>.md before using each. This means the redesign is also a token/convention migration, not just new components.
grounding/probe: current IA — routes observe/search/discovery (+ root redirect). observe/+page.svelte assembles the 3-pane as a plain <div class=flex> with ScopeRail (210px) + flex-1 [MemoryList + prev/next offset pagination buttons] + MemoryDetail (300px); URL-driven via svelte-query v6 (scope/categories/visibility/offset/selectedId; listScopes/listMemories/getMemory). SearchPalette is a RAW <input> on a separate /search route (NOT a ⌘K Command modal); AppShell header has only the ⌘K->/search button + theme toggle — NO persistent nav between observe/search/discovery. Redesign implications: add real nav chrome (Sidebar/Tabs), make ⌘K a Command-in-Dialog overlay, Resizable 3-pane, Pagination component over the existing server offset, Empty/Skeleton states. svelte-query v6 runes pattern + URL-as-state must be preserved.
DESIGN DECISION (shell layout): Option A — far-left slim icon NAV RAIL (Observe/Search/Discovery/Dashboard) + collapsible Scopes SIDEBAR + resizable List + Detail panes. Maps to shadcn Sidebar + Resizable + ScrollArea. Scales as views are added; keeps scopes/list/detail glanceable for power browsing. (Considered B list-first-with-Sheet-detail and C modernized-classic-3-pane+tabs.)
DESIGN DECISION (list row): Option A — Compact: category Badge chip + one-line truncated summary + a muted meta line (relative time · first N tags · +overflow). shadcn Item + Badge. Fixes: badge replaces redundant category prefix, real ellipsis/line-clamp (no hard 80-char slice), relative recency timestamp (was absent), tag overflow as +N, drop the dangling ·visibility. Table/Data-Table (option C) reserved for a future 'all memories' power view. OPEN sub-qs: strip leading ALLCAPS category token from summary; mono-vs-sans typography (next screen).
DESIGN DECISION (typography): Option A — ALL SANS (system/Inter), dropping the all-monospace identity for a clean product feel. (Considered B hybrid sans+mono-for-data and C refined-all-mono.) Also CONFIRMED: strip the redundant leading ALLCAPS category token from displayed summaries (badge carries the category). Theme: adopt shadcn standard semantic tokens (light + dark) and keep the four category hues (convention/gotcha/decision/preference) as Badge accents.
DESIGN DECISION (detail pane): Option B — Card header (badge + relative time + copy) → metadata strip of provenance pills (scope/by/src/vis) → content body (ScrollArea, whitespace-preserved) → tag chips. Full scope on Tooltip, full timestamp on hover. Copy action in v1; edit/delete deferred to a later write-phase epic. ALL VISUAL DECISIONS SET: shell=A (nav rail+scopes sidebar+resizable list+detail), row=A compact, type=all-sans, detail=B.
DETAIL B CORRECTION (user caught scope-fidelity loss): the full scope is PRIMARY provenance and must be shown VERBATIM, never collapsed to the last path segment. In the detail pane B, scope gets its OWN full-width line (mono, ellipsis+Tooltip on overflow) showing the complete value e.g. repo:github.com/fzymgc-house/selfhosted-cluster or discovery:repo:*; by/source/visibility are compact pills below. SCOPE-IN-ROW RULE: Observe rows OMIT per-row scope (rail fixes it) to avoid repetition; cross-scope Search rows GAIN a small scope chip (shortened display, full value on hover). General principle: shorten for glance, never destroy the identifying value (always available via Tooltip/full line).

title: C-3: mountMCPRoutes doc comment uses markdown list to restate visible branch logic
description:
Pattern C-3 — over-annotation of self-documenting code, with an AI-provenance structural tell.

File: cmd/engram/mcproute.go, lines 33–43 (the mountMCPRoutes doc comment).

The doc comment uses a markdown bullet list (Go // comments, not godoc prose) to enumerate the two branches of the six-line function. The bullets duplicate what the function body makes immediately obvious: mcpPath=="/" → mux.Handle("/", mcpHandler); else → mux.Handle(mcpPath, …) + mux.Handle("/", rootHandler). The parentheticals repeat phrasing already in the surrounding sentences.

Contrast with house style: httplog.go and root.go doc comments are 1–2 tight sentences that add information not in the code (e.g., 'observe is a test seam (nil in production)'). No other function in cmd/engram uses a markdown list inside a // doc comment.

The markdown-list structure inside a Go doc comment is also a formatting provenance tell: Go authors write prose in doc comments; AI generators frequently reach for bullet structure.

Suggested fix: replace the block with a single sentence such as 'mountMCPRoutes wires the MCP handler and the root fallback onto mux; mcpPath="/" uses the legacy catch-all.' The detail about the ServeMux 301 is load-bearing and belongs here, but as a prose continuation, not a bullet.
close_reason: Fixed: mountMCPRoutes doc comment rewritten as prose (removed markdown bullet list), matching cmd/engram house style.

title: memory-mcp.yaml: 'Empty omits' comment renders only when mcpPath is non-empty, never when it matters
description:
File: charts/engram/templates/memory-mcp.yaml, lines 43-44 (in the PR diff).

The comment reads:
  # Empty omits → server defaults the MCP transport to /mcp. "/" restores
  # the legacy root catch-all.

It is placed INSIDE the {{- with .Values.memory.mcpPath }} block. The {{- with }} action only executes (and renders its body) when mcpPath is non-empty/non-zero. This means:
- When mcpPath is empty (the common default case the comment is describing), the entire block — including the comment — is skipped and the env var is omitted. The comment is invisible.
- When mcpPath is non-empty, the comment renders alongside the env var entry, but the 'Empty omits' clause is irrelevant — empty is not what is happening.

The comment therefore explains the case where it never appears and is redundant where it does appear. A reader of the rendered YAML (or a Helm developer reading the template when mcpPath is unset) never sees this explanation at the point it would be useful.

Suggested fix: move the comment outside the {{- with }} block so it is always rendered. Place it immediately before the {{- with .Values.memory.mcpPath }} line:
  # MEM_MCP_PATH: empty omits → server defaults to /mcp. Set "/" to
  # restore the pre-0.7 root catch-all.
  {{- with .Values.memory.mcpPath }}
  - { name: MEM_MCP_PATH, value: "{{ . }}" }
  {{- end }}

Note: In Helm templates, YAML comments inside action blocks are subject to the same conditional rendering as the surrounding template logic.
close_reason: Fixed: chart MEM_MCP_PATH explanation converted to a Helm template comment ({{- /* */}}), always present in source regardless of value.

title: resolveMCPPath does not reject reserved path prefixes, causing startup panic on misconfiguration
description:
File: cmd/engram/mcproute.go — resolveMCPPath

resolveMCPPath validates that the path starts with '/' but does not check for collision with routes that are registered unconditionally before mountMCPRoutes is called: /ui/ (subtree), /auth/login, /auth/callback, /auth/logout, /engram.v1.EngramService/ (Connect).

If an operator sets MEM_MCP_PATH to one of those prefixes (e.g. /ui/ or /auth/), mux.Handle in mountMCPRoutes registers a second handler on an already-registered exact or subtree pattern. Go's http.ServeMux panics on duplicate registrations (Go 1.22+). The result is an unrecovered runtime panic at startup instead of a clear startup-time error with a diagnostic message.

Suggested fix: add a small blocklist check in resolveMCPPath (or a separate validateMCPPath helper) that rejects paths matching the reserved prefixes and returns a descriptive error. This keeps the early-exit error-return pattern already established in runServe and avoids a panic-at-startup regression vector for operators migrating from a default install.
close_reason: Fixed: resolveMCPPath now rejects reserved roots (/ui, /auth, /engram.v1.EngramService) with a clear error before any mux registration.

title: MCP transport at explicit configurable path (MEM_MCP_PATH) with console at root when UI enabled
description:
## Context

Until 0.6.x the MCP StreamableHTTP transport was the root catch-all (mux.Handle("/", mcpHandler)); the console was a sub-path under /ui/. With the web UI enabled this had three consequences: (1) a browser hitting the host root got a 401 "no bearer token" wall instead of the console; (2) the catch-all swallowed /, /favicon.ico and stray paths into the bearer gate as noisy 401s; (3) in gateway-fronted deployments the console hostname's root re-exposed the MCP transport, bypassing the gateway's policy/audit front door (still bearer-gated, so defense-in-depth, not a vuln). The go-sdk StreamableHTTPHandler dispatches on HTTP method + session-ID header and ignores the request path, so it answered at every path under the catch-all.

## Decision

Introduce MEM_MCP_PATH (flag --mcp-path, env-first). It defaults to /mcp in ALL modes (headless and UI-enabled) and must be an absolute path. The MCP transport is mounted at that exact path. When MCP is off the root, "/" is owned by a small handler: a browser GET of the bare root 302-redirects to /ui/ when the UI is enabled; every other request (non-GET, sub-paths, or any request when headless) returns 404 instead of the MCP bearer gate. The special value MEM_MCP_PATH=/ is an escape hatch that restores the legacy root catch-all (MCP answers every path) in either mode. Routing lives in a testable mountMCPRoutes(mux, mcpHandler, uiEnabled, mcpPath) seam; the Helm chart exposes memory.mcpPath (empty omits the env var).

## Rationale

An explicit /mcp endpoint lets gateway-fronted deployments keep MCP strictly behind the gateway path and make the console hostname a console only — no accidental second door to the transport. It also kills the 401 noise: stray paths and mis-targeted MCP clients get a clear 404 rather than a bearer-gate 401. A uniform /mcp default (rather than only-when-UI-enabled) gives one predictable, documented endpoint everywhere and a single escape hatch. Exact-path mounting is correct because the go-sdk handler ignores the path; a subtree (/mcp/) mount would trigger the ServeMux trailing-slash 301 that breaks MCP POSTs. The transport endpoint itself is never redirected: MCP is POST/SSE-based and clients do not follow redirects, so only browser GET / can be redirected — which is also why a headless /->/mcp redirect was rejected (it would break POST clients and there is no browser in headless to benefit). Connect API (/engram.v1.EngramService/), /auth/*, and /ui/ are explicit ServeMux patterns that win over "/" by longest-prefix, so the SPA's baseUrl:"/" Connect calls are unaffected.

## Alternatives Considered

(1) Keep headless as the root catch-all and only move MCP to /mcp when the UI is enabled — narrower breaking change, but two divergent routing models and /mcp would not be a stable documented endpoint in headless. Rejected for a uniform model. (2) Mount MCP at subtree /mcp/ — rejected: ServeMux 301-redirects POST /mcp to /mcp/, which MCP POST clients mishandle. (3) Redirect headless "/" -> /mcp — rejected: the MCP transport is POST/SSE and clients do not follow redirects, and headless has no browser, so the redirect helps nobody and breaks clients still POSTing to /. (4) Always also mount /mcp alongside the headless catch-all (no behavior change) — rejected as it leaves "/" re-exposing the transport, defeating purpose (3) of the change.

## Consequences

BREAKING for all installs: MCP previously answered at "/" (and every path); it now answers only at /mcp by default. UI-enabled and headless clients that POST to the host root must target /mcp, or set MEM_MCP_PATH=/ to restore the catch-all. This is signalled as a BREAKING CHANGE in the release (release-please / Conventional Commits). Gains: browsers landing on the host root get the console; MCP has a stable explicit endpoint; gateway deployments can scope the proxy to /mcp with no second transport door on the console hostname; bearer-gate 401 noise on stray paths is gone. The routing decision is unit-tested via mountMCPRoutes + resolveMCPPath; the Helm chart gained memory.mcpPath.
notes: Implements GH #108 / bead engram-orm.

title: Configurable MCP transport path (MEM_MCP_PATH) + console at / when UI enabled
description:
GH #108. Restructure the UI-enabled serving path in cmd/engram/serve.go (lines 160-179) so MCP is an explicit endpoint and the console is the default landing.

CURRENT: MCP StreamableHTTP is the root catch-all (mux.Handle("/", mcpHandler)); console is a sub-path under /ui/. Consequences when UI enabled: (1) browser hitting host root gets 401 'no bearer token' instead of console; (2) catch-all swallows /, /favicon.ico etc into the bearer gate -> noisy 401s; (3) in gateway-fronted deploys the console hostname's root re-exposes the MCP transport, bypassing the gateway's policy/audit front door (still bearer-gated, so defense-in-depth not a vuln).

PROPOSED (UI enabled only): mount MCP at configurable MEM_MCP_PATH (default /mcp); serve console at / (302 / -> /ui/ for browser GETs). UI disabled (headless): keep MCP as root catch-all -> zero change for MCP-only installs. Operators can set MEM_MCP_PATH=/ to preserve catch-all even with UI on.

DESIGN DECISIONS TO PIN (not in the FR):
- Redirect approach (302 / -> /ui/, assets stay under /ui/) keeps the SvelteKit base:'/ui' build valid -> no UI rebuild. Truly serving at / would require rebuilding SvelteKit with base:'/'. Recommend the redirect approach.
- http.ServeMux: 'mux.Handle("/mcp", h)' matches /mcp exactly; '"/mcp/"' matches subtree. Decide which StreamableHTTP needs (likely exact).
- 302 should apply to browser GET / only; decide behavior for non-GET or MCP clients that POST to / when MEM_MCP_PATH=/mcp.

BACKWARD COMPAT: UI-enabled installs that currently POST MCP to / must switch to /mcp (or set MEM_MCP_PATH=/). Release note required.

DEPENDENCY: blocked by the #106 embed fix (engram-0y0) — the console can't render its assets until that lands, so 'console at /' is untestable before it.

Per dev-flow, this feature should go through brainstorming -> spec before implementation (config surface + redirect semantics + backward-compat warrant a short design).
notes:
grounding/probe: serve.go routing — mux mounts (UI on): /engram.v1.EngramService/ (Connect), GET /auth/{login,callback}, POST /auth/logout, /ui/ (StripPrefix StaticHandler), / (MCP catch-all). ServeMux longest-prefix => Connect/auth/ui all win over /, so restructuring / is safe for the SPA's Connect calls (baseUrl:'/' hits the explicit Connect pattern).
grounding/probe: go-sdk@v1.6.1 StreamableHTTPHandler.ServeHTTP dispatches on req.Method + sessionID header, never on req.URL.Path. => mounting at exact '/mcp' is correct (POST+GET both land); subtree '/mcp/' risks the ServeMux trailing-slash 301 that breaks MCP POST. Recommend exact.
DESIGN (converged, scoped brainstorm). MEM_MCP_PATH (flag --mcp-path, EnvOr) defaults to /mcp in ALL modes; must start with /; '/' = escape hatch restoring the legacy root catch-all. Routing via testable mountMCPRoutes(mux, mcpHandler, uiEnabled, mcpPath): if mcpPath=='/' -> mux.Handle('/', mcp) (catch-all, either mode); else mux.Handle(mcpPath, mcp) exact + mux.Handle('/', rootHandler(uiEnabled)) where rootHandler does GET / -> 302 /ui/ when uiEnabled, else http.NotFound. Matrix: UI-on default {/mcp:MCP, GET/:302 /ui/, else 404}; headless default {/mcp:MCP, /:404}; MEM_MCP_PATH=/ {root catch-all, both modes}. Grounded: go-sdk handler ignores path (exact /mcp safe; subtree 301 hazard avoided); Connect/auth/ui are explicit patterns that win over / so SPA baseUrl:'/' unaffected. BREAKING for all installs (was: MCP catch-all at /); back-compat = MEM_MCP_PATH=/. Deliverables: code + unit tests (resolveMCPPath) + routing test (mountMCPRoutes w/ stub) + ADR (bd decision + docs/adr) + BREAKING release note. User decisions: exact /mcp; 302 GET-only + else 404; uniform /mcp default; headless GET/ plain 404; ADR yes.
ADR engram-bj6 (Accepted) rendered to docs/adr/engram-bj6-*.md.
IMPLEMENTED (TDD). New cmd/engram/mcproute.go: resolveMCPPath (empty->/mcp, must be absolute, '/'=escape hatch) + mountMCPRoutes(mux,mcpHandler,uiEnabled,mcpPath) + rootHandler(uiEnabled) (GET / ->302 /ui/ when UI on, else http.NotFound). serve.go: added --mcp-path/MEM_MCP_PATH flag, resolve+mount via mountMCPRoutes (replaces mux.Handle('/',handler)); updated /ui/ comment. Helm: charts values memory.mcpPath + memory-mcp.yaml conditional MEM_MCP_PATH (empty omits). ADR engram-bj6 (Accepted) rendered. title: Inject Store clock via WithClock option; keep public signatures stable
description:
## Context

Search and List must read 'current time' to build the recall gate. Three injection points were evaluated: thread now through every public method signature, carry it in context.Context, or store it as a field on Store set at construction. The public signatures of Search and List are stable contracts used by tools.go and tests; changing them for clock injection would break every caller.

## Decision

Store gains an unexported now func() time.Time field defaulting to time.Now, injectable at construction via a WithClock(fn) functional option; Search and List read s.now() internally.

## Rationale

- Zero change to the public Store interface — all existing callers in tools.go compile unchanged.\n- Tests inject a fixed clock via New(client, coll, WithClock(fn)) to deterministically exercise active/scheduled/expired boundaries.\n- The functional-options pattern is the idiomatic Go extension point and matches the existing New signature.\n- Keeps 'current time' a store-construction concern, consistent with the store being the authz/isolation boundary.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Store.now field via WithClock functional option (chosen):** zero public-signature change, fully testable via fixed-clock injection, smallest blast radius. Clock is fixed at construction (no per-call override — not needed).\n- **Thread now time.Time through Search/List (rejected):** explicit per call site, but every caller in tools.go and tests must change and the stable public interface breaks; leaks 'current time' into the MCP layer.\n- **Carry the clock in context.Context (rejected):** no signature change, but misuses the context contract (meant for cancellation/request-scoped values) and is hard to discover/document.

## Consequences

Positive: no caller changes in tools.go or the server test harness; deterministic boundary tests without sleeps; New(client, collection) still compiles via the variadic. Negative: clock fixed at construction — per-call override requires reconstructing a Store (not needed today). Neutral: the unexported now field doubles as a white-box test seam.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Soft-hide expired records at recall; opt-in prune-expired for storage reclaim
description:
## Context

engram is a pull-based MCP server with no scheduler or notification loop. Expired records are already invisible to agents via the recall gate; the only open question is whether to destroy them eagerly, lazily, or never. Automatic destruction adds server-side state, a scheduler dependency, and irreversible data loss; never destroying wastes storage indefinitely.

## Decision

Expired records are soft-hidden at recall time by the Qdrant gate; storage is reclaimed only by the explicit operator command 'engram prune-expired', which is never run automatically.

## Rationale

- engram is explicitly pull-only; adding any server-initiated process is out of scope.\n- Soft-hide is sufficient for correctness — agents never see expired records via normal recall.\n- An opt-in CLI sweep gives operators control over when irreversible deletion occurs.\n- PruneExpired is collection-wide with no subject authz, so making it explicit and manual is a safety property.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Soft-hide at read + opt-in operator CLI sweep (chosen):** no scheduler, no irreversible auto-deletion, operator controls reclamation; consistent with pull-only architecture. Expired records accumulate until the operator runs prune-expired.\n- **Auto-prune via background goroutine or cron (rejected):** reclaims automatically but adds a scheduler to a pull-only server, goroutine lifecycle complexity, and a silent destructive action — contradicts the stated 'no scheduler' scope.\n- **Lazy destructive expiry on access (rejected):** unpredictable; a get_memory on an expired record would silently destroy it, conflicting with the ungated by-id contract.

## Consequences

Positive: no scheduler or background goroutine added; expired records stay inspectable via list_scheduled (state=expired) and get_memory until pruned; operator retains full control of reclamation. Negative: expired records accumulate in Qdrant until prune-expired runs. Neutral: a future cron/k8s CronJob can wrap the CLI without changing this decision.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Add schedule_memory/list_scheduled tools; keep store_memory windowless
description:
## Context

store_memory's contract explicitly forbids timestamps as content and is built around curated, unscheduled records. Adding not_before/not_after to it would require category-conditional validation (both fields optional, at least one required only when scheduling), muddying a deliberately clean signature. The discovery tools established the precedent of dedicated tools for structurally different record shapes.

## Decision

schedule_memory and list_scheduled are separate MCP tools with dedicated signatures; store_memory is not modified and retains its windowless contract.

## Rationale

- store_memory's design intent is 'explicit, zero-junk, correctable, no auto-extraction' — temporal bounds are scheduling metadata, not memory content.\n- A shared tool cannot enforce 'at least one bound required' without category-conditional validation absent from the windowless case.\n- Consistent with the discovery-tools precedent: structurally different record shapes get dedicated tools.\n- schedule_memory's signature fully describes a valid scheduled call with no optional-conditional ambiguity.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Dedicated schedule_memory + list_scheduled tools (chosen):** preserves store_memory's clean contract; dedicated signature fully describes a valid scheduled call; validation is unconditional. Costs two more tools on the MCP surface.\n- **Add not_before/not_after as optional params to store_memory (rejected):** fewer tools, but violates the 'no timestamps' contract and forces confusing conditional validation onto the curated-four signature.

## Consequences

Positive: store_memory's contract stays stable and well-understood; schedule_memory validation is unconditional and self-documenting; discovery category is explicitly rejected at the schedule_memory boundary. Negative: larger MCP tool surface — agents must choose between store_memory and schedule_memory. Neutral: get/update/delete operate by id and serve all record kinds unchanged.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Gate recall via Qdrant filter; leave get_memory ungated
description:
## Context

engram's Search returns Qdrant top-k with no Go post-filter, so any temporal gate must be a server-side Qdrant condition or it silently shrinks results below k. By-id operations (get_memory / FetchForUpdate) are the only path an owner has to manage a pending or expired record surfaced via list_scheduled. The gate must therefore be asymmetric: recall paths are gated, by-id is not.

## Decision

Temporal validity is enforced as two composable Must conditions in the Qdrant filter on Search and List; get_memory and all by-id paths remain ungated so owners can manage hidden records.

## Rationale

- Search is Qdrant top-k with no Go post-filter; a post-filter silently under-returns.\n- The gate composes orthogonally with the existing ownerOrSharedCondition via extra Must conditions, without rewriting the authz envelope.\n- By-id ungating is the management escape hatch: list_scheduled surfaces the ID, then get/update/delete operate on the record.\n- NewIsEmpty ensures zero behavior change for every existing unwindowed record.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Server-side Qdrant filter on recall paths only (chosen):** prevents under-returning on top-k; backward-compatible via NewIsEmpty; no over-fetch into Go memory. Asymmetric contract needs documenting; fields unindexed (full scan, acceptable today).\n- **Post-filter in Go after fetch (rejected):** silently shrinks Search below requested k and over-fetches into server memory.\n- **Gate everywhere including get_memory (rejected):** removes the only management path for pending/expired records — owner cannot inspect or update what they cannot fetch.

## Consequences

Positive: full backward compatibility (pre-feature records match via NewIsEmpty); the gate lives in the store layer so no future handler can bypass it; no Go-memory over-fetch. Negative: asymmetric recall-vs-by-id contract must be understood by contributors; payload fields unindexed (full scan at scale). Neutral: a payload index can be added later without changing the contract.

title: MEM_UI_ISSUER-alone sufficiency not independently tested
description:
The override test case ('MEM_UI_ISSUER overrides MCP issuer (split topology)') uses merge(full, "MEM_UI_ISSUER", "https://console.example"), which leaves MEM_OIDC_ISSUER="https://mcp.example" present in the env map. No test case sets MEM_UI_ISSUER while MEM_OIDC_ISSUER is absent.

This means the test suite does not prove that MEM_UI_ISSUER alone (without any MEM_OIDC_ISSUER) is sufficient to activate the UI. If the two getenv lines in resolveUIConfig were swapped (or the MEM_UI_ISSUER branch were removed entirely and MEM_OIDC_ISSUER always used), the existing tests would still pass.

Suggested addition in cmd/engram/uiconfig_test.go:

  {"MEM_UI_ISSUER alone, no MEM_OIDC_ISSUER (split-only topology)",
   dropThenMerge(full, "MEM_OIDC_ISSUER", "MEM_UI_ISSUER", "https://console.example"),
   true, false, "https://console.example"},

i.e. a case where MEM_OIDC_ISSUER is absent but MEM_UI_ISSUER is set, asserting wantIssuer="https://console.example". This would catch a regression where the first getenv call is inadvertently skipped or the fallback order is reversed.

This gap is distinct from but corroborates the already-filed precedence finding (engram-jrd.1): engram-jrd.1 covers the swap/ordering attack; this covers the standalone-sufficiency case.

title: Defensive nil guard in resourceFromOptions is annotated dead code
description:
File: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/fix-otlp-partial-resource/internal/telemetry/providers.go, lines 153-155.

The guard:

    if res == nil { // defensive: resource.New never returns a nil Resource
        res = resource.Empty()
    }

is self-described as dead code in its own comment. resource.New allocates the Resource struct before invoking detectors, so res is always non-nil when err is nil or ErrPartialResource. Keeping an explicitly-unreachable branch adds a question for every future reader: 'did the author know this cannot fire, or is there a real concern here?' The comment partially answers that, but the branch is still noise.

Suggestion: remove the nil guard and its comment. If a future upstream change ever makes resource.New return nil, the resulting nil-pointer panic will surface immediately in the existing regression test (TestResourceFromOptionsToleratesDetectorFailure), which constructs res from resourceFromOptions and immediately dereferences it. No silent misbehavior is possible.

If the team prefers retaining the guard for belt-and-suspenders safety, consider a t.Nil assertion in the test instead, or replace the comment with a build-time assertion (var _ = resource.Empty().Len()) so the invariant is machine-checked.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #103: removed the annotated dead nil guard. resource.New never returns a nil Resource (SDK contract, documented in the godoc); the regression test asserts non-nil, so a contract break would be caught.

title: No integration-level test confirms buildProviders completes when resource detection is partial
description:
The unit test TestResourceFromOptionsToleratesDetectorFailure correctly verifies that resourceFromOptions returns a non-nil, attribute-bearing resource when a detector fails. This is a solid regression guard for the fixed function.

However, the regression's real failure surface was buildProviders aborting early and returning (nil, nil, err), which caused Setup to fall back to stdout-only logging with no OTLP trace/metric export. That abort path no longer exists in the new code (res := buildResource(ctx, cfg) has no error branch), but no test exercises the end-to-end path: inject a failing detector → buildProviders completes → OTLP trace/metric/log providers are non-nil.

The existing TestSetupEnabledBuildsProvidersAndShutsDown calls real buildProviders but runs on a non-distroless host where WithHostID succeeds, so it does not reproduce the partial-resource scenario at that level.

A targeted test could use the buildProvidersFn injection pattern already established in telemetry_test.go, or alternatively replace buildResource with a test double that returns resource.Empty() to simulate the distroless partial case, and then assert that the returned lp (log provider) and shutdown are non-nil — confirming that a partial resource does not abort provider construction.

File: /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram_worktrees/fix-otlp-partial-resource/internal/telemetry/telemetry_test.go
The injection seam (buildProvidersFn) is already present; the gap is a test case that exercises buildProviders with a partial resource rather than bypassing it entirely.
close_reason: Declined (suggestion): the tolerance decision is unit-tested at the resourceFromOptions seam (both plain and sentinel error cases) and the Setup→buildProviders happy path is covered by TestSetupEnabledBuildsProvidersAndShutsDown. A buildProviders-level partial-resource test cannot deterministically reproduce the partial path without injecting a failing detector into buildResource's hardcoded set — a seam not worth adding for marginal coverage over the unit test.

title: Broad error swallow in resourceFromOptions silently drops non-ErrPartialResource detector attributes without distinct log context
description:
File: internal/telemetry/providers.go, resourceFromOptions (lines 146-157)

The error-swallow is mechanically correct (SDK auto.go:71-73 confirms resource.New always returns a non-nil *Resource and the detect loop always continues), but the WARN message is identical regardless of error type:

  'partial telemetry resource; exporting with detected attributes'

The OTel SDK distinguish two error categories with meaningfully different operator impact:
- ErrPartialResource: detector produced a partial result; attributes are merged.
- Plain error (e.g. host.id on distroless): detector result is NOT merged at all — those attributes are gone entirely, not just partial.
- ErrSchemaURLConflict: schema URL is stripped from the resource.

All three produce the same 'exporting with detected attributes' message. An operator debugging why host.id is absent gets no indication whether the issue is (a) partial merge, (b) completely dropped, or (c) schema conflict. The err value is logged, so the information is technically present, but the message does not guide the operator.

The justification for swallowing ALL errors (plain errors from WithHostID not being ErrPartialResource-wrapped) is sound and documented. This is a suggestion to improve log message specificity:

  if errors.Is(err, resource.ErrSchemaURLConflict) {
      slog.Warn('telemetry resource schema URL conflict; schema URL cleared', 'err', err)
  } else {
      slog.Warn('partial telemetry resource; exporting with detected attributes', 'err', err)
  }

Note: this is subordinate to the more critical issue of using global slog before SetDefault (engram-1id.1).
close_reason: Declined (suggestion, by design): the single WARN logs the underlying err, which names the failing detector and reason (e.g. 'host id not found in: /etc/machine-id'), so distinct context IS present. Dropping the failed detector's attribute is the intended tolerance behavior, not a silent loss.

title: Decouple UI OIDC issuer from MCP bearer issuer (MEM_UI_ISSUER), defaulting to MEM_OIDC_ISSUER
description:
GitHub issue #101 (https://github.com/seanb4t/engram/issues/101), filed by @seanb4t while wiring engram 0.6.0 into the fzymgc-house cluster.

PROBLEM
The Connect web UI lane and the MCP bearer lane share a single OIDC issuer (MEM_OIDC_ISSUER). On an IdP that mints a distinct issuer per application (Authentik default issuer_mode, common elsewhere), the security-preferred split topology — agents via a public PKCE client, console via a confidential client = two different apps = two different iss values — cannot be expressed. Enabling the console forces MEM_OIDC_ISSUER onto the console app's issuer, after which engram rejects the agents' forwarded bearer tokens (issued by the other app) and loses per-user sub attribution / memory-ownership partitioning. Authentik escape hatches don't apply: issuer_mode=global breaks discovery (no root /.well-known/openid-configuration), and the UI lane fail-fast requires a non-empty MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET so the public PKCE client can't be reused.

COUPLING (confirmed on main @42178a9)
- cmd/engram/serve.go:136 webauth.NewAuthenticator(oidcCtx, oidcIssuer, ...) — same oidcIssuer var as the MCP bearer verifier at serve.go:223 auth.New(ctx, oidcIssuer, oidcAudience).
- internal/webauth/oidc.go:28-29 oidc.NewProvider(ctx, issuer) enforces discovery.issuer == issuer.
- cmd/engram/uiconfig.go:25-29 requiredUICreds mandates MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET (fail-fast), so the public no-secret client is rejected.

REQUESTED CHANGE
Add MEM_UI_ISSUER / --ui-issuer, defaulting to MEM_OIDC_ISSUER when unset (fully backward compatible — single-app deployments unaffected). MCP bearer lane keeps MEM_OIDC_ISSUER (agents' app); UI lane uses MEM_UI_ISSUER (console app). Only the issuer needs decoupling — the audience check is already independent (UI verifier pins aud==clientID via oidc.Config{ClientID: clientID}; MCP verifier uses MEM_OIDC_AUDIENCE). Wiring: thread a second issuer var through serve.go's web-UI setup into NewAuthenticator; the MCP lane is untouched.

SCOPE NOTES
- Additive config knob, not a trust-model change — both lanes still verify issuer+audience+signature independently; no ADR needed against the locked private-per-author trust model.
- Helm chart: add memory.ui.issuer (optional scalar, MEM_UI_ISSUER) following the env-var gating convention; empty => omit => server defaults to MEM_OIDC_ISSUER.
- Docs: document the split public-agent / confidential-console topology.
- Alternative (lighter) resolution if a second issuer is undesirable: document a supported single-application topology for split public/confidential deployments. Issue prefers the MEM_UI_ISSUER approach.

ENVIRONMENT
engram v0.6.0; Helm chart oci://ghcr.io/seanb4t/charts/engram 0.6.0; IdP Authentik (per-application issuer URLs); two apps — mcp-public (public PKCE, agents) + confidential engram-ui (console).
acceptance_criteria: A new MEM_UI_ISSUER / --ui-issuer config knob exists; when unset it defaults to MEM_OIDC_ISSUER (existing single-app deployments behave identically); the web-UI authenticator discovers/verifies against MEM_UI_ISSUER while the MCP bearer verifier continues to use MEM_OIDC_ISSUER; a deployment with two distinct per-app issuers can run both lanes simultaneously (console login works against engram-ui, agent bearer tokens from mcp-public still verify with correct sub attribution); Helm chart exposes memory.ui.issuer per the gating convention; split-topology documented.
notes: Root cause: the web-UI login lane and MCP bearer lane both read the single oidcIssuer var (serve.go:136 NewAuthenticator + serve.go:223 auth.New), so a per-application IdP (distinct iss per app) couldn't run agents on a public PKCE app and the console on a confidential app. Fix: added MEM_UI_ISSUER / --ui-issuer, resolved inside the already-tested resolveUIConfig seam (cmd/engram/uiconfig.go) as UIConfig.Issuer = MEM_UI_ISSUER or-else MEM_OIDC_ISSUER, fail-fast when neither set; serve.go threads uiCfg.Issuer into NewAuthenticator while the MCP withAuth lane keeps oidcIssuer untouched. Default resolves at runtime so --oidc-issuer flag overrides flow through (backward compatible — single-app deployments unaffected). Also: chart memory.ui.issuer (gated MEM_UI_ISSUER env, empty omits), and docs-site auth.md 'Two auth lanes' + split-issuer topology section. Gates green: gofmt clean, go build/vet, go test ./cmd/engram ./internal/webauth, golangci-lint 0 issues, helm lint + template (MEM_UI_ISSUER renders only when set), yamlfmt, license-eye 0 invalid. New test cases in TestResolveUIConfig cover default-fallback, MEM_UI_ISSUER override, and no-issuer error. No ADR (additive config; trust model unchanged).

title: Helm chart comment: WithFromEnv() does not directly consume POD_NAME etc.
description:
File: charts/engram/templates/memory-mcp.yaml, lines added in PR (the Downward API block comment).

The comment reads: 'Pod identity via the Downward API, folded into OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES. WithFromEnv() in the binary consumes these; same image works on a laptop, in Docker, and in k8s.'

'These' is ambiguous — it could read as 'WithFromEnv() consumes POD_NAME, POD_NAMESPACE, NODE_NAME, POD_UID'. But WithFromEnv() only reads OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME). POD_NAME etc. are intermediate Kubernetes env-var substitution variables that k8s interpolates into the OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES value at container start before the process sees any env. The process never directly sees or reads POD_NAME — it only sees the already-expanded OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES string.

This is a subtle but meaningful distinction: a future reader who does not know Kubernetes env-var interpolation semantics might believe the binary has special logic to read POD_NAME, or might wonder why WithFromEnv() is not documented to handle those vars.

Suggested fix: Clarify the indirection, e.g.:
  # Downward API values are injected as env vars; Kubernetes interpolates them
  # into OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES ( syntax) before the process starts.
  # WithFromEnv() in the binary then reads the already-expanded
  # OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES string — no binary-side changes needed.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: store.go instrumentation: defer-ordering is critical but undocumented
description:
File: internal/store/store.go, all instrumentation blocks added in the PR.

Every instrumented method follows this pattern:
  ctx, span := tracer.Start(...)
  defer span.End()             // registered first
  start := time.Now()
  defer func() {
      telemetry.RecordStoreOp(...)   // registered second
      span.RecordError(...)
      span.SetStatus(...)
  }()                          // runs FIRST (LIFO)

The two defers execute in reverse registration order: the inner closure (RecordStoreOp + span status) fires BEFORE span.End(). This ordering is intentional and correct — span status/error must be set before End() seals the span. However, no comment documents why the status-setting defer is registered *after* span.End.

A future reader who sees 'defer span.End()' before the status defer may think the order is irrelevant, or may refactor by pulling defers into a helper in the wrong order, silently breaking span status export.

Suggested fix: Add a brief comment at the pattern site, e.g.:
  // defer span.End() is registered first; the status-setting closure below
  // is registered second and therefore runs first (LIFO), ensuring span
  // status and error are set before End() seals the span.

This is repeated across ~12 methods, so a single anchor comment on the first occurrence (EnsureCollection) would suffice.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: Metric name engram.auth.verify.duration uses three segments vs two for store and embed
description:
File: internal/telemetry/metrics.go, lines 951-957 (diff context)

The three new histograms are registered as:
  engram.store.duration      (two-segment: store.duration)
  engram.embed.duration      (two-segment: embed.duration)
  engram.auth.verify.duration (three-segment: auth.verify.duration)

The auth metric uses a three-segment suffix while the other two use two segments. This inconsistency means:
- Dashboard/alert queries that glob on engram.*.duration will miss auth.verify.duration
- Grafana panel templates using the two-segment pattern will require a special case for auth
- Any future auth metrics (e.g. engram.auth.cache.duration) will be ambiguous in how many segments to use

The de-facto contract for metric names is established the moment consumers build dashboards or alerts.

Suggested fix: rename to engram.auth.duration (matching the two-segment pattern) or establish the three-segment convention consistently and rename the others to engram.store.op.duration / engram.embed.call.duration. Either is fine; consistency is the goal.

The span name is auth.VerifyToken (internal/auth/auth.go line ~104), which is fine as span names have no convention constraint here. Only the metric name is inconsistent.

description:

title: RecordEmbed and RecordAuthVerify metric helpers have no histogram output assertions
description:
TestRecordStoreOpRecordsOperationAndOutcome verifies that RecordStoreOp emits a data point to engram.store.duration with the correct operation and outcome attributes. The analogous helpers RecordEmbed (engram.embed.duration) and RecordAuthVerify (engram.auth.verify.duration) are only exercised by TestRecordHelpersAreNilSafeWhenUninitialised, which calls them against a nil layer — so the real recording path (non-nil layer, correct histogram name, correct outcome attribute) is never asserted.

File: internal/telemetry/metrics_test.go

A copy-paste error (e.g. wiring embedDur to authDur in InitLayerMetrics) would go undetected. The fix is two short table-driven or standalone tests mirroring TestRecordStoreOpRecordsOperationAndOutcome: call InitLayerMetrics with a ManualReader-backed MeterProvider, invoke RecordEmbed/RecordAuthVerify once with nil-err and once with a non-nil error, collect the named histogram, and assert the data point count plus outcome attribute.

title: InitLayerMetrics silently discards histogram-creation errors with no log or startup diagnostic
description:
In internal/telemetry/metrics.go, InitLayerMetrics ignores instrument-creation errors:

  storeDur, _ := m.Float64Histogram("engram.store.duration", ...)
  embedDur, _ := m.Float64Histogram("engram.embed.duration", ...)
  authDur, _ := m.Float64Histogram("engram.auth.verify.duration", ...)

The comment justifies this as 'nil instrument from the no-op provider still records safely.' This is correct for the no-op provider case, and the OTel SDK guarantees a valid no-op on error (not a nil pointer). However, when a real meter provider is configured and an instrument-name conflict exists (e.g. same name registered with a different type), the SDK returns an error and a no-op instrument — all store/embed/auth latency metrics are silently disabled with zero diagnostic signal at startup.

The same pattern exists in NewToolMetrics (pre-existing, out of scope), but this PR adds three new histogram instruments with the same swallow.

Suggestion: log a warning on non-nil errors so a misconfiguration is visible:

  storeDur, err := m.Float64Histogram("engram.store.duration", ...)
  if err != nil {
      slog.Warn("InitLayerMetrics: store histogram unavailable", "err", err)
  }

This is a suggestion rather than a bug because the OTel contract makes it safe in the common case; it only becomes a problem when there is a name conflict which would itself be a configuration error.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES Helm template interpolates operator-controlled resourceAttributes without validation, enabling attribute injection
description:
charts/engram/templates/memory-mcp.yaml line 32 (diff +32): OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is constructed as a Go template string concatenation:

  value: "k8s.pod.name=$(POD_NAME),k8s.namespace.name=$(POD_NAMESPACE),k8s.node.name=$(NODE_NAME),k8s.pod.uid=$(POD_UID){{ with .Values.observability.resourceAttributes }},{{ . }}{{ end }}"

The .Values.observability.resourceAttributes field is interpolated verbatim into the env var. The OTel attribute format is key=value,key=value — there is no shell injection vector here (this is a container env var, not a shell command), but a values.yaml entry like:

  resourceAttributes: "k8s.node.name=attacker-controlled"

would silently override the Downward-API-sourced k8s.node.name by appending a second k=v pair for the same key. The OTel SDK processes OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES with last-writer-wins (or first-writer-wins depending on merge order), so the spoofed value may shadow the legitimate one in the trace backend.

Separately, if the operator interpolates a value that contains a MEM_* env var reference (e.g. $(MEM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET) in a future deployment), Kubernetes container env var interpolation would expand it, potentially exposing the secret as a resource attribute.

Fix: add a brief Helm NOTES.txt or values.yaml comment warning that resourceAttributes values are operator-supplied and must not contain secret values or keys that duplicate the auto-populated Downward-API keys (k8s.pod.name, k8s.namespace.name, k8s.node.name, k8s.pod.uid). Optionally strip leading/trailing commas and validate format in a _helpers.tpl helper.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: WithProcess() exports process.command_args on every OTel signal; future secret flags would leak to trace backend
description:
internal/telemetry/providers.go — buildResource() includes resource.WithProcess() which captures os.Args onto the process.command_args resource attribute, exported on every OTel signal (traces, metrics, logs). The comment at line 1129 correctly identifies this and states engram flags are non-secret today, with a documented migration path to WithProcessRuntimeName()+WithProcessRuntimeVersion().

The concern is forward-looking: if any future flag accepts a secret value (e.g. --oidc-client-secret, --api-key, or a path like --tls-key-file that reveals filesystem layout), that secret would appear on every exported signal in every trace backend, metric store, and log pipeline the operator has configured. Trace backends are often durably retained and readable by operators beyond the security perimeter of the application.

Current state: config is env-first (MEM_* env vars); flags today carry only URLs and non-secret identifiers (--oidc-issuer, --oidc-audience, --addr, etc.). The existing comment is an adequate acknowledgement for today.

Hardening recommendation: Add a CI lint or go vet check that rejects new cobra flags whose names match a secret-sensitive pattern (e.g. *key*, *secret*, *token*, *password*, *credential*). Alternatively, proactively swap resource.WithProcess() for resource.WithProcessRuntimeName()+resource.WithProcessRuntimeVersion() now, before a secret flag is added, accepting the loss of process.pid and process.command_args. This removes the risk class permanently rather than relying on future authors to remember the comment.
close_reason: PASS turn 1; suggestion-severity, non-blocking. Preserved on PR #88 review comment for maintainer triage.

title: Inject k8s resource attributes via chart Downward API, not Go SDK detectors
description:
## Context

A production-grade OTel resource needs k8s attributes (pod name, namespace, node name, pod UID) when running in Kubernetes. The Go OTel SDK offers experimental (x.Resource-gated) k8s detectors, but the engram binary runs on laptops, in Docker, and in k8s. The design must decide where k8s attribute injection belongs: the binary (SDK detectors) or the deployment layer (Helm chart).

## Decision

K8s resource attributes are injected by the Helm chart via the Downward API into OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, which resource.WithFromEnv() already consumes. The binary's resource.New() adds no k8s detector. Exactly one OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES env entry is emitted (k8s attrs folded with any user-supplied observability.resourceAttributes) to avoid k8s last-wins duplication.

## Rationale

- Keeps the binary deployment-agnostic: the same image is correct on a laptop, in Docker, and in k8s, with the orchestrator supplying its own identity (12-factor).\n- The k8s SDK detector is experimental; the Downward API is stable Kubernetes functionality.\n- OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is already consumed by WithFromEnv(); no new binary code path.\n- Clear responsibility boundary: the chart knows deployment topology, the binary should not.

## Alternatives Considered

- Go k8s resource detector in binary: self-contained and needs no chart config, but uses an experimental API, adds a k8s API client dependency, requires a pod-metadata API call at startup, and makes the binary k8s-aware. Rejected.

## Consequences

Positive: no binary dependency on the k8s API server; non-k8s deployments are unaffected and need no stub. Negative: running the binary in k8s without the chart (raw manifests) means k8s attrs are absent unless the Downward API env block is replicated manually. Neutral: k8s.pod.uid from the Downward API gives a stable pod identity alongside the per-process UUID service.instance.id.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Reuse OTel-standard env vars for sampler and export interval; add no MEM_* equivalents
description:
## Context

engram's config convention is env-first MEM_* vars with cobra flag overrides. The OTel SDK already reads OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL natively (sdktrace.NewTracerProvider and metric.NewPeriodicReader honor them when no WithSampler/WithInterval option is passed, which is engram's case). The chart did not previously expose these knobs. The design must choose whether to surface them as MEM_* vars or template the OTel-standard vars directly.

## Decision

Sampler and metric export interval are configured exclusively through the OTel-standard env vars. The Helm chart templates them via observability.traces.sampler, observability.traces.samplerArg, and observability.metrics.exportInterval, with no MEM_* counterparts and no Go code change.

## Rationale

- Deepwiki grounding confirmed the SDK reads these vars without explicit code; MEM_* wrappers would duplicate SDK behavior with no benefit and risk precedence bugs if both namespaces were set.\n- Telemetry tuning (OTEL_*) is already a distinct concern from engram domain config (MEM_*); sampler and interval are SDK concerns.\n- Avoids minting a new MEM_ knob for every future OTel-standard var.

## Alternatives Considered

- Invent MEM_TRACES_SAMPLER / MEM_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL: consistent with the MEM_* namespace, but requires code to parse and forward to the SDK, duplicating native behavior and risking double-set precedence bugs. Rejected.

## Consequences

Positive: no code change; any OTel-standard sampler works immediately; operators can override with standard OTEL_ vars outside the chart. Negative: the config convention is split (MEM_* domain vs OTEL_* telemetry) and contributors must know which namespace owns which knob. Neutral: the chart observability block is the canonical operator interface, with direct OTEL_ override as an escape hatch.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Spans carry engram.owner only; exclude actor and email as PII
description:
## Context

When adding caller identity as a span attribute across the store/embed/auth/tool spans, the design must choose which identity fields to surface in the trace backend. The server tracks two identity fields: owner (opaque OIDC sub, the authz key) and actor (human-readable email or preferred_username). Trace backends (e.g. Tempo, Jaeger) store spans durably and may be readable by operators who should not see PII.

## Decision

Span attributes across every instrumented seam carry engram.owner (the opaque OIDC sub) and never actor. Actor (email/username) remains only on structured log lines, correlated to spans via trace_id/span_id.

## Rationale

- Email and preferred_username are PII; trace backends must not become a PII store (data-minimization).\n- The opaque sub is sufficient for cross-request correlation and per-owner latency analysis without exposing human-readable identity.\n- Actor already appears on structured access-log lines; logs are the correct channel for human-readable identity, and the slog *Context-variant rule keeps them correlated to the trace.

## Alternatives Considered

- owner + actor (sub + email/username): human-readable identity on spans speeds debugging, but embeds PII in traces, attaching GDPR/CCPA obligations to trace retention. Rejected.\n- No caller identity on spans: zero PII risk, but cannot correlate a slow/erroring span to an owner, defeating per-user latency analysis. Rejected.

## Consequences

Positive: trace backends stay PII-free; consistent with the authz model where sub is the canonical identity. Negative: debugging a specific user's trace requires a sub->actor lookup via logs; rotated subs cannot be re-attributed in historical traces. Neutral: actor stays available on trace-correlated log lines.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Instrument store/embed/auth with inline spans, not a decorator layer
description:
## Context

engram's three inner packages (internal/store, internal/embed, internal/auth) previously had zero direct OpenTelemetry instrumentation; they were visible only through transport-level otelgrpc/otelhttp auto-instrumentation. Adding domain spans requires choosing between inline spans (each public method calls otel.Tracer directly) and a decorator/wrapper interface layer that intercepts calls without coupling the package to the OTel API.

## Decision

Each public method in store, embed, and auth creates its own span inline via a package-level otel.Tracer (attributes at creation, RecordError+SetStatus on the error path, defer span.End()). Per-operation duration metrics are delegated to thin helper functions in internal/telemetry (RecordStoreOp/RecordEmbed/RecordAuthVerify) so domain packages never import the meter; the dependency is one-way (domain -> telemetry, never the reverse).

## Rationale

- The Go OTel SDK guarantees a no-op tracer/meter when no provider is registered, so inline spans cost nothing when telemetry is disabled (preserves ADR engram-uxh).\n- Samplers only observe attributes set at span creation; inline instrumentation is the only pattern that can set engram.owner/engram.scope before the sampling decision.\n- A decorator over 19 store methods adds more abstraction than the problem warrants, and result-derived attributes (result_count, error detail) cannot be set by an outer wrapper without return-value inspection.\n- Routing metric recording through internal/telemetry keeps histogram instruments at a single registration point.

## Alternatives Considered

- Decorator / wrapper interface layer: isolates telemetry outside domain packages and is easy to swap or disable, but requires new interface types for ~19 store methods, doubles the API surface, adds indirection, and cannot set in-method attributes from outside. Rejected as over-abstracted and non-idiomatic for Go OTel.

## Consequences

Positive: span attributes are available at the correct call site with no return-value inspection; new store methods are instrumented by following the in-file pattern; no new interface types. Negative: store/embed/auth now import go.opentelemetry.io/otel, and reversing the decision touches every instrumented method; instrumentation logic is distributed across three packages. Neutral: the telemetry helper boundary separates the tracing concern (inline) from the metrics concern (centralized).
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: C-3: identity-map derived is defensive no-op in select.svelte
description:
Pattern C-3 (defensive validation for impossible cases).

File: ui/src/lib/components/ui/select/select.svelte, line 1417.

The added line:
  const items = $derived(options.map((o) => ({ value: o.value, label: o.label })));

maps every Option to an object of the same shape { value: string; label: string }. The prop type already guarantees this shape, so the transform is an identity — it cannot change the output. A careful human author would pass `options` directly as `{items}` (or just rename the prop binding) rather than adding a no-op intermediate derived. The only reason to write this is defensive uncertainty about the bits-ui primitive's type requirements, which is a classic AI tell.

Suggested fix: remove the derived and pass options directly:
  <SelectPrimitive.Root type="single" bind:value {onValueChange} items={options}>

This clusters with the padded file-level comment in the same new file (see C-6 note below), strengthening the provenance signal.

title: select.svelte: items derived is identity map — pass options directly
description:
ui/src/lib/components/ui/select/select.svelte line 17:

  const items = $derived(options.map((o) => ({ value: o.value, label: o.label })));

The Option type is { value: string; label: string }, so this map produces objects with exactly the same shape as the input. It is a pure identity copy that allocates a new array and reactive dependency on every options change. The SelectPrimitive.Root {items} prop can receive options directly:

  <SelectPrimitive.Root type="single" bind:value {onValueChange} items={options}>

The separate items derived can be deleted entirely. The selectedLabel derived is legitimate and unaffected.

title: errorBanner not cleared on navigation — stale error persists across routes
description:
ui/src/lib/errors.ts / ui/src/routes/+layout.svelte

The errorBanner writable store is a module-level singleton with no automatic clearing on navigation. The only way to dismiss it is the explicit '✕' button in the layout banner. There is no beforeNavigate or afterNavigate hook calling clearError().

Consequence: a transient error from one route (e.g., a failed listMemories on /observe) leaves the red role="alert" banner visible after the user navigates to an unrelated route (/search, /discovery, /). The banner then falsely signals an error state on pages whose queries all succeeded. Screen readers will announce the stale error.

Suggested fix: add a beforeNavigate handler in +layout.svelte:

  import { beforeNavigate } from '$app/navigation';
  beforeNavigate(() => clearError());

This is the standard SvelteKit idiom for per-navigation cleanup. It only clears on inter-route navigation, not on query retries within the same page.

description: ui/src/routes/discovery/+page.svelte declares const q = derived(page.url.searchParams.get q) and const scope = derived(page.url.searchParams.get scope) at the top of the script block. title: Go: List 4-tuple return ([]Memory, uint64, bool, error) discards total/approximate at MCP tool call site
description:
internal/server/tools.go line 310-311: the MCP list_memory tool calls store.List and discards total and approximate with blank identifiers (ms, _, _, err := d.st.List(...)). This is correct for now because the MCP tool has no pagination UI, but the 4-tuple return type makes it easy for future callers to silently miss them.

A named result struct (e.g. ListResult{Memories []Memory; Total uint64; Approximate bool}) would make discarding total/approximate visible to a reviewer and give the IDE a natural place to document the approximate semantics. The 4-tuple is idiomatic Go and not wrong per se, but the blank discards at the only non-proto call site are a mild design smell given that approximate carries a load-bearing meaning (scanCap ceiling reached).

This is a suggestion only — no real bug is reachable from the blank-identifier discard in tools.go since that path doesn't surface pagination to callers at all.
close_reason: Accepted by design: the MCP list_memory tool intentionally discards total/approximate (its contract returns []Memory); the Connect handler consumes them. Not a defect.

description: ui/src/lib/components/MemoryDetail.svelte line 3397: The error branch renders only 'failed to load' regardless of the Connect error code. title: next pagination button never disabled — user can page past final results with no feedback
description: ui/src/routes/observe/+page.svelte line 4167: The 'next ›' button has no disabled condition. The server now returns total and approximate in ListMemoriesResponse, so the client has the information needed to disable the button when params.offset + PAGE_LIMIT >= $listQ.data?.total. Currently a user can keep clicking 'next' after the last page, each click fires a request, the server returns an empty memories array with the correct total, and the list renders the 'no memories in this scope/filter' empty-state message — which is misleading because memories do exist, just on earlier pages. Suggested fix: compute isLastPage = $listQ.data != null && BigInt(params.offset + PAGE_LIMIT) >= $listQ.data.total and apply disabled={isLastPage || $listQ.isLoading}.
close_reason: Duplicate of engram-af5.12 (observe 'next' pager has no upper-bound guard).

title: Search route setQuery drops existing scope param; SearchPalette ignores prop changes
description:
Two related issues in the search lane:

1) ui/src/routes/search/+page.svelte:22 — setQuery() rebuilds the URL as '/search?q=...' and discards any existing 'scope' param. But the search query reads scope from the URL (line 15: scope = searchParams.get('scope')) and passes it to engram.searchMemories({ query, scope, k }). So once a user has a scope-narrowed search, submitting a new query silently widens it back to all scopes. The discovery route's setQuery (discovery/+page.svelte:17) correctly preserves scope; search should do the same (preserve via URLSearchParams as the select() handler on line 23 already does).

2) ui/src/lib/components/SearchPalette.svelte:3 — let q = $state(value) seizes the prop only at init. In Svelte 5, reassigning the parent's 'value' prop does not update this local $state, so after navigation (e.g. browser back/forward, or programmatic URL change to a different q) the searchbox shows stale text out of sync with the active query. Use $derived or a $effect to resync, or bind through a prop callback.

Both are correctness/UX defects rather than crashes — suggestion severity.
close_reason: Addressed in the UI overhaul / store fix (scope-preserving search, NotFound detail msg, mode-watcher comment, honest result footer, shared CSS classes, package-level listFilter, multi-category test).

title: Observe console 'next' page button never disables, pages past end into empty results
description:
ui/src/routes/observe/+page.svelte:56. The 'next ›' button always increments offset by PAGE_LIMIT with no upper bound: onclick={() => navigate({ offset: params.offset + PAGE_LIMIT })}. Unlike 'prev' (disabled={params.offset === 0}), 'next' has no disabled guard.

The list response already carries total (List returns the real matched count, and MemoryList receives total). So the component can compute whether a next page exists. Without the guard, the user can keep clicking 'next' indefinitely; the store clamps Offset>=total to an empty page (store.go:359), so the UI shows 'no memories in this scope/filter' on a scope that does have memories — a confusing dead-end.

Fix: disable next when params.offset + PAGE_LIMIT >= Number(total) (guard against the bigint/number boundary; total is bigint). Suggestion severity: no crash or data issue, purely a pagination UX defect.
close_reason: Duplicate of engram-af5.12 (observe 'next' pager has no upper-bound guard).

title: search/+page.svelte passes synthetic total to MemoryList, masking SearchMemoriesResponse's lack of a server-side total
description:
In ui/src/routes/search/+page.svelte (line ~27), MemoryList receives:

  total={BigInt($searchQ.data?.memories.length ?? 0)}

This synthesizes a total from the returned page length rather than a server-supplied count. SearchMemoriesResponse does not include a total field (only memories[]), so this is accurate given the current proto — the search path genuinely has no pre-page total.

However, MemoryList's footer renders: '{memories.length} of {total}' which will always show N of N (e.g. '5 of 5'), which is misleading to users since SearchMemories returns the top-k nearest neighbors and there may be more matching records beyond the k cap. This is not a contract violation (the proto contract for SearchMemoriesResponse is unchanged), but it is a UI contract inconsistency between the observe (paginated, real total) and search (k-capped, synthetic total) paths that uses the same MemoryList component.

Suggestion: either add a totalIsExact: boolean prop to MemoryList so it can render 'top 50 results' instead of '50 of 50', or pass total as undefined / 0n on the search path and suppress the count footer. No proto change needed.
close_reason: Addressed in the UI overhaul / store fix (scope-preserving search, NotFound detail msg, mode-watcher comment, honest result footer, shared CSS classes, package-level listFilter, multi-category test).

title: ListMemoriesResponse.total/approximate fields are new optional proto3 fields with zero defaults — additive and wire-compatible
description:
COMPATIBLE finding (documentation/hardening).

The proto changes are correctly additive:
- ListMemoriesRequest gains offset=3, categories=4, visibility=5 — all new field numbers, all optional (proto3), zero value = previous behavior (offset 0, no filter).
- ListMemoriesResponse gains total=2, approximate=3 — new field numbers, optional; existing clients that ignore unknown fields receive them silently.
- No existing field numbers were reused, renamed, or removed.
- buf.yaml uses FILE-level breaking check (not WIRE_JSON), which would catch field number reuse and type changes. The diff is clean per that ruleset.

One hardening suggestion: the visibility field (ListMemoriesRequest.visibility = 5) accepts any string. The proto and the store both document the valid values as '' | 'private' | 'shared', but there is no protovalidate constraint enforcing this. The project does not yet use protovalidate elsewhere (no buf.validate imports in proto/), so this is not an inconsistency — just an optional improvement if protovalidate is ever adopted.

No action required on this finding; documenting as COMPATIBLE/additive.
close_reason: Not actionable — confirms the proto change is additive/wire-compatible (a strength, not a defect).

title: ListMemories gains offset pagination and server-side filters
description:
## Context

The v1 Observe pane needs paginated listing with left-rail category/visibility filters. Today ListMemoriesRequest is {scope, limit} only; no offset, no filters, and the response has no total. The footer needs an accurate 'N of total' that reflects active filters. Choices: where to filter (client vs server) and which pagination model (offset vs cursor).

## Decision

Extend ListMemoriesRequest with uint64 offset, repeated string categories, string visibility; extend ListMemoriesResponse with uint64 total and bool approximate. The store applies filters server-side, returns the pre-truncation matched count, clamps to an empty page when offset>=total. Additive fields keep buf breaking green and leave the MCP path unaffected.

## Rationale

- Client-side filtering produces inaccurate totals when combined with server pagination — server-side filtering is the only honest-footer model.\n- Offset pagination is sufficient within the existing scanCap=1000 ceiling for the single-operator use case.\n- Additive proto fields are backward-compatible; the MCP/CLI ListMemories path is unaffected.\n- The approximate flag honestly signals the scanCap boundary.

## Alternatives Considered

**Client-side filtering of server pages** — no backend change, but 'showing 3 of 50' lies (50 was unfiltered); accurate totals need fetching everything. Rejected.\n**Cursor pagination** — stable under concurrent writes, but needs cursor tokens, prev-history, no page jumping, more store complexity. Deferred.

## Consequences

Positive: footer count accurate for any filter; non-breaking proto (MCP/CLI unaffected); store stays scroll-and-slice (no cursor state). Negative: offset can duplicate/skip records if data changes between page fetches; approximate needs a UI affordance. Neutral: cursor pagination + free-text server filters deferred.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: SPA-fallback static handler: serve index.html for client routes
description:
## Context

The engram binary serves the SPA under /ui/ from an embedded FS via http.FileServer. A client-routed adapter-static SPA needs any /ui/* path with no real asset to return index.html (200), not 404, so the client router can handle it. The current StaticHandler (internal/webauth/static.go) does not.

## Decision

Wrap StaticHandler with SPA-fallback logic: if the embedded FS has the requested file, serve it; if the path has no file extension (a client route), serve index.html with 200; else 404. A unit test covers the fallback-vs-404 boundary.

## Rationale

- Client-routed SPAs require an index.html fallback for refresh + deep links — a structural requirement of adapter-static + client routing (engram-0lu).\n- The file-extension boundary is explicit and testable.\n- 404 for genuinely missing assets preserves correct behavior.\n- The Go binary is the only server; no nginx/CDN fallback layer exists.

## Alternatives Considered

**Hash-based routing (#/observe)** — any static server works, but hash URLs aren't server-shareable, non-standard, incompatible with SvelteKit default routing. Rejected.\n**Leave http.FileServer as-is** — refresh on /ui/observe 404s; deep links broken; incompatible with URL-driven state. Rejected.

## Consequences

Positive: refresh + deep links resolve correctly; URL-driven state is only viable with this in place. Negative: the extension heuristic can misclassify extensionless asset paths (rare for Vite output). Neutral: change confined to static.go + its test.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Drive SPA shell state via URL parameters
description:
## Context

The Observe three-pane view has state: selected scope, category/visibility filters, search query, selected memory id. These can live in ephemeral component state or the URL query string. The SPA-fallback handler serves index.html for any /ui/* path, so URLs survive refresh.

## Decision

Encode scope, category filters, visibility, query, and selected id in the URL query string. The shell reads/writes URL params; panes are stateless prop consumers. Offset resets to 0 on filter change.

## Rationale

- Deep-linkable views are load-bearing for an operator tool (share/reference a filtered view or a specific memory).\n- URL state is the single source of truth for the svelte-query cache keys.\n- Browser back/forward gives filter undo for free.\n- The SPA-fallback handler makes deep links survive refresh.

## Alternatives Considered

**Ephemeral component/store state** — simpler, no serialization, but lost on refresh, no back/forward restore, no deep-linking. Rejected.

## Consequences

Positive: bookmarkable/shareable filtered views + memory details; back/forward history; single source of truth for query keys. Negative: shell serializes filter state to/from URL; offset must reset to 0 on filter change. Neutral: panes become stateless, simplifying their test surface.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs

title: Use @tanstack/svelte-query as the SPA data layer
description:
## Context

The operator-console SPA calls five ConnectRPC read endpoints with loading/error/empty states, stale-time caching, and stable query keys that compose with pagination + filter params. SvelteKit load() is server-side and unavailable in an adapter-static SSR-off SPA (engram-0lu); hand-rolled stores would re-implement dedup/cache/invalidation.

## Decision

Adopt @tanstack/svelte-query as the sole async data layer. Every RPC call is a query with a stable composite key (e.g. [rpc, scope, filters, limit, offset]); loading/error/empty handled declaratively; staleTime tuned per query. The connect-es client stays a thin singleton that svelte-query wraps.

## Rationale

- load() is unavailable with adapter-static + SSR=false (engram-0lu); client-side fetching is the only option.\n- Query keys including scope/filters/limit/offset make cache invalidation on filter/page change automatic.\n- Built-in states eliminate per-component state machines across five views.\n- staleTime avoids redundant refetches on back-navigation.\n- Scales as the surface grows observe->correct->author.

## Alternatives Considered

**Hand-rolled Svelte stores** — no dep but re-implements dedup/loading/stale/invalidation; grows complex. Rejected.\n**SvelteKit load()** — first-class ergonomics but server-side only; structurally incompatible with adapter-static SSR-off. Rejected.

## Consequences

Positive: declarative states without boilerplate; stable cache; instant cached back-navigation. Negative: ~15kB bundle; query-key shape must stay consistent (drift = silent cache miss). Neutral: connect-es client remains a thin singleton.
notes: Amended 2026-06-11 (engram-gx2 / PR pending): removed the '(v5)' version pin from the Decision line to make the decision version-agnostic — the library choice is the decision; the version lives in package.json. Editorial only; decision unchanged. Pre-existing latent defect NOT fixed here: Rationale + Alternatives store literal backslash-n instead of real newlines (renders literally); likely affects sibling capture-adrs-batch ADRs too.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via capture-adrs
