title: engram plugin ships no bundled MCP server; /engram-setup is the sole registration path
description:
## Context

The skill/engram Claude Code plugin bundled a `.mcp.json` declaring an `engram` MCP server at `${ENGRAM_MCP_URL:-http://localhost:8080}`. A plugin `.mcp.json` is static — it cannot prompt for a URL or auth mode, so it must bake in a default. engram's deployment posture is self-hosted, OAuth-gated, and usually behind a gateway, so the localhost default is wrong for most deployers. In `/mcp` it produced a permanent, confusing `plugin:engram:engram · failed / needs-auth` entry, while being strictly redundant with the user-scope server `/engram-setup` already registers — and user scope ALWAYS outranks a plugin-namespaced definition, so the bundle never actually won name resolution.

## Decision

Ship no bundled MCP server. `/engram-setup` is the single canonical registration path; it runs `claude mcp add --transport http engram <url> --scope user [...]` to write a USER-SCOPE server (a plugin command cannot programmatically write MCP config itself, hence the generator command). Concretely: delete `skill/engram/.mcp.json`, drop the `mcpServers` key from `plugin.json`, and update the validating tests, README, and the `/engram-setup` prose. Implemented in PR #16, released in v0.3.0.

## Rationale

Removes a permanently-failing, confusing duplicate entry; gives one obvious setup path that adapts to any URL + auth mode (OAuth, pre-registered client, bearer, none); and eliminates the fragile `${VAR:-default}` env-interpolation contract. Because user scope always outranks a plugin def, the bundle provided no functional value it did not already get from `/engram-setup`.

## Alternatives Considered

(1) Keep the bundled `.mcp.json` as-is — rejected: a permanent failed entry for the common remote/gateway deployment. (2) Keep the def but drop the localhost fallback (`${ENGRAM_MCP_URL}` with no default) — rejected: an unset/empty var resolves to a malformed URL that fails worse, since Claude Code does not reliably treat an empty URL as "disabled". (3) Generalize the bundled `.mcp.json` via env interpolation (the prior 2026-06-02-generalize-engram-client-config design) — superseded: it still ships a wrong-for-most default and the failed entry.

## Consequences

No more confusing failed/duplicate entry; a single obvious setup path. No zero-config localhost path — even local users run `/engram-setup` (pointing it at `http://localhost:8080`). A marketplace copy installed before v0.3.0 keeps its stale `.mcp.json` until refreshed. Supersedes the `2026-06-02-generalize-engram-client-config` design; those specs/plans remain as dated historical records.
close_reason: Accepted ADR filed via /adr new (retrospective; implemented in #16, released v0.3.0)

title: Design: generalize engram client plugin config + auth for OSS
description: PR #9 ships skill/engram/.mcp.json hardcoding a private homelab endpoint (litellm.fzymgc.house/mcp/engram) and an OAuth-via-gateway auth assumption. For engram as an OSS project, the bundled client plugin must let any consumer point at their own self-hosted engram server with their own auth posture (direct OIDC bearer vs OAuth gateway vs none) without editing repo files. Explore: env-var interpolation in plugin .mcp.json vs a bootstrap/init skill/command that generates local MCP config; how it relates to the engram server's own --oidc-issuer auth; impact on PR #9.
notes:
grounding/claude-code-guide: plugin-bundled .mcp.json DOES interpolate ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default}; ALSO ${user_config.KEY}. plugin.json 'userConfig' is the first-class per-install prompt mechanism (string/number/bool/dir/file; sensitive->keychain). NO supported way for a skill/command to programmatically write MCP config into settings. http MCP auth fields: headers (interpolated), oauth{clientId,clientSecret,callbackPort,authServerMetadataUrl,scopes}, headersHelper. OAuth auto-discovery triggers on 401/403 + WWW-Authenticate / RFC9728 resource-metadata. Plugin servers are LOWEST precedence; consumer overrides by same-name server in project/user scope.
grounding/probe: engram SERVER already supports server-native OAuth discovery — cmd/engram/serve.go has --oidc-issuer (MEM_OIDC_ISSUER, enables bearer enforcement), --oidc-audience, AND --oidc-resource-metadata (MEM_OIDC_RESOURCE_METADATA = RFC9728 protected-resource-metadata endpoint). So a directly-exposed engram server returns 401+metadata and Claude Code auto-discovers OAuth WITHOUT a litellm gateway. internal/auth validates Authentik OIDC (JWKS+issuer+expiry, optional aud). Server default listen :8080. README documents helm install + MEM_* env. The litellm gateway is the USER's deployment choice, not a requirement.
grounding/probe: engram server mounts mcp.NewStreamableHTTPHandler at ROOT via http.ListenAndServe(listenAddr, handler) (cmd/engram/serve.go:54-59) — no path prefix. So direct-server MCP endpoint = http://host:8080 (root); the /mcp/engram path is purely the litellm gateway's routing. Confirms url must be fully configurable (path shapes differ), OSS default = http://localhost:8080.
grounding/claude-code-guide(2): claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> [--scope local|project|user] [--header 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>'] [--client-id --client-secret --callback-port]. scope user -> ~/.claude.json all projects; project -> .mcp.json. OAuth purely 401-discovered (add bare, then /mcp). Plugin slash commands: commands/<name>.md w/ frontmatter (description, argument-hint, disable-model-invocation); body instructs Claude to run bash + ask questions. Decision: /engram-setup shells to claude mcp add (no hand-written JSON).
decisions: (A) generalize skill/engram/.mcp.json to url ${ENGRAM_MCP_URL:-http://localhost:8080} + generic oauth.callbackPort (covers direct-OIDC/gateway/no-auth via on-demand 401). (C) add /engram-setup command (commands/engram-setup.md) shelling to claude mcp add --scope user per auth-mode incl bearer --header. All 4 postures first-class. Fold A+C+docs+tests INTO PR #9 before merge. No userConfig (avoids marketplace/symlink divergence). bundled .mcp.json stays zero-config default; user-scope override shadows it via precedence.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-02-generalize-engram-client-config-design.md
design-review round 1 NOT READY: (Critical) Testing section omits that the .mcp.json url assertion must REPLACE the existing test_mcp_declares_engram_server endswith('/mcp/engram') check (will break CI). (Important) --client-secret flag arity unverified. (Minor) add unset-vs-empty ${VAR:-default} callout to Docs; clarify 4 postures vs 5 table rows (pre-registered OAuth is a sub-variant).
grounding/claude-code-guide(3): claude mcp add --client-secret is a BOOLEAN flag (prompts masked; bypass with MCP_CLIENT_SECRET env var); --client-id takes a value; --callback-port takes an int (mcp.md 'Use pre-configured OAuth credentials'). Spec's '--client-secret' (no inline value) is correct. Resolves design-review round-1 Important finding.
design-review READY (round 2). All round-1 findings fixed (Testing 'replaces' language; --client-secret arity grounded; unset-vs-empty in Docs; 4-vs-5 postures clarified); no new issues. Proceeding to implement A+C+docs into PR #9 per user direction (skipping separate writing-plans; spec is implementation-detailed).
IMPLEMENTED in PR #9 (engram-w8b-design). A: .mcp.json url -> ${ENGRAM_MCP_URL:-http://localhost:8080} + on-demand oauth; private-host guard (no fzymgc/litellm in shipped bundle); test pinned to the literal (TDD red->green). C: skill/engram/commands/engram-setup.md slash command (interview -> claude mcp add --scope user per auth mode: OAuth/gateway/pre-registered/bearer/none), .licenserc exempts skill/**/commands/*.md (frontmatter line-1), command-shape test. Docs: README 'Connect your coding agent' section (install both paths, ENGRAM_MCP_URL, /engram-setup, 4-posture matrix). 36 tests pass; all 6 CI jobs green. Remaining human step: live round-trip with the generalized config against a real engram server.

title: Unify UI test DOM via vitest 4 browser mode
description: DESIGN-SCALE. The ui/ suite juggles two DOM emulators because neither does both jobs: happy-dom (default) drives bits-ui (Tabs + Select both work) but mis-sanitizes DOMPurify (cure53 XSS bypass); jsdom 29.1.1 sanitizes DOMPurify correctly but breaks bits-ui (Tabs throw 'ResizeObserver is not defined', Select throws in onpointerdown). Consolidating on either emulator loses something — proven by probe, see memory f9cbc7b0. The only single-env unifier is vitest 4 browser mode (real browser DOM via Playwright/WebdriverIO provider): bits-ui AND DOMPurify both run correctly, eliminating the per-file // @vitest-environment split. vitest 4.1.9 is already installed. Sean's stated preference (2026-06-27): this tooling change is the best long-term answer. Scope to evaluate: (1) provider choice (Playwright vs WebdriverIO) + CI cost (browser binary download, runtime, caching); (2) migration of ~15 test files off node @testing-library/svelte onto vitest-browser-svelte locators; (3) whether to fully drop jsdom+happy-dom or keep a fast node tier for pure-logic tests (queries/app.css). Run the formal design lifecycle (brainstorming -> writing-plans -> plan-to-beads); do NOT implement directly from this bead.
design: Candidate: vitest browser mode with Playwright provider + vitest-browser-svelte. Open question: hybrid (browser tier for component/DOM tests, node tier for logic) vs all-browser. Required CI gate today is only 'ui vendored-asset drift' (pnpm build), so adding a browser test job is additive, not a required-check rename (see memory protect-main-ruleset).

lesson: The plan's verbatim Task-1 vite.config.ts STALLS (60s browser-connect timeout). Root cause: svelte.config.js sets kit.paths.base='/ui', so sveltekit() forces Vite base='/ui', which 404s vitest 4 browser-mode orchestrator assets (/__vitest_browser__/*, /@fs/*). Fix (now committed canonical in ui/vite.config.ts): a 'forceTestBase' Plugin ordered AFTER sveltekit() returning {base:'/'} only when process.env.VITEST is set. Any task copying the plan's verbatim config MUST carry this forward. The plan's levers 1-3 (optimizeDeps/inline/isolate) are INEFFECTIVE for this cause. Cosmetic warning 'options will be overridden by SvelteKit: base' prints every browser run (kit #15361) — harmless, plugin still wins.
lesson: PLAN DEFECT — the pre-flight API-shift table (line ~33) maps 'getByLabelText -> getByLabel', which is WRONG. vitest-browser-svelte's render() result exposes getByLabelText (testing-library style), NOT getByLabel (that's a Playwright PAGE-level method, absent on the render-result selectors object). Verified in @vitest/browser/dist/context.js: it spreads getByAltText/getByLabelText/getByPlaceholder/getByRole/getByTestId/getByText/getByTitle. So KEEP getByLabelText unchanged when migrating. Hit on Task 6 (MemoryRow); any later task querying an aria-label must use getByLabelText. (Note getByLabelText->getByLabel in the table is the only wrong row; getByPlaceholderText->getByPlaceholder and getByLabelText were conflated.)
lesson: A FAILED vitest browser-tier run writes failure artifacts — __screenshots__/ PNGs next to the test file (e.g. ui/src/lib/components/__screenshots__/) and ui/.vitest-attachments/*.png. These got swept into the MemoryRow commit before being squashed out. Now gitignored (chore commit xyomylsu: ui/**/__screenshots__/ + ui/.vitest-attachments/), so they no longer dirty the tree or risk a bad commit. Passing runs emit nothing. If an implementer sees these after a red run, they're expected debris — clean/ignore, do not commit; the test-file rename/rewrite is the only intended change per migration.
lesson: getByRole name-matching SEMANTICS DIFFER between libraries. @testing-library treats a STRING name as a full/EXACT match; Playwright (vitest-browser locators) treats a string name as case-insensitive SUBSTRING match. So a verbatim port of getByRole('option', { name: 'Search' }) can match MULTIPLE options (e.g. 'Search' AND 'Search memories for...') -> Playwright strict-mode violation (refuses to click 2+ matches). FIX: add exact:true to string names whenever the name is/could-be a substring of another visible element's accessible name -> getByRole('option', { name: 'Search', exact: true }). This restores testing-library's exact semantics; it is a faithful translation, not a weakening. Use a REGEX only when substring is genuinely intended and resolves ONE element. Hit on Task 7 (CommandPalette test 3). Tasks 8-9: pre-check the rendered option/element set for substring collisions before porting verbatim.

title: engram reindex: resumable reindex via skip-by-content-hash
description: Deferred feature from PR #123 review (epic engram-3ge), split out of engram-5xa. Reindex is currently all-or-nothing with no rollback (idempotent re-run overwrites). title: Add tags as an optional filter condition on search_memory / list_memory
description:
Today recall is pure vector-over-content: Store.Search and Store.List build Qdrant filters only on scope/category/owner/visibility plus the active-window conditions — never on tags. So tags are presentational, not a recall dimension. This bead makes tags a first-class filter: search_memory/list_memory gain an optional tags parameter, and the store adds a Qdrant condition over the tags payload list (already persisted via store.go payload()/fromPayload()).

This is the read-path complement to engram-4sw (which adds tag MUTATION on the write path). Tag-filtered recall is what makes mutable tags worth having; engram-4sw is what keeps a tag taxonomy correctable. Neither hard-blocks the other — ship in either order.

Open design questions (warrant a short brainstorm/ADR before implementing):
1. SEMANTIC-INTENT TENSION: the curating-memory design is deliberately semantic-first / zero-junk so agents don't manage a tag taxonomy. Tag-filtered recall invites exactly that. Decide whether this aligns with design intent (ADR) and update the curating-memory skill guidance accordingly.
2. AND vs OR semantics: match-all (Must of NewMatch per tag) vs match-any (Should). Default + override?
3. Interaction with vector ranking: Qdrant applies the filter as a hard pre-filter, then ANN-ranks survivors — confirm that is the desired 'filter then semantically rank' behavior.
4. PAYLOAD INDEX: filtering an unindexed payload field in Qdrant is supported but slow; check whether the tags field needs a keyword payload index added at collection-ensure time (current filters index scope/category/owner — verify tags).

Touch points: internal/store/store.go (Search/List filter builders, collection ensure/index), internal/server/tools.go (searchArgs/listArgs + handlers), docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md, CLAUDE.md Memory contract, curating-memory skill.
design:
Qdrant payload already carries tags as a string list, so filtering needs no data migration — but likely a keyword payload index for performance. Default AND (Must) semantics; consider an explicit match-mode. Gate on an ADR first: does tag-filtered recall fit the semantic-first design intent? Cross-refs engram-4sw (write-path mutation).

VERIFIED: tags do NOT participate in recall today, by EITHER mechanism. The embedder only ever sees content (storeMemory/updateMemory: Embed(a.Content); searchMemory: Embed(a.Query)); tags are written to the Qdrant payload but no recall path reads them — neither the vector nor any filter condition. So tags are doubly presentational; a tag only sways a search if its words also appear in content.

ADR must choose deliberately between two distinct mechanisms (not mutually exclusive, but different products):
1. HARD FILTER (this bead's default): Qdrant payload Must/Should condition on the tags list — exact, boolean, 'only records carrying tag X'. Precise; good for operator-console scoping; but binary and invites taxonomy management (the tension with semantic-first intent).
2. SOFT SEMANTIC SIGNAL (rejected-by-default alternative to record): fold tags into the text embedded at store/update time (append to content before Embed) so tags nudge similarity without a hard gate — closer to semantic-first spirit, but pollutes the content vector, is a weak/fuzzy signal, and cannot be queried precisely.
Recommendation to capture in the ADR: hard filter for the operator-console/precise-scoping use case; record the soft-signal approach as the considered-and-rejected alternative (vector pollution, no precise query) so it is not relitigated.
acceptance_criteria: search_memory and list_memory accept an optional tags filter; results restricted to records carrying the requested tags (match-mode per ADR); filter composes with vector ranking and existing scope/owner/window gates; payload-index decision made and applied; ADR recorded on the semantic-first tension; docs + Memory contract + curating-memory skill updated; tests cover filter match, no-filter passthrough, and authz/window interaction.
notes:
Implemented in workspace engram-6ec (off trunk #163 / v0.7.7). Decision (user): tag-filtered recall on BOTH search_memory + list_memory, hard Qdrant filter, AND-default, no match-mode/OR, no payload index. ADR engram-4xt7 (Accepted) records the semantic-first tension + rejected soft-signal/index/OR alternatives.

Implementation: new store.tagMatchConditions(tags) -> one Qdrant Must NewMatch('tags',t) per tag (list-membership => contains-all = AND). Wired into Store.Search (new tags []string param) and listFilter via ListOptions.Tags, composed onto the existing owner/visibility/window Must envelope so authz is never bypassed. search_memory pre-filters then ANN-ranks. searchArgs/listArgs gain optional Tags; handlers thread through; Connect read API passes nil (proto unchanged). Grounding: ensureCollection has zero payload indexes today, so 'no index' matches existing scope/owner/category filtering.

Tests (TDD, RED->GREEN verified): store TestSearchAndListTagsFilter (passthrough / single / AND / non-match / authz: another actor's tagged record not surfaced) on both Search and List; handler TestSearchListMemoryTagsHandler. Docs: docs-site tools.md (both tools), CLAUDE.md Memory contract, curating-memory SKILL.md (new Tagging section softening no-taxonomy stance). Gates: go test ./... 0 fail; golangci-lint 0; gofmt/vet/license/rumdl clean. Left in_progress (closure at merge).

title: update_memory cannot mutate tags (or category) — only content + visibility
description:
update_memory exposes no way to change a record's tags. updateArgs (internal/server/tools.go) carries only ID/Content/Shared; the handler calls Store.Update(ctx, cur, a.Content, a.Shared, vec), and Store.Update (internal/store/store.go:861) mutates only cur.Content and optionally cur.Visibility — Tags/Category/etc. are carried over verbatim from the FetchForUpdate snapshot. Correcting a stale tag therefore requires delete_memory + store_memory, which loses the record id, created_at, and history.

Surfaced by another agent session that hit it correcting a legacy 'design-not-implemented' tag on memory 371eb02d — it fixed the body instead (sound, since recall is semantic/vector-over-content and tags are not used in search filtering today).

Priority rationale: P3. Tags are currently presentational (Store.Search builds no tag condition), so the body-fix workaround fully covers recall. Value is operator-console browsing + any future tag-filtered queries.

Proposed fix: add tag mutation to updateArgs and thread through Store.Update. Mirror the 'shared *bool' nil-preserve pattern — use a presence-signal type (e.g. *[]string or a dedicated flag) so a content-only update does NOT wipe existing tags. Decide whether category should be mutable too (likely yes, same mechanism). Update docs-site/src/content/docs/reference/tools.md and the Memory contract section in CLAUDE.md.
design: nil/absent = preserve, present = replace (mirrors Shared *bool). A content-only update must never silently clear tags — this is the load-bearing invariant, same as the unshare-protection on visibility.
acceptance_criteria: update_memory accepts a tags field; omitting it preserves existing tags; supplying it replaces them; record id/created_at/history preserved across the update; docs + Memory contract updated; test mirrors TestUpdateMemoryPreservesSharingHandler for the preserve-on-omit case.
notes:
Related: engram-6ec adds the read-path complement (tags as a search/list filter). They are mutually reinforcing but neither hard-blocks the other. If engram-6ec lands, the 'tags are presentational, hence P3' rationale here weakens — revisit priority then.
Implemented in workspace engram-4sw (off trunk 0.7.6). Root: update_memory's updateArgs + Store.Update only carried Content/Shared; Tags (and other fields) were carried verbatim from the FetchForUpdate snapshot, so no mutation path existed. Fix: added Tags *[]string to updateArgs and a tags *[]string param to Store.Update following the existing 'shared *bool' presence-signal contract — non-nil replaces the full set (empty slice clears), nil preserves. Wired through the handler; updated the live MCP tool description, docs-site reference, and CLAUDE.md Memory contract. Scope: tags only (category deferred — constrained value-set doesn't fit the nil-preserve slice pattern). New TestUpdateMemoryTagsHandler covers replace + preserve-on-omit + id/created_at preservation; 3 existing Store.Update callers updated with nil tags arg. Verified: build exit 0; internal/store + internal/server pass; golangci-lint 0 issues; gofmt/vet clean. Left in_progress (closure at merge).

title: engram brand: PR #127 review follow-ups (dark-contrast tuning + cat-discovery token)
description:
Deferred non-blocking findings from the PR #127 (engram-w6v) review gate. Standalone follow-ups, not part of the brand-system epic deliverable.

1. [from engram-w6v.1, was 'important' but PRE-EXISTING] MemoryRow/Badge use var(--cat-{memory.category}); app.css defines only convention/gotcha/decision/preference. If discovery records (category='discovery') ever render in MemoryRow, --cat-discovery resolves undefined (transparent dot, unstyled badge color). The Badge already used this var before PR #127 (the PR only added the matching cat-dot), so this is pre-existing, not a regression. Investigate whether discovery records reach MemoryRow; if so add --cat-discovery to :root + .dark (distinct hue) + the @theme inline bridge.

2. [from engram-w6v.2, design-intent tuning] Console + docs favicons and the docs logo hardcode brand violet #6E56CF (per spec: a favicon has no currentColor context; the Starlight logo must stay brand-violet, so currentColor is NOT the fix — it would render the mark white/black and lose the brand). Optional dark-mode contrast tuning: add an @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) <style> inside the favicon/logo SVGs shifting to the dark brand violet #8B7BE8 for crisper contrast on dark browser chrome / Starlight dark header. Apply uniformly (console + docs) to preserve unification.

3. [from engram-w6v.4, suggestion] docs-site/src/styles/brand.css: --sl-color-accent: #6E56CF is repeated identically in :root and :root[data-theme='light']; the light block need only override the differing low/high endpoints.

4. [from engram-w6v.3, suggestion] ui/src/lib/assets/engram-lockup.svg lacks role/aria-label (intentional: BrandMark wrapper owns a11y; adding them would double-label in the DOM). Tracked only as a maintenance note in case the asset is ever consumed without the wrapper.
notes: Resolved 3 of 4 follow-ups (item 4 is an intentional no-op). ITEM 1 — root cause CONFIRMED (broader than bead guessed): discovery records carry category="discovery" (internal/server/tools.go:415) and DO render via var(--cat-{category}) — through MemoryRow (MemoryList) AND MemoryDetail on the /discovery route, not just MemoryRow. app.css defined only convention/gotcha/decision/preference, so --cat-discovery resolved undefined (transparent dot, unstyled badge). Fix: added --cat-discovery (Primer green #1a7f37 light / #3fb950 dark — distinct from existing blue/orange/fuchsia) to :root, .dark, and the @theme inline bridge. Regression guard: ui/src/app.css.test.ts asserts every renderable category has a token in all 3 places. ITEM 2 — favicons + docs logo hardcode #6E56CF. Added @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) attribute-selector style block ([stroke=#6E56CF]/[fill=#6E56CF] -> #8B7BE8) to ui/static/favicon.svg, docs-site/public/favicon.svg, docs-site/src/assets/engram-mark.svg (internal/webauth/static/favicon.svg regenerated via task ui:build). Uniform across console + docs; currentColor deliberately NOT used (would lose the brand mark, per spec). ITEM 3 — docs-site/src/styles/brand.css: removed redundant --sl-color-accent from :root[data-theme='light'] (identical to :root; now inherits, only low/high endpoints overridden). ITEM 4 — no change (engram-lockup.svg aria intentionally omitted; BrandMark wrapper owns a11y). Vendored SPA regenerated (task ui:build) so the ui-drift gate stays green. Gates: go test ./... PASS, UI vitest 52/52, docs-site build (12 pages) PASS, license:check 0 invalid. Caveat: app.css.test.ts reads app.css via node:fs (@tailwindcss/vite eats ?raw -> empty). svelte-check flags the node:* imports (project tsconfig scopes types to jest-dom) but svelte-check is non-gating (CI uses pnpm build) and already red from pre-existing shadcn errors. Clean svelte-check would need @types/node + tsconfig types:[node] — deferred as disproportionate. Finished: pushed bookmark engram-l0x-brand-followups -> PR #129 (OPEN, mergeable), awaiting human merge. Bead stays in_progress; closes at merge. Review gate /review-pr 129 -> PASS (turn 2). Turn 1 raised 2 important + 3 suggestions, ALL fixed: - IMPORTANT (en3.2/en3.4): docs logo dark-mode via prefers-color-scheme inside the -embedded SVG only tracked OS dark, not Starlight's data-theme toggle. FIX: Starlight light/dark logo pair (engram-mark.svg light + new engram-mark-dark.svg #8B7BE8) in astro.config.mjs. Favicons KEEP prefers-color-scheme (correct for OS browser chrome). - SUGGESTION (en3.3): --cat-discovery used the retired GitHub greens #1a7f37/#3fb950. FIX: retuned to teal #0d9488/#2dd4bf. - SUGGESTION (en3.1): test category list hardcoded. FIX: exported CATEGORIES from queries.ts; test derives [...CATEGORIES, 'discovery']. - SUGGESTION (en3.5): test used positional indexOf/slice. FIX: selector-anchored regex extraction.

title: Migrate @tanstack/svelte-query v5 -> v6 (runes API)
description: svelte-query v6 drops the Svelte-store interface (createQuery no longer returns a subscribe-able store; $query auto-subscription is gone) in favor of a Svelte-5 runes reactive object accessed directly (query.data, query.isLoading). Attempted during the engram-mo0 dep upgrade and reverted to v5.90.2 because it produces 44 type errors across all 5 query call-sites (+layout.svelte, +page.svelte, observe/search/discovery/+page.svelte, lib/client.ts) and is a runtime-behavior refactor of the Observe shell's core data layer — not a mechanical bump. Needs: migrate all createQuery/QueryClientProvider usages to the v6 runes pattern, update tests, and update/supersede ADR engram-2xl (svelte-query reactive pattern). Held latest GA at v5.90.2 in the meantime.
notes:
CORRECTION on the ADR angle: this is primarily a CODE migration (createQuery store -> runes across the 5 call-sites + tests). ADR engram-2xl does NOT need supersede/re-decision — its decision ('use @tanstack/svelte-query as the SPA data layer') is unchanged by v6; only the '(v5)' version pin in the decision line goes stale. At most file a minor ADR ADDENDUM (via /adr addendum) bumping the version reference to v6. Not a blocker for the code work.
Migrated @tanstack/svelte-query v5.90.2 -> v6.1.34 (runes API). v6 contract verified via context7 docs (svelte migrate-from-v5-to-v6): createQuery takes an options FUNCTION '() => ({queryKey, queryFn, enabled})' for reactivity, and the result is a runes object read DIRECTLY (query.data/isLoading/error) — no $ store prefix. Changes (4 route files; +layout.svelte provider/QueryCache unchanged in v6): +page.svelte static queries wrapped in () => ({...}), $q. -> q.; observe/search/discovery reactive queries: replaced createQuery(derived(page, $p => ...)) + $app/stores with createQuery(() => ({... page.url.searchParams ...})) reading the runes page from $app/state (drops 'svelte/store' derived). No test changes needed — the 6 test files cover client/components/errors/queries, none touch the route pages or createQuery. Verified: svelte-check 44->0 errors, pnpm build, vitest 14/14, go test ./internal/webauth (embed), deterministic re-vendor. Runtime reactivity not live-exercised (needs a deployed backend) but follows the documented v6 idiom exactly. ADR engram-2xl already made version-agnostic (PR #97), so no ADR change needed. Supersedes renovate PR #96.

title: engram skill hook tests fail under global git commit-signing (1Password)
description: skill/engram/hooks/tests/{test_session_start_memory_recall,test_posttooluse_memory_capture_nudge}.py create temp git repos and run 'git commit --allow-empty -m init' with only -c user.email/-c user.name. When the developer has global commit signing (e.g. 1Password gpg.ssh.program), the fixture commit fails: 'error: 1Password: failed to fill whole buffer / fatal: failed to write commit object' (exit 128), making 'task' (test:python) red locally even though the code is fine and CI is green. Fix: the test git helper should pass -c commit.gpgsign=false (and/or -c gpg.format=) when initializing/committing in fixtures so they are robust to a dev's global signing config. Discovered during drain engram-9xm / epic engram-6tl.5 Final Verification — unrelated to that epic's Go code.
notes: Root cause CONFIRMED (reproduced deterministically): skill/engram/hooks/tests/{test_session_start_memory_recall,test_posttooluse_memory_capture_nudge}.py git_repo fixtures run 'git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit --allow-empty -m init' WITHOUT disabling signing, so they inherit the dev's global commit.gpgsign/gpg.ssh.program. When the signer can't sign (locked 1Password vault, headless drain, CI) the commit fails 'failed to write commit object' exit 128 → 8 fixture errors → task test:python red, despite correct code. Did NOT reproduce in my interactive session (vault unlocked, op-ssh-sign succeeds), so I forced it: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL pointing at commit.gpgsign=true + gpg.ssh.program=/usr/bin/false → pytest gave 8 ERRORs (exit 128) [RED]. Fix: added '-c commit.gpgsign=false' to BOTH fixture commit invocations (the only two test files that git-commit; the other 4 don't). Post-fix under the same forced broken signer: 36 passed [GREEN]; normal env 36 passed; ruff check + format clean. Test-only change (no product code), so typed test(hooks) to avoid a spurious release-please bump. PR pending.
close_reason: Merged in engram-shk-signing-fixtures via PR #60

title: Typed Subject authz-core refactor
description: LARGER REFACTOR. Today the anonymous caller is represented by an empty-string sub sentinel (sub=="") threaded through ownerFromContext / store filters / write gates; this is the root of the fail-closed bugs hand-hardened in epic engram-dg5 (xic/99z.13). Replace it with a typed discriminated Subject (e.g. Anonymous vs Authenticated{Sub string}) so the empty-sub case is impossible to forget at a call site and the compiler enforces the distinction. Touches internal/server ownerFromContext + internal/store filter/gate signatures. Source review finding: engram-t1p.8 (PR #54). Note: this is the structural fix that subsumes the manual empty-sub hardening.
notes:
drain assessment (engram-9mc): NOT a safe autonomous one-shot. Surface: 11 store method signatures take sub string, ~12 server call sites, ~100 empty-string sentinel literals across 69 test call sites; authz core governed by ADRs engram-cgb/hvg/kyz; subsumes engram-dg5 fail-closed hardening. No design doc/ADR exists for the Subject type (placement: store pkg vs auth pkg; API; relation to Memory.Owner). Recommend design-first: brainstorm -> ADR for the typed Subject -> plan -> decompose into sub-beads (store-layer type intro, server threading, test migration), each individually reviewable. Halting drain here for a human decision.
grounding/probe: ownerFromContext/sub surface — sub string threaded through ownerOrSharedCondition, GetReadable, getWritable, OwnedOrAbsent, DeleteAll, Search/List/SearchDiscovery; ownerFromContext returns (string,error) where ''=anonymous(auth-disabled)=owner=='' bucket AND error='validated token no sub' (fail-closed). Footgun: sub,_:=ownerFromContext collapses err→'' (identityForLog does this deliberately for logs). Pre-isolation records use ownerlessFilter (NewIsEmpty), separate from sub.
grounding/adr: cgb (authz enforced in store layer, handlers pass identity through — type must be store-consumable), hvg (owner=stable sub, actor=audit — Authenticated carries sub), kyz (read owner-OR-shared vs write owner-only asymmetry — unchanged), xa6 (404/ErrNotFound for unauthorized id ops — unchanged). owner Qdrant payload stays string; Subject maps to it.
grounding/context7: N/A — refactor introduces NO new external dependency (pure internal Go type design). go-sdk auth sub semantics (TokenInfo.Extra['sub'], unexported context key blocks handler-test injection) already grounded in epic engram-99z; unchanged here.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-08-typed-subject-authz-core-design.md
design-review round 1 NOT READY: critical — Memory.Owner population from Subject unspecified (sealed interface had no owner-string accessor for anonymous); important — SetVisibility/Delete/FetchForUpdate omitted from scope; minor — server call-site count off (12→11), DeleteAll default-deny mechanism ambiguous. All addressed.
design-review round 2 READY: added Subject.Owner() persistence accessor (anon→'',authed→sub) with explicit 'Owner() stamps; switch enforces' rule + nil-panic-not-silent-grant property; enumerated the 3 getWritable-backed id gates; corrected counts; DeleteAll filter-based default returns error/deletes nothing. ADR-aligned (cgb/hvg/kyz/xa6). Next: writing-plans.
grounding/probe-paths: verified internal/store/store.go, internal/store/store_test.go, internal/server/tools.go, internal/server/tools_test.go, internal/server/instrument.go exist; subject.go to be created in existing internal/store/. Sole production callers of sub-gated store methods = tools.go handlers + instrument.go identityForLog (no other packages).
grounding/context7-reverify: /qdrant/go-client — Filter{Must,Should,MustNot []*Condition}; NewMatch/NewFilterAsCondition confirmed. matchNothing() = Must[owner==X]+MustNot[owner==X] contradiction (provably empty, no sentinel collision).
Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-08-typed-subject-authz-core.md
plan-review READY (round 1): no blockers; 5 minor findings. Folded the catch-all rg call-site sweep into the test-migration tasks (covers TestAnonBucket*/TestSearchAndDeleteAll beyond the named list); line-number hints confirmed accurate; model labels to be applied at plan-to-beads (mechanical → sonnet).
ADRs: engram-12c (sealed Go interface for authz Subject)
lesson: Task 2 reviewer — consider whether subjectFromContext's boundary guard (sub!="") is sufficient, or whether store.Authenticated() should ALSO guard empty sub (panic, consistent with the nil-Owner()-panics fail-loud philosophy). Raised in 6tl.5.1 code-quality review; deferred as the constructor is only reached via the guarded boundary, but in-package future edits could reintroduce Authenticated("").
lesson-resolved (Task 2): subjectFromContext boundary guard 'ok && sub!=""' provably rejects all empty/missing-sub token shapes -> returns (nil,error), so store.Authenticated("") is never constructed on the production path. The constructor guard from the 6tl.5.1 finding is therefore DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH ONLY (guards future in-pkg edits), not a correctness blocker. Boundary mechanism stands as the design intended.
lesson: review subagents — PIN every reviewer to an explicit commit id (jj --no-pager show/diff --git -r <commit_id>), NOT bare 'jj show' (which shows the empty working-copy @, not @-). A reviewer left to default-inspect can land on the wrong revision (observed: a resumed reviewer reported a 'docs-only' diff and a vacuous READY while inspecting the wrong rev). Also: re-dispatching a review agent does NOT inherit prior context like a true continuation — re-state the target commit each time.
lesson (potential hardening, non-blocking): TestNilSubjectFailsClosed's SearchDiscovery(nil) check seeds only plain Memory records (no category=='discovery'), so it would pass even if the nil branch resolved to Anonymous — the assertion is redundant with the Search/List checks on the same ownerOrSharedCondition default arm rather than independently isolating SearchDiscovery's nil-denial. If tightening per-method pin coverage later, seed a discovery-category record in that test.
close_reason: Typed Subject authz-core refactor complete: all 9 sub-beads (6tl.5.1-9) closed. Sealed store.Subject (Anonymous|Authenticated) replaces the sub-string sentinel across all read/write/id-gated/bulk authz paths + stamping; ownerFromContext retired; nil-Subject fail-closed guarantee locked under test. Semantics-preserving (kyz/hvg/xa6/cgb); Go gates green.

title: Assertion-guard TestSetVisibilityTOCTOU against Qdrant version bump (t1p.7)
description: TestSetVisibilityTOCTOU relies on Qdrant v1.18.2 SetPayload behavior (SetPayload on a deleted point does not resurrect it). The version is pinned in TestMain but the test does not assert/guard against a silent behavior change if the pinned image is bumped. Add an explicit guard or comment-coupled assertion so a future Qdrant bump that changes SetPayload semantics fails loudly here rather than silently invalidating the TOCTOU contract. Source review finding: engram-t1p.7 (PR #54).
close_reason: Added env-gated version guard coupling TestSetVisibilityTOCTOU to the pinned qdrantImageTag via HealthCheck; a testcontainer image bump now fails loudly (external-addr path exempt). (engram-t1p.7)

title: Eliminate double Qdrant round-trip in OwnedForUpdate happy path (t1p.6)
description: On the updateMemory happy path, OwnedForUpdate performs a pre-check Get and then updateMemory does a second Get of the same record — two Qdrant round-trips for one update. Either pass the pre-fetched Memory through from the ownership gate to the update so the second Get is dropped, or (if keeping the two-call shape) soften the code comment that calls the gate 'cheap'. Prefer passing the fetched record through. Source review finding: engram-t1p.6 (PR #54).
close_reason: updateMemory now makes one ownership Get: FetchForUpdate returns the writable record, Update operates on it (no re-Get). Isolation contract preserved; security-reviewed. (engram-t1p.6)

title: Handler-layer regression test: authenticated cross-actor shared-read (t1p.5)
description: After the ownerOrSharedCondition tightening in PR #54 there is no handler-layer regression test asserting that an authenticated caller CAN read another actor's shared (visibility=shared) records while still being denied private ones. Add a handler-path test (search_memory / list_memory) covering: caller B reads caller A's shared record = visible; A's private record = not visible. Source review finding: engram-t1p.5 (PR #54).
close_reason: Added TestAuthedCrossActorSharedReadHandlers + authedContext middleware helper; authenticated caller B reads A's shared but not private via searchMemory/listMemory (engram-t1p.5)

title: list_memory handler-path test for anon read isolation (t1p.4)
description: TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers (internal/server) calls d.st.List directly instead of going through the list_memory handler method, so it does not exercise the handler layer it is meant to cover. Reroute the assertion through the list_memory handler (the deps method that wraps store.List) so the anonymous-bucket read-isolation guarantee is verified end-to-end at the handler boundary. Source review finding: engram-t1p.4 (PR #54).
close_reason: Extracted (d *deps) listMemory method; rerouted TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers list assertion through the handler path (engram-t1p.4)

title: Authz hardening follow-ups from PR #54 review (optional)
description:
Optional quality/test-hardening suggestions surfaced by the PR #54 review (epic engram-t1p), deferred as non-blocking:
- t1p.4: TestAnonReadIsolationHandlers calls d.st.List directly instead of through a list_memory handler method — handler-path fidelity gap.
- t1p.5: no handler-layer regression test for authenticated cross-actor shared-read after the ownerOrSharedCondition tightening.
- t1p.6: OwnedForUpdate doubles the Qdrant round-trip on the updateMemory happy path (pre-check Get + Update Get); either pass the pre-fetched Memory through or soften the 'cheap' wording.
- t1p.7: TestSetVisibilityTOCTOU relies on Qdrant v1.18.2 SetPayload behavior; pinned in TestMain but not assertion-guarded against a version bump.
- t1p.8: empty-string anonymous sentinel — consider a typed Subject (Anonymous vs Authenticated(sub)) discriminated union (larger refactor).
- t1p.9: test deferred cleanup discards Delete/DeleteAll errors, could mask cross-run contamination.
notes: lesson: authenticated-identity handler tests are possible via an authedContext(t,sub) helper that round-trips a request through mcpauth.RequireBearerToken with a stub verifier (Extra{sub}, future Expiration) and captures r.Context() — the go-sdk tokenInfoKey is unexported so context.WithValue cannot inject it. See internal/server/tools_test.go.
close_reason: All follow-ups landed: 5 test/perf fixes via PR #55 (6tl.1-.4,.6); typed Subject refactor (6tl.5) via PR #57. Residual: engram-shk + engram-bvh (P3, new follow-ups from #57 review).

title: Revisit serve.go WriteTimeout vs MCP streaming responses
description: Review finding from engram-ew7.8: http.Server.WriteTimeout=60s (a verbatim value from the observability plan) can silently terminate long-running MCP streamable-HTTP tool responses (e.g. slow LLM/embedding calls) without a clean client error. Current engram tools (store/search memory) are short so it's not an active bug, but revisit once real-world latency data exists — consider raising/removing WriteTimeout on the MCP handler path. Source: cmd/engram/serve.go runServe http.Server literal.
notes: Root cause: STALE finding (3rd this session, same pattern as engram-99z.14/9je). The finding (engram-ew7.8) flagged http.Server.WriteTimeout=60s from the observability PLAN, but that value was removed WITHIN PR #44 before merge. Resolution: NO CODE CHANGE — main@origin cmd/engram/serve.go (introduced in #44, commit 0b074e387) already sets the http.Server with ReadHeaderTimeout=10s (slowloris) + IdleTimeout=120s and BOTH ReadTimeout and WriteTimeout intentionally UNSET (0), with a comment documenting the precise concern the bead raised: 'the streamable-HTTP / SSE transport holds connections open indefinitely and the go-sdk never clears write deadlines, so either timeout would sever long-lived SSE streams.' Verified: rg 'WriteTimeout' across non-test Go finds only the explanatory comment — it is set nowhere. The finding's recommendation ('consider raising/removing WriteTimeout on the MCP handler path') is already implemented; nothing latency-dependent remains to revisit (no write deadline = slow embedding calls can't be severed). Closing as resolved-by-existing-code. NOTE: default jj workspace is stale at #57 (fetch doesn't rebase the empty working copy); harmless — solving-a-bead workspaces base off fetched trunk().
close_reason: Resolved-by-existing-code: serve.go already has WriteTimeout/ReadTimeout intentionally unset (0) with a documented SSE-streaming rationale, shipped in #44 (0b074e387). The 60s value never reached merged main. Stale finding.

title: Async-on-write summary queue (auto-fill new records without an operator sweep)
description: Future enhancement deferred from the auto-summary design (epic engram-cly5, ADR engram-4y7p). Today auto-summaries are filled only by the offline 'engram summarize-missing' CLI. The seam already exists: Store.FillSummary (internal/store/summarize.go) is idempotent + vector-preserving. Build: after a successful store_memory upsert, enqueue the record id; an in-process worker pool drains the queue via FillSummary so new summary-less records get summaries without an operator sweep — and WITHOUT putting the summarizer on the synchronous write path (a gateway outage must never fail store_memory). Gate enabling auto broadly on the fidelity eval (task eval:summary). Spec/plan: docs/superpowers/{specs,plans}/2026-06-25-auto-summary-curated-memories*.

value: Agent-tool worktree isolation (isolation:worktree) can parent the agent's jj workspace on main rather than the orchestrator's @. Fix-workers MUST 'jj new <pr-bookmark>' first and verify @- is the expected tip, else their commit conflicts at integration. CLEANUP (bigger than just bookmarks): each isolation:worktree agent leaves a FULL jj workspace named worktree-agent-* (plus same-named bookmark), nested under <orchestrator-ws>_worktrees/agent-*. One drain+review-gate run accumulated ~24 workspaces (~1.2GB), NOT auto-cleaned. Post-merge teardown MUST: (1) 'jj workspace forget' every worktree-agent-* + the drain workspace (never 'default'); (2) 'jj bookmark delete' the same names; (3) rm -rf BOTH <repo>_worktrees/<drain-ws> AND <repo>_worktrees/<drain-ws>_worktrees. Always 'jj git push -b <bookmark>' (scoped) so stray worktree-agent-* bookmarks aren't pushed.

In engram's colocated jj+git repo, the gh CLI (and any git plumbing that walks parents for repo discovery) fails from inside a jj workspace with 'fatal: not a git repository' — the workspace dir (e.g. <repo>_worktrees/worktree-<id>) is NOT under the main repo's .git common-dir, so git discovery hits the filesystem boundary and stops. Fix: run gh from the MAIN checkout (cd /Volumes/Code/github.com/seanb4t/engram) and use --head/--base flags to target the pushed bookmark; OR use 'jj git push -b <bookmark>' which works from inside the workspace (only gh/git-discovery is affected). Hit on PR #228 creation: gh pr create from the workspace errored, re-ran from main checkout and succeeded.

protect-main ruleset (id 17228701, enforcement active, target branch) requires 8 status checks matched by exact CI job name (integration_id 15368 = GitHub Actions): test, golangci-lint, commit-lint, license headers, helm chart, actionlint, python, AND "ui vendored-asset drift" (added 2026-06-28, engram bead engram-38c6 Option 2 — gates Renovate ui/ dep bumps that drift the vendored SPA). Renaming a job name strands PRs on Expected until the ruleset is updated. Never add workflow-level paths-ignore/branches filters to ci.yaml — skipped workflows never report and block merges; job-level if: skips are safe (skipped satisfies required checks). The ui-drift job has if: !startsWith(github.head_ref,'release-please--') so release-please PRs skip it safely. Backup of the 7-check ruleset captured 2026-06-28 before adding ui-drift. This supersedes the prior 'requires-7-status' memory (now 8).
